# Ripple — Key Coverage Hunt (Box 1: what public data exists)

**Date:** 2026-07-22 · **Mission:** for every connection key, the full landscape of public datasets that carry it.
**This is reconnaissance only.** Nothing here was downloaded, landed, or ingested. Landing is a separate decision.

## How to read this

A *key* is an ID number that shows up in more than one dataset. One key in two lists = a question you can ask ("is the banned provider still billing?"). This report answers, for each key: **where does it actually live in public data?**

| Tier | Means |
|---|---|
| **STEEL** | A real unique government ID. A match here *is* a connection. |
| **STRONG** | A real code, but shared by many entities. Groups things; doesn't link them. |
| **GEO** | A location. Same place ≠ same entity. |
| **PROBABILISTIC** | Name/address text. Weakest — needs corroboration. |

**Verified** column: a separate skeptic agent re-fetched the page and looked for the key in a data dictionary or sample. `yes` = confirmed. `REFUTED` = the claim did not hold up (reason given). `—` = not checked (verification was capped at the top new datasets per key; unchecked is *not* the same as wrong).

## The score

- **33 of 33 keys** hunted across the open web; **33 of 33** swept against our own scouted index.
- **1047 public datasets** named and located, of which **915 are new to Ripple** (not landed, not already in the index).
- **507 hits** found inside our own 338K-dataset portal index — data we'd already scouted and never connected.
- **88 datasets independently verified**, **23 claims refuted** by the skeptic pass and corrected below.
- **86 findings** on what the brief itself missed — new keys, new domains, and join tricks that aren't ID matches.

# Part 1 — What the brief missed

*The mission asked for this separately: the 24-key list was a limitation of the brief, not a map of what's out there. Five agents attacked the list itself.*

## Keys the brief got wrong, overvalued, or missed

**PARCEL / APN family is the biggest unanticipated cross-source key in the scouted universe**

Assessor parcel numbers (PARCEL_ID, APN, PARCEL_NO, PARCEL_NUMBER, PIN_NUM, USER_APN, ASSESSORS_PARCEL_NUMBER) are not in the tagger vocabulary yet they are the single most common real-world join key in local government data. Within a jurisdiction the same parcel number links the assessor roll, building permits, code-violation cases, foreclosure registries, tax accounts, and incident data — exactly the 'who owns the building that hurts people' join. Caveat: parcel IDs are county-scoped, so the key must be namespaced by portal/county (parcel 123 in Tucson is not parcel 123 in Boston). Already has a landed foothold: 84 LANDING tables carry PARCEL (Tucson), 18 carry PARCEL_ID (Boston, WPRDC/Allegheny, Virginia), 12 PARCELID (Atlanta, San Jose, Tennessee), plus APN and ASSESSORS_PARCEL_NUMBER variants.

*Evidence:* Family aggregate across name variants: 2,625 datasets on 62 of 96 portals (PARCEL_ID alone 460 ds / 28 portals; APN 413 / 21; PARCEL_NUMBER 93 / 23). Query: flatten COLUMN_NAMES, family = RLIKE APN|PARCEL_(ID|NO|NUM|NUMBER)|PIN_NUM. LANDING check: LIBRARY_RAW.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS TABLE_SCHEMA='LANDING' shows 100+ tables with parcel columns.

*Datasets:* LAHD Property Look-Up for 2025 Registered Foreclosure Properties (DataLA); Austin Code Cases Related to Winter Storm Uri (Austin Open Data); City of Asheville Permit Inspections (APN column); Well Completion Reports (California Open Data); Connecticut CAMA Data 2022 (ACCOUNT_NUMBER, same property-tax family)

**LICENSE_NUMBER family - the 'banned but still operating' key the tagger cannot see**

State and municipal license numbers (LICENSE_NUMBER, LICENSENUMBER, LICENSENO, LICENSE_NUM, WI_LICENSE_NUM, PA_LICENSE_NO) appear across 45 portals and are genuinely cross-source within a jurisdiction: license rosters join to inspections, violations, and enforcement actions by the same number. This is the direct mechanism for Ripple's first-story lens (revoked/disciplined licensee still active in another dataset). Bonus bridge: FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS in LANDING carries COVERED_RECIPIENT_LICENSE_STATE_CODE1-5, meaning state medical license numbers can bridge Open Payments to state licensing boards where NPI is missing. Scoped by issuing authority (state + license type), so needs a namespace like parcel.

*Evidence:* Family aggregate: 241 datasets on 45 portals (LICENSE_NUMBER 147 ds / 32 portals; LICENSENUMBER 36 / 15; LICENSENO 26 / 6). LANDING: LICENSE_NUMBER in 10 tables (CA healthcare facilities, LA County, Harris County, WPRDC); COVERED_RECIPIENT_LICENSE_STATE_CODE1-5 in all three FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS tables.

*Datasets:* Business Licenses (Chicago Data Portal); Licensed and Certified Healthcare Facilities (California Open Data); Active Right of Way Contractor License Holders (Austin); FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS (landed - state license code columns)

**GNIS_ID - a national geographic-feature registry ID nobody put on the key list**

USGS Geographic Names Information System IDs (GNIS_ID, GNISID, GNIS_NAME alongside) are a true federal-standard identifier for named places and water features, used identically across 24 portals. Unlike parcel/license numbers it needs no jurisdiction namespace - GNIS_ID is nationally unique. It joins hydrography, water rights, hazard layers, and place features across completely different sources (e.g. Colorado water rights to national hydrography). Sits alongside two sibling water-domain keys that surfaced in the same sweep: RCH_CODE (NHD reach code, 30 ds / 6 portals) and AU_ID (EPA water-quality assessment unit, 35 ds / 6 portals), which together join impaired-waters lists to stream geometry - a pollution-harm mechanism.

*Evidence:* GNIS family: 268 datasets on 24 portals (GNIS_ID 214/23, GNISID 54/4). Sample titles show cross-source use: water rights, hydrography, HUC12 watershed layers. AU_ID samples are all state impaired-streams / 305(b) assessments from different states (TX TCEQ, KY DOW, NM, King County WA) - same EPA assessment-unit scheme.

*Datasets:* DWR Water Right - Net Amounts (Colorado Information Marketplace); TCEQ Impaired Streams (Fort Worth, AU_ID); Ky DOW 2024 Integrated Report 305b Assessed Streams (AU_ID); Lakes, Ponds, Impoundments (Asheville, GNIS_ID)

**TRI_FACILITY_ID - small but pure: EPA toxics facility ID already landed in 40 tables**

EPA Toxics Release Inventory facility IDs are nationally unique and appear verbatim in local portal data (Allegheny toxics inventory, Harris County ethylene-oxide point sources, LA County RSEI risk scores). This is the gateway key into EPA's facility universe (TRI, and via TRI to the FRS registry) - directly a who-gets-hurt key: it links a polluting facility's emissions and risk scores across sources. Only 5 portals, but every LANDING table that has it is already in the warehouse, so it is immediately actionable.

*Evidence:* TRI_FACILITY_ID: 40 datasets / 5 portals in the index, and exactly 40 LANDING tables carry the column (Harris County, LA County, WPRDC x2, 35 Utah tables). Sample titles are all toxics/emissions datasets - semantically uniform, unlike generic FACILITY_ID.

*Datasets:* Allegheny County Toxics Release Inventory (WPRDC); Ethylene Oxide Emission 2020 Point Source (Harris County); Risk-Screening Environmental Indicators (RSEI) Score (LA County)

**SOC_CODE - an occupation taxonomy key, same class as NAICS but absent from the vocabulary**

The tagger knows NAICS and SIC (industry taxonomies) but not SOC, the Standard Occupational Classification. SOC_CODE joins DOL H-1B/PERM labor certifications (FED_DOL_OFLC, already landed) to state and local wage/employment datasets - the mechanism for 'are visa workers paid below the local prevailing wage for the same occupation'. Low dataset count but it is a taxonomy key like NAICS: value comes from federal-to-local comparison, not from raw frequency.

*Evidence:* SOC_CODE: 23 datasets / 4 portals in the index; in LANDING it sits in FED_DOL_OFLC plus a landed Cambridge PERM/LCA dataset and a Utah employment-projections dataset - the two sides of the comparison already in the warehouse. Sample titles: CT OES wages, PERM/LCA applications, county employment projections.

*Datasets:* Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) and LCA Programs H-1B Applications (Cambridge portal mirror); CT Occupational Employment & Wages (OES) 2022-Q1; FED_DOL_OFLC (landed)

**EDGAR header IRS-NUMBER: document-citation bridge from CIK to EIN**

MECHANISM: Every EDGAR filing header carries the filer's IRS number — the EIN, printed inside the document rather than existing as a join column anywhere. Extract it from Ripple's existing EDGAR holdings to mint a CIK-to-EIN crosswalk. This is the 'one filing citing the number of another registry' pattern, and it connects two currently-disconnected islands: SEC financials (CIK) and the EIN world (DOL Form 5500, IRS BMF, IRS revocations). WHO GETS HURT: workers — the question it unlocks is 'which public companies reporting healthy SEC financials are simultaneously filing Form 5500s showing underfunded or fee-larded employee benefit plans.' TIER: effectively STEEL once extracted (self-reported but unique per entity); corroboration is just name agreement between the EDGAR company name and the 5500 sponsor / BMF name. This is the cheapest new bridge available to Ripple — no new data source needed, only extraction from data already held.

*Evidence:* Notre Dame's SRAF 10-X header dataset publishes the cd_irs_number field parsed from EDGAR headers (https://sraf.nd.edu/sec-edgar-data/10-x-header-data/), and academic CIK-EIN crosswalks are routinely built this way; SEC's own guidance notes EINs appear in 10-K/S-1/8-K headers (https://www.sec.gov/search-filings).

*Datasets:* EDGAR filings (CIK); DOL Form 5500 (EIN); IRS BMF; IRS revocations

**Banking: RSSD alone misses its siblings — FDIC CERT, OCC charter, and NCUA charter are separate keys with their own enforcement datasets**

The list carries RSSD as the lone banking candidate. But FDIC-keyed data (CERT number) is a distinct universe: BankFind Suite API, Summary of Deposits branch-level data, failed-bank list, and FDIC enforcement decisions are keyed by CERT, not RSSD. OCC enforcement actions key on charter number; credit unions are a whole parallel system keyed by NCUA charter number (5300 call reports, NCUA enforcement) that RSSD coverage of banks never touches. Treating 'RSSD' as 'the banking key' silently drops credit unions and most branch-level and enforcement data.

*Evidence:* FFIEC NIC attributes bulk file carries ID_RSSD, ID_FDIC_CERT, and ID_OCC as separate identifier fields for the same institutions (ffiec.gov NPW Data Dictionary), which only exists because the agencies genuinely key their own datasets differently. FDIC BankFind/Summary of Deposits are CERT-keyed; NCUA publishes credit-union call report data under its own charter numbers.

*Datasets:* FDIC BankFind Suite / failed banks; FDIC Summary of Deposits; OCC enforcement actions; NCUA 5300 call reports

**'NCES' conflates three different education key systems — and the accountability key, OPEID, isn't on the list at all**

NCES is listed as one tagger-known key. It is at least three: (1) NCES LEA/School IDs for K-12 (CCD, CRDC, EDFacts); (2) IPEDS UNITID for postsecondary statistics; (3) OPEID, the Federal Student Aid identifier for Title IV eligibility. OPEID is the one that carries harm data: cohort default rates, federal loan/Pell volumes, heightened cash monitoring, closed-school and borrower-defense lists, and accreditation actions are all OPEID-keyed. UNITID↔OPEID is explicitly NOT one-to-one (parent-child program participation agreements roll campuses up), so a tagger treating 'NCES ID' as one key will produce wrong joins. The for-profit-college harm domain runs on OPEID.

*Evidence:* College Scorecard data documentation (collegescorecard.ed.gov/data) defines OPEID as the OPE/FSA identifier for Title IV participation and publishes annual UNITID↔OPEID crosswalk files precisely because the mapping is many-to-one; higher-ed researcher Robert Kelchen's 'Beware OPEIDs and Super OPEIDs' documents the parent-child aggregation problem; NSLDS cohort default rates are reported by OPEID.

*Datasets:* FSA cohort default rates; College Scorecard; FSA closed school / borrower defense lists; CRDC (K-12, NCES-keyed)

**Insurance: the list has the paywalled key (NAIC code) and misses the free ones (HIOS issuer ID, CMS contract numbers)**

NAIC company code is the state-regulation key, but NAIC's financial statement data is licensed, not open. The free federal insurance accountability data is keyed by two siblings absent from the list: HIOS issuer ID (CMS's Health Insurance Oversight System — MLR public use files including rebates owed for failing the 80/20 rule, rate review, ACA QHP landscape files) and CMS contract numbers (H####/S####) for Medicare Advantage and Part D plans (enrollment, star ratings, sanctions, terminations). Ripple's health spine covers providers (NPI) and facilities (CCN) but has no payer-side key; hunting only NAIC codes would point the machine at data it has to pay for while the free harm data sits under HIOS/contract IDs.

*Evidence:* CMS collects MLR reporting through the Health Insurance Oversight System and posts MLR reports as public use files (cms.gov/cciio/mlr and MLR annual form instructions); QHP landscape and rate review PUFs are HIOS-keyed; CMS publishes MA/Part D enrollment and star ratings by contract number. NAIC bulk financial data requires purchase from NAIC.

*Datasets:* CMS MLR public use files; QHP landscape files; MA/Part D contract enrollment and star ratings; CMS plan sanctions/terminations

**FDA FEI is a missing key that opens the FDA enforcement domain — and DUNS is its bridge**

No FDA establishment key appears anywhere on the list, yet FDA runs a full enforcement dataset family keyed by FEI (FDA Establishment Identifier): inspection classifications (OAI/VAI outcomes), import refusals, and registered drug establishment site lists. The drug establishment registration data carries both FEI and DUNS per site, which bridges FDA enforcement onto the corporate spine (DUNS→legacy SAM/USAspending→UEI). Story shape this unlocks: plants with failed inspections still shipping product, foreign sites never inspected — classic hidden-harm territory adjacent to the already-wired Open Payments/Part D pharma coverage.

*Evidence:* FDA's inspection classifications database and Data Dashboard exports are FEI-keyed; FDA's eDRLS/UFI documentation (verified this session) establishes DUNS as the registration UFI, and FDA's drug establishment current registration site catalog lists FEI and DUNS together — the crosswalk ships inside the dataset itself.

*Datasets:* FDA inspection classifications; FDA import refusals; Drug establishment current registration site list

**FINRA/SEC CRD number — securities brokers and investment advisers**

IDENTIFIES: every securities broker, broker-dealer firm, investment adviser firm, and adviser rep (one CRD number per person/firm, national, lifetime). FLAGSHIP: SEC Form ADV bulk data — https://www.sec.gov/foia-services/frequently-requested-documents/form-adv-data (historical CSV table sets) plus current data at https://adviserinfo.sec.gov/adv ; individual lookups via BrokerCheck (brokercheck.finra.org). Free. TIER: STEEL. UNLOCKS: 'Is the barred broker still in the money business?' — FINRA bar/suspension actions keyed by CRD vs. current registrations, the securities-world twin of LEIE-vs-Medicare. BRIDGE: Form ADV filings carry the firm's CIK and LEI — a direct machine crosswalk CRD↔CIK↔LEI into two already-landed Ripple spines (EDGAR, GLEIF). Highest-priority missing person-level key in finance.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: SEC FOIA Form ADV data page (sec.gov/foia-services/frequently-requested-documents/form-adv-data) offers CSV data sets; adviserinfo.sec.gov/adv hosts current Form ADV data; Form ADV API docs confirm filings searchable by CRD, CIK, and LEI, confirming the crosswalk fields exist in the filings.

*Datasets:* SEC Form ADV data sets (CSV): https://www.sec.gov/foia-services/frequently-requested-documents/form-adv-data; IAPD: https://adviserinfo.sec.gov/adv; FINRA BrokerCheck: https://brokercheck.finra.org

**NMLS ID — mortgage loan originators and consumer-finance companies**

IDENTIFIES: every mortgage loan originator, mortgage/consumer-finance/money-services company and branch, one national NMLS ID each. FLAGSHIP: NMLS Consumer Access — https://nmlsconsumeraccess.org (free lookup by NMLS ID; no free bulk file — CSBS is only now standing up a paid B2B subscription feed). TIER: STEEL key, but ACCESS IS THE CATCH: lookup-only, so landing it means state-regulator license exports or scraping, not one clean download. UNLOCKS: 'Which sanctioned loan originators moved to a new company and kept originating?' BRIDGE: money-services companies in NMLS overlap CFPB complaint respondents (landed) and HMDA lenders (landed via LEI); CFPB enforcement orders cite NMLS IDs. Recommend: treat as wired-when-a-state-export-lands, not a quick win.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: nmlsconsumeraccess.org is lookup-format only; CSBS 'NMLS Consumer Access B2B Subscription Service' RFI PDF confirms bulk data is a planned commercial feed, not open download.

*Datasets:* NMLS Consumer Access: https://nmlsconsumeraccess.org

**FAA airman certificates — Releasable Airmen Database**

IDENTIFIES: every certificated pilot, mechanic, and other airman (~1M+ people). FLAGSHIP: FAA Releasable Airmen Database — https://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/releasable_airmen_download — free, monthly, CSV or fixed-width, basic + certificate records. CAVEAT: actual certificate numbers are withheld; the file's unique airman ID is the join key, and opt-out airmen are excluded. TIER: STEEL within the FAA file family (same unique ID reused across releases); PROBABILISTIC (name+address) to anything outside FAA. UNLOCKS: pairs with the already-planned FAA aircraft registry (TAIL_NUMBER/ICAO24) — people-to-planes: 'which surrendered/revoked airmen still own registered aircraft, and whose aircraft show up in NOAA-style tracking?' BRIDGE: complements landed IMO/AIS maritime lens with the aviation twin.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: faa.gov releasable_airmen_download page exists, monthly updates, CSV/TXT formats; FAA help PDF confirms certificate numbers are not included in the releasable file.

*Datasets:* FAA Releasable Airmen DB: https://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/releasable_airmen_download; FAA Releasable Aircraft Registry (companion): https://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/aircraft_certification/aircraft_registry/releasable_aircraft_download

**State bar numbers — attorneys (California as flagship)**

IDENTIFIES: licensed attorneys, per-state namespace (no national ID exists). FLAGSHIP: State Bar of California public licensee directory — https://apps.calbar.ca.gov — ~270k licensees with bar number, status, discipline history; public record but NO bulk file or API (access = bar-number-range crawling; third-party scrapers exist). TIER: STEEL within a state. UNLOCKS: 'disbarred but still filing' — bar discipline vs. court-docket appearances (DOCKET is already tagger-known), plus attorney names recur in FARA and LDA filings. BRIDGE: FARA/LDA registrants (below) and future PACER/docket work. Recommend CA + NY + TX first; treat as a scrape-and-freshen pipeline, not a download.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: calbar.ca.gov attorney search is the official public record; multiple search results confirm no official bulk API and that access is via bar-number range crawling.

*Datasets:* CA State Bar attorney search: https://apps.calbar.ca.gov

**ASC national appraiser registry — real-estate appraisers and AMCs**

IDENTIFIES: ~340k state-credentialed real-estate appraisers plus registered appraisal management companies, with state license number, status, and disciplinary flags — the federally mandated national roster. FLAGSHIP: https://www.asc.gov/appraiser/advanced (free searchable registry, states submit at least monthly) plus daily change/discipline reports at https://www.asc.gov/national-registries/notices . CAVEAT: no advertised one-click bulk export on the registry page — confirm whether the advanced-search interface exports full result sets before committing. TIER: STEEL (state+license composite). UNLOCKS: 'appraiser disciplined in one state still active in another' and appraisal-fraud patterns under HMDA lending (landed via LEI). BRIDGE: HMDA/mortgage lens; NMLS companies.

*Evidence:* Verified via WebFetch of https://www.asc.gov/national-registries this session: searchable registry and state-level reports confirmed; no bulk download described on that page (flagged as open question). Daily update reports page confirmed via search.

*Datasets:* ASC Appraiser Registry: https://www.asc.gov/appraiser/advanced; ASC daily update reports: https://www.asc.gov/national-registries/notices

**FARA registrant number — registered foreign agents**

IDENTIFIES: every registered agent of a foreign principal (firms and individuals), DOJ-assigned registrant number, plus foreign-principal and short-form (individual) records. FLAGSHIP: FARA eFile bulk data — https://efile.fara.gov/ords/fara/fara_ws/r/api/bulkdata — full CSV/XML zips (e.g. FARA_All_Registrants.csv.zip), updated daily, free, plus a free document API (https://efile.fara.gov/api). TIER: STEEL. UNLOCKS: 'who is being paid by which foreign government, and what else do they touch?' BRIDGE: FARA registrants are heavily the same law/PR firms as Senate LDA registrants; foreign principals cross-match OFAC SDN (landed) and legislator contacts (BIOGUIDE landed). Cheap to land, high story density.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: efile.fara.gov bulk data page confirmed with daily-updated CSV/XML zips including FARA_All_Registrants.csv.zip, and a public API for registrant documents by registration number.

*Datasets:* FARA bulk data: https://efile.fara.gov/ords/fara/fara_ws/r/api/bulkdata; FARA API: https://efile.fara.gov/api

**Senate LDA registrant and client IDs — domestic lobbying**

IDENTIFIES: lobbying firms (registrant ID), their clients (client ID), and named individual lobbyists across LD-1 registrations, LD-2 quarterly reports, and LD-203 contribution reports. FLAGSHIP: Senate LDA REST API — https://lda.senate.gov/api/ (free key, JSON; note old redoc v1 endpoint retires July 31 2026 — build against the current lda.senate.gov API). TIER: STEEL for registrant/client IDs; lobbyist individuals are name-level (PROBABILISTIC). UNLOCKS: the triangle Ripple is uniquely positioned for — 'which federal contractors (UEI, landed) lobby the committees (landed) that control their funding, and what did those members (BIOGUIDE/ICPSR, landed) vote (Voteview, landed)?' BRIDGE: client names → UEI/CIK/EIN via name-match; LD-203 → FEC (planned). This key turns four already-landed spines into one story engine.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: lda.senate.gov/api/ confirmed as the REST API with free key and throttling tiers; registrant/client ID lookup service confirmed; v1 redoc deprecation date July 31 2026 surfaced in results.

*Datasets:* Senate LDA API: https://lda.senate.gov/api/; Registrant/Client ID lookup: https://lda.senate.gov/registrants/public/registrant-client/lookup/

**ROR ID — research organizations**

IDENTIFIES: ~110k research organizations worldwide (universities, hospitals, agencies, funders) with a persistent ROR ID. FLAGSHIP: ROR data dump on Zenodo — https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6347574 — full registry, JSON + CSV, CC0, new release roughly monthly, programmatic retrieval via Zenodo API; live API at api.ror.org. TIER: STEEL. UNLOCKS: institution-level rollups — ROR records carry external IDs (Wikidata, ISNI, funder IDs), and ROR is the org key in OpenAlex/Crossref, so university/hospital research output becomes joinable. BRIDGE: research institutions ↔ EIN (IRS 990/BMF, landed) and ↔ NIH/NSF grantee orgs (below) — the org-resolution glue for the whole research-money domain.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: Zenodo ror-data community hosts the full dump (JSON/CSV, v1/v2 schema) with documented API retrieval; ROR docs confirm CC0 and release cadence.

*Datasets:* ROR data dump: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6347574; ROR API: https://api.ror.org

**State Secretary-of-State entity numbers — the incorporation layer**

IDENTIFIES: every corporation/LLC at formation — the layer BELOW every federal ID, where shells are born. Per-state namespace (state + entity number). FLAGSHIP for free bulk: Colorado — full business-entity dataset on https://data.colorado.gov (1M+ records, entity ID, registered agent, addresses, status; Socrata CSV/API, free). Several other states (WA, others) publish similar; many (DE!) do not. TIER: STEEL within a state. UNLOCKS: registered-agent clustering — 'one agent address, four hundred contractors' — and shell-behind-the-contractor tracing. BRIDGE: SAM registrations (UEI, landed) record state of incorporation; EIN↔entity via name/address. Recommend landing 3-5 open-data states first rather than chasing all 50.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: data.colorado.gov hosts the complete SOS business-entities dataset for free bulk download with entityid as unique key; Colorado SOS pages confirm the Information Marketplace as the official channel.

*Datasets:* Colorado business entities: https://data.colorado.gov (SOS Business Entities dataset)

**UK Companies House — free bulk company numbers, officers, and beneficial owners (the international model)**

IDENTIFIES: every UK company (company number), its officers, and its beneficial owners (PSC — persons with significant control). FLAGSHIP: free monthly full-company snapshot CSV at http://download.companieshouse.gov.uk (no registration), PSC bulk product, and a free JSON API (600 req/5min) at https://developer.company-information.service.gov.uk . TIER: STEEL. UNLOCKS: the offshore/UK-shell end of US stories — UK LLPs and PSC-declared owners recur in sanctions-evasion and procurement cases. BRIDGE: the sleeper — GLEIF LEI records (ALREADY LANDED) carry each entity's local registration authority + registry number, so Ripple's LEI table already maps LEI↔Companies House number natively for UK LEI holders. This is the template for 'one national registry, fully open' — the standard to hold US states against.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: download.companieshouse.gov.uk free monthly bulk CSV confirmed (no key/login), PSC and accounts bulk products confirmed, free API with 600/5min rate limit confirmed. GLEIF RA/registration-number fields are standard LEI-CDF schema (verify column presence in Ripple's landed GLEIF staging).

**DOL OFLC case numbers (LCA / PERM / H-2A / H-2B) — immigration labor**

Per-application case numbers for H-1B Labor Condition Applications, PERM green-card certifications, and H-2A/H-2B temporary labor. Flagship: OFLC Performance Data (https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/foreign-labor/performance) — quarterly xlsx disclosure files per program with record layouts, covering employer name/address, job, wage, worksite; data.gov entry: https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/office-of-foreign-labor-certification-oflc-case-disclosure-data. Tier: case number = STEEL per application (docket-style); the EMPLOYER is the entity of interest and employer FEIN is NOT reliably present across programs/years — treat employer resolution as PROBABILISTIC name/address until the record layouts are checked vintage by vintage (some older files did carry FEIN). Bridges: employer name → EIN/UEI; WHD debarment lists and OFLC debarments close the loop. Ripple question: 'Which employers certified for thousands of visa workers at suspiciously low prevailing wages also show up in WHD wage-theft enforcement — sponsor-and-underpay as a pattern?'
