**FACILITY_ID looks like a key but is mostly a trap - name frequency is not joinability**

FACILITY_ID is the 12th most common identifier-shaped name (254 datasets, 38 portals) but samples show each agency mints its own: childcare centers, restaurant inspections, vaccination sites - none share an ID scheme across sources. Same verdict for CASE_NUMBER (753 ds / 59 portals: samples span police incidents, zoning scan logs, wetlands, dumpster violations - semantically scattered, joinable only within one agency's own systems) and GTFS STOP_ID (180/36, agency-feed-scoped). One important exception inside the trap: FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_COMPARE in LANDING has a column literally named FACILITY_ID that is actually a CCN - column-name tagging alone would miss a known key hiding under a generic name.

*Evidence:* FACILITY_ID 254 ds / 38 portals but sample titles show incompatible schemes (Buncombe childcare, Austin food inspections, Chicago COVID vaccination sites, Colorado restaurant inspections). LANDING check shows FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_COMPARE.FACILITY_ID among 21 tables with the name.

*Datasets:* Food Establishment Inspection Scores (Austin); COVID-19 Vaccination Locations - Historical (Chicago); FED_CMS_HOSPITAL_COMPARE (FACILITY_ID column is a CCN in disguise)

**DEA number is overvalued as a hunt key — there has been no open bulk registrant file since 2020**

DEA registration data was formerly sold as flat-file subscriptions through NTIS; that ended November 2020 when DEA took the database back and now grants access by individual application and fee, mostly for credentialing use cases. Public bulk appearances of DEA numbers are one-off artifacts (the ARCOS opioid litigation release covering 2006-2014). Unless Ripple pays and qualifies for access, DEA is a key the tagger can recognize but never join on. Keep it as tagger-known metadata; do not plan hunts around it. NPI already covers the prescriber universe with free data.

*Evidence:* NTIS discontinued its CSA/DEA registration subscription service effective Nov 17, 2020 (deachronicles.com, classic.ntis.gov/products/dea); DEA now runs application-based access to the CSA Registration Information Database. No open bulk file exists.

*Datasets:* ARCOS litigation release (historical, one-off)

**VIN is not a bulk join key — NMVTIS is closed, and vehicles aren't entities on Ripple's spine anyway**

Two independent problems. Access: the only national title/brand/salvage database (NMVTIS) is available solely through DOJ-approved commercial providers on a per-report basis, with DPPA stripping owner identity — there is no free bulk VIN file, and the owner linkage (the part Ripple would actually want) is exactly what's redacted. Semantics: a VIN identifies a vehicle, not a person or company, so even a perfect VIN join connects records to an object, not to an accountable entity. NHTSA's free flat files are complaint/recall-level with inconsistent VIN capture. VIN belongs as a record-level attribute the tagger recognizes, not a planned connection key.

*Evidence:* NMVTIS consumer access is only via approved data providers (vehiclehistory.bja.ojp.gov/nmvtis_vehiclehistory); DPPA prohibits owner name/address in reports (VINData FAQ, AAMVA NMVTIS pages: 'No personal identifying information will be made available'). NHTSA ODI complaints flat file (static.nhtsa.gov/odi/ffdd/cmpl/) is the main free VIN-bearing dataset and is self-reported complaint data.

*Datasets:* NHTSA ODI complaints flat file; NHTSA recalls (make/model-level, not VIN)

**APN is county-scoped by construction and should be demoted out of the key list into the GEO lane**

Assessor Parcel Numbers are assigned independently by ~3,000 county assessors with incompatible formats; the same APN string recurs across counties, and there is no free national parcel file (national layers like Regrid are commercial). An APN is only meaningful as (county FIPS + APN), and even then it identifies land, not an owner — owner linkage requires the county's assessment roll, which varies in availability and quality. This is a GEO-tier locator that can support a specific county-level investigation, never a national hunt key. Listing it beside DEA/CLIA overstates it.

*Evidence:* No federal or national open APN registry exists; parcel data aggregation is a commercial industry (Regrid, CoreLogic) precisely because formats and access are per-county. Any de-duplication requires pairing APN with a county identifier, which makes it definitionally not a standalone key.

*Datasets:* County assessor rolls (per-county); Regrid (commercial)

**SIC and NAICS are classification codes, not connection keys — sharing one is a cohort, not a connection**

Both appear in the tagger-known list alongside real entity IDs, but two companies sharing NAICS 621111 are not connected — they're just both doctors' offices. These codes can never produce a lead of the form 'same entity in two datasets'; they produce peer groups for benchmarking ('this nursing home chain vs. its industry'). That's genuinely useful, but it's a different machine part. SIC specifically survives only inside EDGAR (SEC still assigns SIC codes to filers); everywhere else NAICS replaced it in 1997. Recommendation: move both out of the connection-key tiers into a separate 'cohort attribute' bucket so the hunter never treats a code match as a hit.

*Evidence:* SIC was superseded by NAICS as the federal statistical standard in 1997 (OMB/Census); SEC EDGAR remains the notable SIC holdout, assigning SIC codes on filings. Neither code is unique per entity — they are many-entities-per-code by design, which fails even the STRONG tier's premise of connective value.

*Datasets:* EDGAR company filings (SIC); SAM/USAspending (NAICS as attribute)

**ORCID is low-value for harm mapping — self-asserted, patchy, and federal grant data doesn't key on it**

ORCID sits in new candidates but fails the 'who gets hurt' test and the join test at once. Coverage is voluntary and skewed toward active academics; the identifier is self-managed (researchers control their own record contents); and the federal datasets Ripple would join it against key people their own way — NIH RePORTER uses internal person profile IDs, NSF awards key on institutions. Research-integrity stories (retractions, undisclosed foreign funding) are real but are case-work domains, not bulk-join domains. Keep ORCID as tagger-known text; don't spend hunt capacity on it.

*Evidence:* ORCID registration is voluntary and record contents are researcher-controlled per ORCID's own model; NIH RePORTER's person-level linkage runs on NIH profile person IDs rather than ORCID as the join key. No major federal harm dataset is ORCID-keyed in bulk.

*Datasets:* NIH RePORTER; NSF award data

**IRS PTIN — sounds like a key, is not one in public data**

CALIBRATION WARNING for the candidate list: the Preparer Tax Identification Number looks like a perfect STEEL key for the tax-preparer industry (700k+ preparers, IRS-assigned, unique). But the FOIA-released PTIN holder files deliberately EXCLUDE the actual PTIN — you get name, credential type, and business address only. So the public data is PROBABILISTIC (name/address), not STEEL, and any pipeline that budgets PTIN as a real join key will be disappointed. The searchable IRS credentialed-preparer directory is lookup-only and covers only a subset. Verdict: track preparers via the FOIA name/address file if a tax-prep story demands it, but do not add PTIN to the key registry as a STEEL identifier.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: irs.gov 'PTIN information and the Freedom of Information Act' page confirms FOIA listing releases contact data but the actual PTIN is not made available; the IRS credentialed-preparer directory confirmed as partial-coverage lookup only.

*Datasets:* IRS PTIN FOIA info: https://www.irs.gov/tax-professionals/ptin-information-and-the-freedom-of-information-act

**EPA NPDES is not a standalone key — FRS is a crosswalk hub that delivers NPDES plus a dozen sibling program IDs in one load**

The list carries FRS_ID (planned) and EPA NPDES (new candidate) as unrelated items. FRS is EPA's master entity registry: its public download includes a Program Links file mapping each FRS REGISTRY_ID to program-system IDs across ICIS-NPDES (water), RCRAInfo (hazardous waste), TRI (toxics), ICIS-Air, SDWIS (drinking water violations — a harm-heavy sibling nobody listed), RMP, GHG, and Superfund/SEMS. Hunting NPDES separately duplicates work FRS already did; the right move is one FRS ingest that makes every EPA program ID a spoke. SDWIS in particular (who's drinking water with violations) belongs on the map.

*Evidence:* EPA FRS description (epa.gov/frs/frs-description) and ECHO FRS download documentation (echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads/frs-download-summary) document the Program Links file cross-referencing REGISTRY_ID to ICIS-NPDES, RCRAInfo, TRI, ICIS-Air, SDWIS, RMP, SEMS and others; EPA publishes explicit FRS program crosswalks (epa.gov/frs/frs-program-crosswalks).

*Datasets:* EPA FRS national download; ECHO exporter; SDWIS drinking water violations; TRI; RCRAInfo

**ISIN is redundant with CUSIP for US securities, and both are licensing-encumbered — FIGI is the open key missing from the list**

For US securities the ISIN is mechanically 'US' + the 9-character CUSIP + a check digit — carrying both as separate hunt keys double-counts one identifier. Worse, both are proprietary: CUSIP is owned by the ABA and operated commercially, and redistribution is restricted enough that even OpenFIGI refuses to return CUSIP/ISIN values in API results. CUSIPs seen inside public SEC filings (13F, N-PORT) are usable as found, but building and republishing a CUSIP-keyed master index is a licensing exposure. The open alternative, FIGI (Bloomberg's Financial Instrument Global Identifier, free unlimited OpenFIGI API that maps from CUSIP/ISIN/ticker), is absent from the list entirely.

*Evidence:* ISIN construction from national identifiers (CUSIP for US) plus check digit is the ISO 6166 standard. OpenFIGI FAQ (openfigi.com/about/faq) states FIGI is provided at no cost as a public good and that third-party proprietary identifiers (ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL) are not returned in results 'because of licensing/redistribution restrictions' — direct evidence of the encumbrance on the other two keys.

*Datasets:* SEC 13F holdings (CUSIP as filed); N-PORT fund holdings; OpenFIGI mapping API

**DUNS is dead for procurement but is FDA's live establishment identifier — its value is mislabeled in both directions**

In the UEI era DUNS adds nothing to the wired procurement stack: SAM dropped DUNS in April 2022, and historical USAspending rows carry both DUNS and UEI, so the legacy crosswalk is largely embedded in data Ripple already holds. But writing DUNS off entirely is also wrong: FDA's preferred Unique Facility Identifier for drug establishment registration is the DUNS number, so FDA drug establishment/listing data is DUNS-keyed today. Net: demote DUNS from general-purpose key to a single-purpose bridge into FDA-land — where it links pharma manufacturing sites to the corporate spine.

*Evidence:* FDA eDRLS guidance (fda.gov, 'Electronic Drug Registration and Listing System') states DUNS is FDA's preferred UFI and is required for establishment registration; FDA's UFI specification document (fda.gov/media/89926/download) formalizes it. GSA completed the DUNS-to-UEI transition April 2022 and SAM extracts are UEI-keyed (open.gsa.gov SAM extract layouts).

*Datasets:* FDA drug establishment registration & listing (DUNS/FEI-keyed); USAspending pre-2022 archives (DUNS+UEI both present)

## Join mechanisms that are not shared IDs

**VIN and PHONE_NUMBER - two non-obvious cross-source match mechanisms**

Two survivors are not registry keys but real entity-resolution mechanisms. VIN (24 ds / 11 portals) is globally unique per vehicle and links parking citations, DMV registrations, car-share fleets, and city auction lots - a vehicle-level spine for towing/citation-abuse or fleet stories. PHONE_NUMBER (619 ds / 64 portals) is not an ID, but shared phone numbers across business licenses, facility rosters, and complaint datasets are a classic same-operator signal - useful as a fuzzy-match feature for the entity spine, in the same tier as NAME/ADDRESS which the tagger already has.

*Evidence:* VIN: 24 datasets / 11 portals (Parking Citations LA, NY DMV Peer To Peer Car Sharing, KC Monthly Car Auction). PHONE_NUMBER: 619 datasets / 64 portals from the main identifier sweep - the 3rd most common identifier-shaped column overall.

*Datasets:* Parking Citations (DataLA, VIN); DMV Peer To Peer Car Sharing (New York State, VIN); Kansas City Monthly Car Auction (VIN)

**LEIE rows with no NPI matched to NPPES/Medicare billing via name+DOB+address**

MECHANISM: Many LEIE exclusion records (pre-2008 exclusions and most business entities) carry no NPI, so the wired NPI join silently misses them. Match LEIE last/first/middle name + date of birth (LEIE carries DOB for individuals) + city/state against the NPPES roster and Medicare provider utilization files. WHO GETS HURT: patients treated by, and taxpayers billed by, providers who were banned for fraud or patient abuse but are still enrolled under an NPI the ban list never linked. This is the fallback that keeps Ripple's flagship 'banned but still operating' lens honest — the ID join alone undercounts the banned population. TIER: PROBABILISTIC. Corroboration needed: exact DOB match, specialty consistency between the exclusion record and the NPPES taxonomy, state overlap, and OIG's own SSN-verification service for candidate matches (OIG confirms a match can be uniquely verified by SSN).

*Evidence:* HHS-OIG Exclusions FAQ states outright that many excluded individuals and entities have no NPI in the LEIE (NPIs only added since 2008) and that candidate matches are verified via SSN: https://oig.hhs.gov/faqs/exclusions-faq/ . The entire compliance-screening industry exists because this match cannot be done on ID alone; billing for an excluded person carries CMPs up to $20,000 per item.

*Datasets:* LEIE exclusion list (rows lacking NPI); NPPES roster; Medicare provider utilization

**Address-cluster anomaly detection across NPPES practice addresses**

MECHANISM: Normalize NPPES practice addresses (suite-level), count distinct NPIs and organization enumerations per address, and flag anomalous hubs; then intersect the hub population with LEIE exclusions and Part D prescribing outliers at the same address. No ID is shared — the address itself is the join. WHO GETS HURT: Medicare/Medicaid patients funneled through shell clinics and phantom home-health/hospice agencies; the pattern marks fraud infrastructure before individual actors are charged. TIER: PROBABILISTIC as an entity link, but STRONG as a lead-ranking signal. Corroboration needed: distinguish legitimate medical office buildings and registered-agent addresses (business-type mix at the address, enumeration-date bunching, shared authorized officials across the NPIs at the hub).

*Evidence:* HHS-OIG found 112 different licensed hospice agencies registered at a single Los Angeles County address (House Energy & Commerce letter citing OIG: https://energycommerce.house.gov/posts/chairmen-guthrie-joyce-griffith-smith-schweikert-and-buchanan-ask-hhs-oig-about-ongoing-hha-and-hospice-fraud-in-los-angeles-county-1). OIG's nationwide home-health fraud analysis (OEI-05-16-00031, https://oig.hhs.gov/oei/reports/oei-05-16-00031.asp) flagged 500+ HHAs and 4,500+ physicians in 27 geographic hotspots using exactly these clustering characteristics.

*Datasets:* NPPES roster (practice addresses, authorized officials); LEIE; Part D prescribers

**SAM exclusions matched to USAspending recipients by name+address after exclusion date**

MECHANISM: Exclusion evasion works by obtaining a fresh UEI or filing under a name variant, so the wired UEI join only catches the honest crooks. Match excluded entity names + addresses (and excluded individuals' names appearing as officers of recipient entities) against USAspending prime and sub-award recipients, restricted to awards dated AFTER the exclusion date — a name+address+temporal co-occurrence, not an ID join. WHO GETS HURT: taxpayers, and the honest bidders displaced, when debarred contractors (fraud, safety violations, illegal dumping) keep winning federal money. TIER: PROBABILISTIC. Corroboration needed: exact street-address match, award-after-exclusion timing, shared officer names, and continuity of NAICS/industry between the excluded firm and the suspect recipient.

*Evidence:* GAO-09-174 'Excluded Parties List System: Suspended and Debarred Businesses and Individuals Improperly Receive Federal Funds' (https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-09-174) documented exactly this failure — including a case where USDA's exclusion search missed a debarred company because of a missing comma in the name — proving both that the leak is real and that naive exact-name matching is not enough.

*Datasets:* SAM exclusions; USAspending prime awards; USAspending sub-awards

**Temporal dose-response: Open Payments payment stream vs Part D brand-prescribing shift**

MECHANISM: The entity link is the NPI, but the LEAD is not the ID — it is the systematic temporal correlation between two filing streams Ripple already holds: industry payment events (Open Payments, 3 years wired) and subsequent changes in a doctor's brand-name prescribing share (Part D), with the paying manufacturer matched to the manufacturer of the prescribed drug. Within-doctor before/after comparison across the 3 payment years is the signal. WHO GETS HURT: patients steered to expensive brand drugs (and their side-effect profiles) because of a payment relationship, and Part D/taxpayers paying the brand premium. TIER: STRONG as a statistical signal but strictly correlational — the corroboration is the within-doctor design (same doctor, prescribing shift after payment onset), manufacturer-to-drug matching, and specialty-peer baselines. Never publishable per-doctor without human review; it ranks who to look at.

*Evidence:* ProPublica Dollars for Docs, 'Now There's Proof: Docs Who Get Company Cash Tend to Prescribe More Brand-Name Meds' (2016, https://www.propublica.org/article/doctors-who-take-company-cash-tend-to-prescribe-more-brand-name-drugs) analyzed 150,323 physicians across five specialties and found a near-linear payment-to-brand-prescribing relationship; methodology at https://projects.propublica.org/graphics/d4dpartd-methodology . Ripple holds all the ingredients ProPublica used.

*Datasets:* Open Payments (3 years); Part D prescribers; NPPES roster (specialty)

**AIS behavioral joins: dark gaps, two-hull rendezvous, and post-designation identity churn**

THREE MECHANISMS on the already-wired IMO datasets, none reducible to an ID column: (1) DARK GAPS — AIS transmission gaps in NOAA AIS tracks near sanctioned ports or SDN-associated routes; (2) RENDEZVOUS — two vessels loitering at the same position/time window at sea (a pairwise spatiotemporal self-join of AIS against itself) = likely ship-to-ship transfer; (3) IDENTITY CHURN — vessel rename, reflag, or suspicious IMO re-registration within N days AFTER an OFAC SDN designation date (temporal correlation of a registry event with an enforcement event). WHO GETS HURT: sanctions regimes exist because the cargo funds weapons programs and repression; evasion also endangers crews and coastal environments via the uninsured shadow fleet. TIER: PROBABILISTIC. Corroboration needed: satellite imagery of the rendezvous position, draught/cargo changes, physical vessel characteristics vs registry claims.

*Evidence:* C4ADS 'Unmasked' (2021, https://c4ads.org/unmasked) documented vessel identity laundering — at least 11 ships creating fraudulent IMO registrations to shed sanctioned identities — plus AIS-disabling and STS transfers in DPRK evasion networks; Planet/C4ADS satellite work confirmed AIS-dark fuel deliveries to North Korea (https://www.planet.com/pulse/planets-data-used-to-reveal-illicit-shipping-networks-delivering-fuel-to-north-korea-in-violation-of-un-sanctions/).

*Datasets:* NOAA AIS; OFAC SDN ships (IMO + designation dates)

**HCRIS related-party disclosures + ownership-name clustering across nursing home CCNs**

MECHANISM: Medicare cost reports (fed_cms_hcris is staged) contain related-party transaction and home-office disclosures — one filing citing the names of affiliated companies. CMS nursing-home ownership data lists owner/officer names with no NPI or EIN. Cluster facilities by shared owner names + addresses across CCNs, then join each cluster to the wired CCN quality/staffing/deficiency tables. This is officer-name network matching plus document-level disclosure, not an ID join. WHO GETS HURT: nursing-home residents whose facilities run 'underfunded' while owners pay themselves through related management/realty/supply companies — the money is extracted before it reaches staffing. TIER: PROBABILISTIC on the name clustering. Corroboration needed: address overlap between owner entities, PECOS ownership percentages, consistent officer role titles, and the HCRIS related-party dollar amounts themselves.

*Evidence:* KFF Health News (Jordan Rau), 'Care Suffers As More Nursing Homes Feed Money Into Corporate Webs' (2018, https://kffhealthnews.org/aging/care-suffers-as-more-nursing-homes-feed-money-into-corporate-webs/) used exactly these cost-report disclosures: $11 billion in related-party payments in 2015, spanning 11,000+ homes (~3/4 of the industry), tied to concrete harm cases like Allenbrooke. NOTE: Ripple just retired the facility-affiliation panel (commit 287f453), which raises the value of this non-ID bridge into the CCN world.

*Datasets:* fed_cms_hcris (cost reports); fed_cms_nursing_home tables; CMS nursing-home ownership file (candidate load)

**Shared officers and hub addresses across 990/BMF/5500 filings (dark-money and captive-vendor networks)**

MECHANISM: Form 990 lists officers/directors and paid preparer; Form 5500 lists plan sponsors/administrators and Schedule C service providers; IRS BMF gives addresses. Cluster filings that share officer names, a street address, or a preparer — the network, not any ID, is the join. Flag hub addresses hosting many nominally independent nonprofits and officer names recurring across entities that grant to each other. WHO GETS HURT: donors and voters (dark-money pass-throughs erase accountability) and plan participants/nonprofit beneficiaries (captive service arrangements drain assets to insiders). TIER: PROBABILISTIC. Corroboration needed: two-plus shared officers, address match at suite level, and money flows between the clustered entities (990 Schedule I grants citing recipient EINs — a document-citation edge). DEPENDENCY: Ripple's IRS 990 load is stale (~200 rows, already flagged) — this mechanism is the concrete reason that load is worth fixing.

*Evidence:* Politico (Nov 2019) exposed the Sixteen Thirty Fund / Arabella network as a 'massive dark money group'; the network's four nonprofits share one downtown DC address and moved ~$600M in 2018 (summarized with 990-based sourcing at https://www.influencewatch.org/for-profit/arabella-advisors/ and https://www.tabletmag.com/sections/news/articles/for-profit-dc-firm-staging-americas-grassroots-movements-arabella-advisors). The investigation is built entirely on shared-address/shared-officer/grant-flow analysis of 990s.

*Datasets:* IRS 990 (needs re-load); IRS BMF; DOL Form 5500; IRS revocations

**CFPB complaint company names matched to GLEIF/HMDA lender identities**

MECHANISM: fed_cfpb_complaints is already staged, but complaints identify companies as normalized free-text names, not LEIs. Match complaint company names against GLEIF legal names (plus GLEIF's 'other/previous names') and HMDA filer names to compute complaint density per lender, then read it against that lender's HMDA lending pattern (denial rates by race/geography, product mix). WHO GETS HURT: borrowers — the compound question is whether lenders generating outsized mortgage-servicing complaints are the same lenders whose HMDA footprints show disparate denial patterns in the same metros. TIER: PROBABILISTIC name match. Corroboration needed: GLEIF alternate-name records, address/state agreement, and CFPB's own company-normalization (the complaint DB only includes companies that responded, which itself constrains matches).

*Evidence:* The HMDA half of this is the mechanism behind Reveal's Pulitzer-finalist 'Kept Out' redlining investigation (2018, Aaron Glantz/Emmanuel Martinez), which computed lender-level disparity from HMDA; complaint-per-lender analyses are standard CFPB-data journalism. The name-to-LEI step is the only novel engineering, and GLEIF publishes alternate names precisely to support it.

*Datasets:* fed_cfpb_complaints; CFPB HMDA (LEI); GLEIF registry

**Open Payments teaching-hospital recipients bridged to CCN facility tables by name+address**

MECHANISM: Open Payments records payments to teaching hospitals by name/address with no CCN, so industry money to institutions is currently stranded in the NPI-world tables. Match teaching-hospital names + addresses (CMS publishes an annual covered-recipient teaching hospital list to normalize against) to the 8 wired CCN facility tables. WHO GETS HURT: patients at hospitals whose device/drug purchasing and research priorities track industry payments; the join lets Ripple put facility-level quality and deficiency data next to facility-level industry money for the first time. TIER: PROBABILISTIC. Corroboration needed: CMS covered-recipient list as the name authority, hospital-name normalization (systems vs campuses), and city/state agreement. Elevated in value because the NPI-to-CCN affiliation table was just retired (commit 287f453) — name+address bridging is now one of the few roads between Ripple's two biggest health islands.

*Evidence:* CMS's Open Payments teaching-hospital covered-recipient list carries name/address but no CCN (structural fact of the dataset, verifiable in the Open Payments data dictionary); the retirement of fed_cms_facility_affiliation in this repo (git log: 'retire affiliations panel ... source table removal') is the internal evidence that the ID road between the NPI and CCN worlds is gone and a probabilistic bridge is needed.

*Datasets:* Open Payments (teaching hospital records); CMS facility tables (CCN); fed_cms_nursing_home

**The key list has a structural blind spot: several of the highest-harm datasets carry no ID at all**

A hunt plan organized purely as a key list will structurally never touch datasets whose only entity handle is a name and address: OSHA inspections/violations (establishment name/address, no EIN), state WARN layoff notices, the SBA PPP loan release (borrower name/address — EIN withheld), and FEC individual contributions (free-text employer field). These are core who-gets-hurt datasets. The PROBABILISTIC lane needs to be a first-class hunting mechanism — seeded by the entities the ID keys already anchor (SAM names/addresses, BMF names, NPPES addresses) — not a leftover tier. Otherwise the list quietly defines these harms out of scope.

*Evidence:* DOL/OSHA enforcement downloads (enforcement.dol.gov) schema is establishment name/address-keyed with no federal entity ID; SBA's PPP FOIA release fields are borrower name/address/lender with no EIN; FEC individual contribution files carry contributor employer as unvalidated free text. All three are widely used in accountability journalism only via name/address matching.

*Datasets:* OSHA inspections/violations; SBA PPP FOIA release; State WARN notices; FEC individual contributions

**OpenCorporates — the aggregation layer for company numbers (licensing is the catch)**

WHAT IT IS: not a new ID but the canonicalizer — jurisdiction + company number as one global key across 140+ registries, solving the 50-state SoS mess in one dataset. ACCESS/LICENSE (the load-bearing detail): database is ODbL; API is free ONLY for open/share-alike projects with attribution; investigative journalists / public-benefit NGOs can apply for free at-scale bulk access but must disclose the project to qualify; commercial API from ~£2,250/yr, bulk by quote. TIER: STEEL (once mapped through it). FIT FOR RIPPLE: share-alike + must-disclose-the-story conditions sit awkwardly with pre-publication investigations — RED-lane call for Chris on whether to apply, since it means telling a third party what Ripple is probing. Fallback: land open-data states directly (previous finding) + Companies House (next).

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: opencorporates.com/legal/licence confirms ODbL and share-alike free tier; their journalist/NGO access page confirms free at-scale access requires disclosing non-public story rationale to qualify as a Permitted User; pricing from £2,250/yr confirmed.

*Datasets:* OpenCorporates API: https://api.opencorporates.com; License terms: https://opencorporates.com/legal/licence

**OpenSanctions — pre-resolved global sanctions/PEP layer on top of landed lists**

WHAT IT IS: an entity-resolution product, not a registry — 400+ sanctions lists, PEP rosters, and watchlists merged into FollowTheMoney entities with cluster IDs and referent lists back to source IDs (OFAC, BIS, EU, UN...). FLAGSHIP: daily bulk JSON/CSV at https://www.opensanctions.org/datasets/ — free for non-commercial use, commercial license required otherwise (Ripple likely qualifies as non-commercial journalism now; re-check if the platform ever monetizes). TIER: the MATCHES it ships are effectively STRONG-to-STEEL because they preserve source IDs; its own cluster IDs are unstable by design (track referents, not just cluster ID). UNLOCKS: 'is this counterparty sanctioned ANYWHERE on earth, or a politically exposed person?' — extends the landed OFAC-only lens to every jurisdiction at once, plus gives Ripple a free benchmark for its own name-matching. BRIDGE: referents point directly at landed SDN entries.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: opensanctions.org bulk docs confirm daily full-dataset JSON/CSV downloads, 412-source default collection, free non-commercial / paid commercial licensing, and the documented caveat that cluster IDs change and referent lists must be tracked.

*Datasets:* OpenSanctions bulk: https://www.opensanctions.org/datasets/; Licensing: https://www.opensanctions.org/licensing/

**EPA FRS 'program interest linkages' file — the rosetta stone for the whole EPA family**

Not a new ID — a shipped JOIN TABLE. ECHO publishes an FRS program-interest linkage download that maps EPA's Facility Registry Service ID (FRS_ID, already planned/spec-only in Ripple) to every program-specific ID at the same physical site: RCRA handler, NPDES permit, ICIS-Air, TRI, and more. One acquisition turns FRS_ID from a spec into a hub connecting four-plus enforcement datasets at once. ECHO's page states directly: to join across datasets, 'use the FRS program interest linkages download.' Mechanism tier: the linkage itself is registry-grade (STEEL joins), maintained by EPA. This changes FRS_ID's priority: it should jump the queue because it comes with its own crosswalk pre-built.

*Evidence:* WebFetch of https://echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads confirmed all four datasets carry FRS ID and the page's own instruction to use the FRS program interest linkages download for cross-dataset joins.

*Datasets:* https://echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads

## Whole domains and IDs nobody listed

**FILER_ID - campaign-finance filer IDs open a politics/money domain the key list lacks**

FILER_ID appears on 5 portals and is the spine of state campaign-finance disclosure systems: the same filer ID links candidates/committees to their contributions, expenditures, and surplus-funds reports (NY State BOE filer IDs, California FPPC filer IDs used by both SF and Oakland, WA PDC). Cross-source within each state system, and California's is shared across multiple city portals. No key in the current vocabulary covers political money at all - this is the cheapest entry point for a follow-the-money lens.

*Evidence:* FILER_ID family: 57 datasets / 5 portals. Sample titles are all campaign finance: NYS 'Campaign Finance Filer Data: Beginning 1974', Oakland 'FPPC Form 460 Schedule A - Monetary Contributions', SF 'Campaign Finance - State Filer Data', WA 'Candidate Surplus Funds Latest Report'.

*Datasets:* Campaign Finance Filer Data: Beginning 1974 (New York State); Campaign Finance - FPPC Form 460 - Schedule A (Oakland); Campaign Finance - State Filer Data (SF OpenData); Candidate Surplus Funds Latest Report (Washington State)

**LDA lobbying reports citing bill numbers joined to Voteview rollcalls and committee seats**

MECHANISM: Lobbying Disclosure Act reports (not yet in holdings) name the specific bills lobbied, in free text. Parse bill numbers out of report text and join to Ripple's wired Voteview rollcalls and committee-membership tables — a document-level citation link from private influence to public votes. WHO GETS HURT: constituents whose representatives' committee assignments and votes track lobbied interests rather than district interests; the mechanism turns 'who lobbied' + 'who voted how' into one graph. TIER: the bill-number citation itself is near-STEEL (bill IDs are unique per Congress); the influence inference is PROBABILISTIC and needs the committee-jurisdiction match plus vote-timing relative to lobbying-report quarters. This is a new-domain ingest (Senate LDA filings are free bulk XML) rather than a new mechanism on held data — flagged because the join target (Voteview + committees) is already wired.

*Evidence:* MIT's LobbyView project (In Song Kim) built exactly this linkage at scale — 1.2M LDA reports parsed and matched to congressional bills (paper: https://web.mit.edu/insong/www/pdf/lobbyview.pdf, data: https://www.lobbyview.org/data-download/), proving the citation-extraction join is tractable and research-grade.

*Datasets:* Senate LDA lobbying reports (candidate ingest); Voteview rollcalls; fed_congress_committee_membership

**USDOT/MC is badly undervalued — it is the trucking version of Ripple's flagship 'banned but still operating' lens**

USDOT number sits in 'new candidates (unconfirmed)' but should be near the top of the hunt list. FMCSA's carrier census, inspections, crashes, safety ratings, and out-of-service orders are all free bulk data keyed by USDOT number. More importantly, the domain has a named, government-documented fraud mechanism that is structurally identical to Ripple's first story: 'chameleon carriers' — carriers shut down by out-of-service orders that re-register under a fresh USDOT number to shed their safety record. FMCSA even has a rule (49 CFR 386.73) for consolidating records of reincarnated carriers. This is a mechanism-first systemic pattern with people getting killed on the other end of the number.

*Evidence:* GAO reviewed chameleon carriers and found FMCSA could not readily count them among tens of thousands of new applicants (GAO-12-364 line of work; gao.justia.com motor carrier safety reports). FMCSA's 2012 final rule under 49 CFR 386.73 targets carriers operating 'under a new identity...to avoid being linked to a negative compliance history.' Industry and FMCSA analyses report reincarnated carriers are roughly 3x more likely to be involved in serious crashes than legitimate new entrants. FMCSA census/inspection/crash files are public bulk downloads keyed by USDOT number.

*Datasets:* FMCSA Motor Carrier Census (MCMIS); FMCSA inspections and crash files; FMCSA out-of-service orders; SAFER/Licensing & Insurance (L&I)

**NIH core project numbers + NSF award IDs — federal research grants as join keys**

IDENTIFIES: not entities but AWARDS — and the award number is the join key that stitches a whole domain together. FLAGSHIP: NIH ExPORTER bulk files — https://reporter.nih.gov/exporter (projects, PIs, publications, patents, clinical studies, per-fiscal-year CSVs, free; live API at api.reporter.nih.gov) and NSF award downloads — https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/download.jsp (full corpus, JSON since Jan 2025, free; API at resources.research.gov). TIER: STEEL as a key. UNLOCKS: the research-money lens: NIH core project number links grants → resulting patents → clinical trials (Ripple already stages fed_clinicaltrials — NIH links core project numbers to NCT IDs) → publications. BRIDGE: grant FAIN in USAspending assistance awards (UEI, landed) is the grant number — so grants join straight into the landed spending spine; PI names → NPI for physician-researchers (Open Payments research payments, landed). Question: 'whose federally funded research becomes whose private patent, and which trial PIs also take industry money?'

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: NIH ExPORTER bulk files confirmed with Core_Project_Num linking patents and clinical-studies files; RePORTER API confirmed; NSF awardsearch/download.jsp confirmed full-corpus download, converted to JSON in Jan 2025, plus resources.research.gov API.

*Datasets:* NIH ExPORTER: https://reporter.nih.gov/exporter; NSF award downloads: https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/download.jsp; NSF award API: https://resources.research.gov/common/webapi/awardapisearch-v1.htm

**DOL OLMS file number — labor unions and their finances [extra angle 2]**

IDENTIFIES: every labor union required to file under LMRDA — stable OLMS file number per union — plus annual LM-2/3/4 finances: officers by name and salary, receipts, disbursements, vendors. FLAGSHIP: OLMS Online Public Disclosure Room — https://olmsapps.dol.gov/olpdr/ — free yearly bulk zips (pipe-delimited, ~46 related tables per year: filings, officers, disbursements, payers/payees). TIER: STEEL (file number), and LM filings also carry the union's EIN — a direct join into Ripple's landed EIN spine (Form 5500 and IRS 990 for the same unions). UNLOCKS: a whole unworked domain — union officer self-dealing, vendor clustering, pension (5500) vs. union (LM-2) money flows for the same EIN. Cheap, structured, and nobody else is systematically cross-keying it.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: olmsapps.dol.gov/olpdr confirmed with 'Download Yearly Data' bulk zips in pipe-delimited format (46 text files per year); DOL's Guide to Working with Downloaded LM Filing Data confirms schema; LM forms collect EIN per DOL documentation.

*Datasets:* OLMS disclosure room + bulk: https://olmsapps.dol.gov/olpdr/; Guide: https://olmsapps.dol.gov/olpdr/Guide_to_Working_with_OLMS_LM_Data.pdf

**FSIS Establishment Number — meat/poultry/egg plants (new domain: food production)**

USDA FSIS establishment number (e.g. 'EST. 38' / 'P-1234') stamped on every federally inspected meat/poultry/egg product. Flagship: Meat, Poultry and Egg Product Inspection Directory (https://www.fsis.usda.gov/inspection/establishments/meat-poultry-and-egg-product-inspection-directory) — weekly CSV keyed by establishment number, plus an Establishment Demographic Data CSV (verified current as of July 20, 2026); FSIS recalls and public-health alerts reference the same EST numbers, and FSIS also publishes noncompliance/enforcement quarterly reports. Tier: STEEL. Bridges: plant owner names → parent packers (JBS, Tyson, etc.) → CIK; plants as worksites → OSHA ITA injury data (EIN side) via name/address; USDA purchase contracts → UEI. Ripple question: 'Which plants supplying federal food purchases (school lunch, military) have recall or humane-handling enforcement histories — and do the same corporate parents own the worst OSHA injury numbers?'

*Evidence:* WebSearch confirmed the FSIS MPI Directory page with weekly-updated CSV downloads by establishment number and the Establishment Demographic Data CSV dated July 20, 2026, plus data.gov catalog entries.

*Datasets:* https://www.fsis.usda.gov/inspection/establishments/meat-poultry-and-egg-product-inspection-directory; https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/fsis-meat-poultry-and-egg-inspection-directory-by-establishment-number

**APHIS Certificate Number — animal welfare licensees (new domain: labs, breeders, exhibitors)**

USDA APHIS certificate number (format ##-A-####: state code, license class, serial) for every Animal Welfare Act licensee/registrant — commercial dog breeders, dealers, exhibitors (zoos, circuses), airlines, and every animal research facility in the country. Flagship: USDA Animal Care Public Search Tool (https://aphis.usda.gov/animal-care/awa-services/usda-animal-care-public-search-tool; tool itself at https://aphis.my.site.com/PublicSearchTool/s/) — licensee/registrant rosters with certificate + customer numbers, inspection reports with citations, and research-facility annual animal-use reports. Access: public search/export; bulk is scrape-or-FOIA. Tier: STEEL. Bridges: research facilities are universities/pharma → name-match to UEI (NIH grants in USAspending), EIN (990s), CIK; this is the pharma/academia accountability angle. Ripple question: 'Which research facilities with repeat AWA citations are drawing the biggest NIH awards — violations on one federal ledger, funding on another?'

*Evidence:* WebSearch confirmed the Public Search Tool provides licensee/registrant certificate and customer numbers, inspection reports, and research facility annual reports, with the tool live at aphis.my.site.com.

*Datasets:* https://www.aphis.usda.gov/animal-care/awa-services/usda-animal-care-public-search-tool; https://aphis.my.site.com/PublicSearchTool/s/

**NRC Docket / License Number — nuclear (new domain)**

NRC docket numbers (05000### for power reactors) and materials license numbers identify every nuclear reactor and radioactive-materials licensee (hospitals, industrial radiography, universities). Flagship: NRC Datasets (https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/datasets/index, also nrc.gov/data, CC0-licensed, mirrored on data.gov) — commercial reactor demographics (docket, licensee, location, type), research/test reactors, and materials licensing actions (applicant, license + docket number, action type). Enforcement actions and event reports key to the same dockets. Tier: STEEL. Bridges: licensees are utilities → CIK (public), UEI (federal work), and the EIA Plant/ORIS candidate Ripple already lists — reactor sites are power plants with ORIS codes, so nuclear joins the grid data cleanly. Ripple question: 'Track enforcement/event history per docket against the licensee's financial condition (CIK) — aging plants, cost-cutting owners, rising event counts.' nrc.gov 403-blocked direct fetch; confirmed via search + data.gov.

*Evidence:* WebSearch confirmed NRC data pages and data.gov catalog entries: reactor demographic datasets carrying docket + licensee, research/test reactor lists, and materials licensing action lists carrying license and docket numbers, CC0 licensed.

*Datasets:* https://www.nrc.gov/data; https://catalog.data.gov/organization/nrc-gov

**NID ID — dams (new domain: infrastructure hazard)**

Unique National Inventory of Dams identifier for 91,000+ US dams, maintained by the Army Corps. Flagship: NID portal (https://nid.sec.usace.army.mil/) with full-inventory download; also USACE geospatial open data (https://geospatial-usace.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/1632cb2bb23046569fbf2bc144f06764). 70+ fields per dam: owner name/type, hazard potential (high = expected loss of life on failure), condition assessment, last inspection, EAP status. Free CSV/geospatial. Tier: STEEL as an asset ID; owner attribution is a name field → PROBABILISTIC to EIN/UEI/municipal entities. Bridges: lat/long + county → GEO join to Ripple's county vulnerability marts; FEMA High Hazard Potential Dam grant program → USAspending UEI. Ripple question: 'High-hazard + poor-condition dams upstream of the counties Ripple already scores as most vulnerable — who owns them, and has the owner taken federal rehab money without fixing anything?'

*Evidence:* WebFetch confirmed nid.sec.usace.army.mil resolves (JS app, title confirmed). WebSearch confirmed 91,000+ dams, 70+ fields including hazard potential and condition, USACE geospatial download portal, and the 2021 NID data dictionary PDF.

*Datasets:* https://nid.sec.usace.army.mil/; https://geospatial-usace.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/1632cb2bb23046569fbf2bc144f06764

**OPEID — higher education accountability (new domain)**

Office of Postsecondary Education ID, the Dept of Education's key for every institution participating in federal student aid. Flagship: College Scorecard data (https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/data/) — full ZIP (470 MB) of institution-level files 1996–2026 INCLUDING an OPEID↔IPEDS-UNITID crosswalk (2000–2023, verified). Federal Student Aid datasets (heightened cash monitoring list, closed-school list, borrower-defense discharges) key on OPEID. Tier: STEEL. Bridges: UNITID → NCES (already tagger-known to Ripple, so the crosswalk activates it); private colleges → EIN via IRS 990/BMF (name match, strong for nonprofits); federal grants/contracts → UEI. Ripple question: 'Schools on heightened cash monitoring still drawing hundreds of millions in Title IV aid while their 990s show executive pay climbing — the aid-cliff pattern, keyed hard end to end.'

*Evidence:* WebFetch of collegescorecard.ed.gov/data confirmed the download packages and explicitly the crosswalk files linking OPEID with IPEDS UNITID for each institution, 2000-01 through 2022-23.

*Datasets:* https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/data/

**CRD Number — brokers and investment advisers (new domain: retail finance)**

FINRA Central Registration Depository number, unique per securities firm AND per individual broker/adviser — the finance industry's NPI. Flagship: SEC Form ADV bulk data (https://www.sec.gov/foia-services/frequently-requested-documents/form-adv-data) — complete registered-adviser compilation, historical data in CSV; IAPD (https://adviserinfo.sec.gov/) and FINRA BrokerCheck for individuals including disciplinary history. Tier: STEEL. Bridges: Form ADV filings can be cross-referenced by CIK and LEI — both keys Ripple ALREADY HOLDS (EDGAR, GLEIF) — making this one of the cleanest hard-bridge candidates in the sweep. Ripple question: 'Barred or sanctioned brokers resurfacing at new firms or as state-registered advisers — the finance version of the banned-provider-still-billing story that is Ripple's founding lens, applied to people's retirement money.'

*Evidence:* WebSearch confirmed the SEC FOIA Form ADV data page (historical CSV + current data via IAPD), CRD as the unique firm/rep ID, and that ADV records cross-reference CRD, CIK, and LEI.

*Datasets:* https://www.sec.gov/foia-services/frequently-requested-documents/form-adv-data; https://adviserinfo.sec.gov/

## What the warehouse itself suggests

**PERMIT_NUMBER family - huge and real, but strictly jurisdiction-scoped**

Building/activity permit numbers (PERMIT_NUMBER, PERMIT_NO, PERMITNUMBER, PERMITNUM, PERMITNO, PERMIT_ID) are the second-largest family after parcels. Within a city the same permit number joins permit issuance to inspections and to the assessor's permit feed (Cook County publishes 'Assessor - Permits' keyed the same way). Value: demolition/eviction/renovation-pressure stories. Like parcels, useless without a portal/city namespace, and permit types are heterogeneous (building, parking, tents, moving trucks), so the key needs the dataset context attached.

*Evidence:* Family aggregate: 790 datasets on 65 portals (PERMIT_NUMBER 211/35, PERMIT_NO 151/16, PERMITNUMBER 119/21, PERMITNUM 99/16, PERMIT_ID 63/16). LANDING already has PERMIT_NUMBER in 6 tables (Virginia, WPRDC/Allegheny) and PERMIT_ID in 6.

*Datasets:* Assessor - Permits (Cook County); Micro-Market Recovery Program - Permits (Chicago); Moving Truck Permits (Analyze Boston)

**FEMA flood-map IDs (DFIRM_ID / FLD_AR_ID) - cross-portal but single-origin; plus procurement IDs worth a later look**

Two second-tier observations. (1) FEMA NFHL identifiers appear on 30 portals (261 datasets) because cities republish FEMA flood layers; the ID is nationally standard but the 'join' mostly reconnects copies of the same federal source - better used as a provenance/dedupe key and as the hook to overlay flood risk on parcel-level harm stories. (2) A procurement family (CONTRACT_NUMBER 99 ds / 18 portals, VENDOR_ID 54 / 8) joins contracts to payments to vendor registries within a government (Chicago 'Payments' + 'List of Contractors Doing Business with the City'); jurisdiction-scoped, but it is the follow-the-money join on the spending side and pairs with FILER_ID on the donation side.

*Evidence:* FEMA family: 261 datasets / 30 portals (DFIRM_ID 228/23, FLD_AR_ID 115/27); samples are all FEMA flood products from different cities. CONTRACT_NUMBER samples: Chicago Payments, Cook County Bid Tabulations, CT Open Expenditures ledger; VENDOR_ID samples: Chicago contractor list, CT Checkbook, TX Vendor List.

*Datasets:* FEMA Effective Floodplain (Harris County); Preliminary Flood Hazard Zones (Fairfax County); Payments (Chicago) + List of Contractors Doing Business with the City Of Chicago (CONTRACT_NUMBER/VENDOR_ID pair)

**990 Schedule I / Schedule R: filings citing other organizations' EINs as a money-flow graph**

MECHANISM: A 990's Schedule I lists grants with recipient EINs and Schedule R lists related organizations with their EINs — one filing citing another registry's number, the purest document-citation join available in Ripple's EIN world. Build a directed grant-flow graph over the BMF universe and intersect it with IRS revocations. WHO GETS HURT: donors and intended beneficiaries when money flows to revoked, sham, or circular-granting entities; this is the machine-readable version of dark-money tracing. TIER: the EIN citations are STEEL once parsed; the 'suspicious flow' inference is PROBABILISTIC and needs officer-overlap (finding 8) as corroboration. WHY data_driven_candidate: this mechanism is blocked today by the flagged stale 990 load (~200 rows) — it requires the full IRS 990 e-file XML corpus, and it is the strongest single argument for prioritizing that re-load.

*Evidence:* Every published dark-money network map (Politico/CRC on Arabella-Sixteen Thirty, ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer-based reporting) is assembled from these grant schedules; the IRS publishes the complete 990 e-file corpus as XML with Schedules I and R intact, so the citation edges are directly parseable.

*Datasets:* IRS 990 e-file XML (full corpus, re-load needed); IRS BMF; IRS revocations

**FFIEC NIC bulk file is a free RSSD↔FDIC CERT↔OCC↔LEI crosswalk — it welds the entire banking domain onto the already-wired LEI spine**

One free download solves the banking bridge problem before it exists. The NIC attributes table carries RSSD, FDIC CERT, OCC ID, and LEI on the same row per institution. Since LEI is already wired (GLEIF registry + CFPB HMDA), ingesting NIC instantly connects HMDA lending patterns to Fed structure data, FDIC enforcement, and call reports with zero probabilistic matching. This upgrades RSSD from 'unconfirmed candidate' to a near-free, high-confidence add — the cheapest big bridge on the board.

*Evidence:* FFIEC NPW bulk data download dictionary (ffiec.gov/npw/StaticData/DataDownload/NPW Data Dictionary.pdf) documents the attributes table with ID_RSSD, ID_FDIC_CERT, ID_OCC, and LEI fields; NIC institution profiles display LEI as a searchable identifier. HMDA post-2018 is LEI-keyed (ffiec.cfpb.gov identifiers FAQ).

*Datasets:* FFIEC NIC attributes/relationships bulk download; FFIEC Call Reports; CFPB HMDA (already wired)

**CLIA is a confirmed cheap add — free CMS bulk files, plus its own built-in sanctions list**

CLIA graduates from 'unconfirmed candidate' to verified: CMS publishes the Provider of Services File — Clinical Laboratories as a free bulk file/API on data.cms.gov keyed by CLIA number with name, address, certificate type, and the CMS Certification Number field, and QCOR publishes a weekly-updated certificate registry. CMS also publishes the annual Laboratory Registry of sanctioned labs — meaning this key arrives with its own ban-list analog (labs sanctioned, certificates revoked) in the same ecosystem as the wired CCN tables. Same shape as LEIE-vs-NPI: is the sanctioned lab's operation continuing nearby under a fresh certificate?

*Evidence:* data.cms.gov hosts 'Provider of Services File - Clinical Laboratories' (CSV/JSON API); qcor.cms.gov provides the CLIA lab lookup updated weekly; cms.gov Laboratory Registry page lists labs sanctioned under CLIA. All verified live this session.

*Datasets:* POS File - Clinical Laboratories; QCOR CLIA registry; CMS Laboratory Registry (sanctions)

**CAGE↔UEI crosswalk is already inside the SAM public extract — CAGE is free, not a hunt**

The SAM Entity Management public monthly extract (SAM_PUBLIC_V2_MONTHLY) carries the CAGE code on the same row as the UEI. Since SAM data is already in Ripple's wired UEI stack, the CAGE↔UEI bridge may already be sitting in ingested files — it's a column, not a project. What CAGE then buys: defense logistics datasets (DLA solicitations/awards, DIBBS) and NATO supply-chain records that key on CAGE rather than UEI.

*Evidence:* GSA's published SAM Entity Management Public V2 Extract Layout (open.gsa.gov/api/sam-entity-extracts-api) documents CAGE Code as a field in the monthly public extract alongside UEI. Verified this session.

*Datasets:* SAM public entity extract (wired ecosystem); DLA DIBBS; FPDS historical records

**GLEIF publishes free ISIN↔LEI and BIC↔LEI mapping files — securities issuer linkage arrives via the wired LEI key, no CUSIP license needed**

GLEIF (already wired for LEI) also publishes open daily ISIN-to-LEI relationship files and BIC-to-LEI files. That means security-to-issuer linkage — the thing Ripple would want CUSIP for — is partially available today through a key already on the spine, at zero cost and zero licensing exposure. Combined with the FIGI finding, this further downgrades the case for hunting CUSIP/ISIN as standalone keys: the open stack (LEI + ISIN-LEI file + OpenFIGI) covers most issuer-accountability joins.

*Evidence:* GLEIF hosts free daily ISIN-to-LEI relationship file downloads (gleif.org/en/lei-data/lei-mapping/download-isin-to-lei-relationship-files), a GLEIF-ANNA cooperation running since 2019, plus BIC-to-LEI and OpenCorporates-to-LEI mappings. Verified this session.

*Datasets:* GLEIF ISIN-LEI relationship files; GLEIF golden copy (wired); N-PORT holdings (LEI-bearing)

**State medical-board license numbers — and they are ALREADY sitting inside landed NPPES**

IDENTIFIES: physician/PA licensure per state (composite key: state + license number). The national roll-up (FSMB Physician Data Center, ~1M physicians incl. NPI and DEA crosswalks) is PAID licensing — https://www.fsmb.org/PDC/ ; free per-person lookup at docinfo.org. But the cheap move: NPPES core file (already in Ripple) carries Provider License Number + license state fields per NPI. TIER: STEEL within a state. UNLOCKS: join landed NPPES license numbers to state medical-board disciplinary downloads (many boards publish action lists) → 'disciplined in state A, still billing Medicare from state B' — a second ban-evasion lens that LEIE alone misses, since most board discipline never reaches LEIE. BRIDGE: NPI (landed) → license number → state discipline files. Zero new spine work; the key is already in-house, unindexed.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: FSMB PDC data files page confirms paid data licensing with NPI/DEA identifiers and monthly-or-faster board feeds; DocInfo confirmed as the free single-lookup front end. NPPES license-number fields are standard NPPES layout (confirm column presence in Ripple's landed staging table before building).

*Datasets:* FSMB Physician Data Center (paid): https://www.fsmb.org/PDC/; DocInfo free lookup: https://www.docinfo.org; State board action lists (per-state downloads)

**OFAC SDN crypto wallet addresses — a STEEL key already inside a landed table**

WHAT: SDN entries (ALREADY LANDED in Ripple) routinely include 'Digital Currency Address - XBT/ETH/...' fields — globally unique wallet addresses, up to 256 chars, per sanctioned entity. This is a STEEL identifier sitting unextracted in an existing source: parse the SDN advanced/alt files and index wallet addresses as first-class connection keys alongside IMO. UNLOCKS: 'which sanctioned wallets touched which exchanges/services' — though exploiting it fully needs blockchain flow data (Chainalysis-style, mostly commercial; some free attribution sets exist). Even without chain data, the extracted addresses cross-match leak datasets, court forfeiture filings, and public attribution lists. COST: near zero — it is a parser change on data Ripple already ingests.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: OFAC FAQs 562/563 confirm the 'Digital Currency Address - [symbol]' field structure on the SDN List and routine publication of wallet addresses in SDN entries; Ripple's OFAC SDN ship table is listed as landed in current state.

*Datasets:* OFAC SDN advanced files (already ingested): https://ofac.treasury.gov/specially-designated-nationals-and-blocked-persons-list-sdn-human-readable-lists

**Federal Audit Clearinghouse — single audits keyed by UEI/EIN, lands directly on two existing spines [extra angle 5]**

WHAT: every nonfederal entity spending $750k+/yr in federal money must file a single audit — findings, questioned costs, going-concern flags, auditor identity — and the records are keyed by UEI (and EIN historically). FLAGSHIP: https://www.fac.gov/ — free API, NO registration, plus CSV downloads; historical pre-2023 data at Census. TIER: STEEL, because it arrives already keyed to Ripple's landed UEI and EIN spines — no crosswalk needed. UNLOCKS: 'which grantees with repeated material weaknesses and questioned costs keep winning awards (USAspending, landed)?' — plus auditor-level patterns (the same small audit firm blessing many troubled grantees). Likely the highest ratio of story value to engineering cost in this entire sweep: one ingest, two existing keys, immediate joins.

*Evidence:* Verified via web search this session: fac.gov confirmed as GSA's FAC portal with free no-registration API and CSV access; UEI collection confirmed; $750k threshold and Census-hosted historical data confirmed.

*Datasets:* FAC: https://www.fac.gov/; FAC data docs: https://www.fac.gov/data/

**Cross-cutting: the landed GLEIF table already contains local company-registry numbers — mine it before buying anything**

The LEI-CDF schema in the landed GLEIF registry carries, per entity, the Registration Authority (RA code = which national/state registry) plus the entity's ID IN that registry — i.e., Companies House numbers, state SoS numbers, and foreign registry numbers are already sitting in a table Ripple ingested. Extracting RA + local-ID into the entity index yields a free multi-registry crosswalk for every LEI holder before any new source is onboarded. Same pattern as the NPPES-license-number and SDN-crypto-wallet findings above: three cases in this sweep where the 'new key' is already inside a landed table, unindexed. Suggested first move of the whole sweep: parser passes over GLEIF, NPPES, and SDN before any new ingestion — then FAC, FARA, and LDA as the first three new sources (all free, bulk, daily-fresh, and keyed or near-keyed to landed spines).

*Evidence:* GLEIF LEI-CDF Level-1 schema includes RegistrationAuthority (RegistrationAuthorityID + RegistrationAuthorityEntityID) per LEI record — standard schema, but verify the columns survived Ripple's staging before building. NPPES license fields and SDN digital-currency fields verified as described in their own findings this session.

*Datasets:* GLEIF LEI-CDF format docs: https://www.gleif.org/en/about-lei/common-data-file-format

**NCT number is already sitting in Ripple's warehouse on BOTH sides of a join — wire it now**

ClinicalTrials.gov NCT number (NCT########) uniquely identifies a registered clinical trial. Ripple already has a fed_clinicaltrials staging table, and — the key discovery — the CMS Open Payments RESEARCH payment file (also already wired, 3 years held) carries a ClinicalTrials.gov identifier field (clinicalTrialId, plus principal investigator NPI). That means NCT is a zero-acquisition STEEL key: research payments → NCT → trial sponsor/PI/status, and PI NPI → the whole NPI spine. Data dictionary: https://www.cms.gov/files/document/open-payments-methodology-data-dictionary-document-january-2026.pdf (Appendix C, Research Payments Detail). ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 for enrichment. Tier: STEEL. Ripple question: 'Which doctors were paid research money tied to trials they ran — and did the same doctors get general (meals/speaking) payments from the same sponsor while prescribing its drug?' Also: trials terminated or never-reported whose sponsors kept paying investigators.

*Evidence:* WebSearch confirmed the CMS Open Payments methodology/data dictionary (Jan 2026 edition) documents research-payment fields including clinicalTrialId in NCT format and principalInvestigatorNpi. Ripple state notes fed_clinicaltrials staging table already exists.

*Datasets:* https://www.cms.gov/files/document/open-payments-methodology-data-dictionary-document-january-2026.pdf; https://clinicaltrials.gov/

**OSHA ITA establishment data carries EIN — a direct hard bridge into Ripple's EIN spine**

OSHA's Injury Tracking Application (ITA) publishes establishment-level injury/illness data (Form 300A summaries + Form 300/301 case detail since 2024) at https://www.osha.gov/Establishment-Specific-Injury-and-Illness-Data (CSV, free). OSHA's final rule requires employers to submit their EIN with the data — so workplace injury rates join to IRS BMF, Form 5500, and IRS 990 on a hard key, no name-matching. Separately, OSHA enforcement (inspections/violations/accidents, keyed by inspection activity number) downloads as CSV from the DOL enforcement portal (https://enforcedata.dol.gov/, migrating to https://data.dol.gov/ and dataportal.dol.gov API), updated daily. Tier: EIN bridge = STEEL; inspection activity number = STEEL per-event ID; enforcement-to-establishment matching without EIN is name/address PROBABILISTIC. Ripple question: 'Which employers have the worst injury rates in their industry while their Form 5500 shows they cut the safety/benefits spend — and which of them hold federal contracts (EIN→name→UEI)?'

*Evidence:* WebSearch confirmed OSHA ITA download page, the two-CSV structure (summary + case detail linked by establishment_id), and the EIN submission requirement in OSHA's electronic recordkeeping rule. WebSearch confirmed DOL enforcement CSVs (OSHA daily updates) and the DOL Open Data Portal API.

*Datasets:* https://www.osha.gov/Establishment-Specific-Injury-and-Illness-Data; https://enforcedata.dol.gov/; https://data.dol.gov/

**TRI Facility ID — toxic releases, with a DUNS parent-company bridge in the file**

EPA Toxics Release Inventory facility ID (TRIFID) for every facility reporting toxic chemical releases. Flagship: TRI Basic Data Files (https://www.epa.gov/toxics-release-inventory-tri-program/tri-basic-data-files-calendar-years-1987-present) — CSV, 100 most-used fields, 1987–present, free; Basic Plus for everything. The payoff: the file carries the PARENT COMPANY name AND the parent's Dun & Bradstreet (DUNS) number — DUNS is tagger-known to Ripple, and TRI also joins the EPA family via FRS. So this is a data-driven candidate: corporate-parent attribution ships inside the file. Tier: STEEL (facility), parent DUNS = STEEL corporate bridge. Ripple question: 'Roll releases up to parent companies via DUNS and rank: which parents put the most toxics into which counties — then cross with the county health marts Ripple already built.'

*Evidence:* WebSearch confirmed TRI Basic Data file format documentation includes the parent company's Dun & Bradstreet number as a reported field, and the EPA download pages for Basic and Basic Plus files 1987-present. ECHO fetch confirmed FRS linkage covers TRI.

*Datasets:* https://www.epa.gov/toxics-release-inventory-tri-program/tri-basic-data-files-calendar-years-1987-present; https://echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads

## Other findings

**MMSI status is wrong twice: a wired table already carries it, and it is not STEEL-grade identity**

MMSI is listed 'tagger-known, no table,' but the wired NOAA AIS data is keyed primarily by MMSI — AIS position reports broadcast MMSI, not IMO. So the table exists today. Second error: MMSI cannot be STEEL. It changes when a ship reflags (new flag state assigns a new MMSI), changes with transponder swaps, and is routinely spoofed or duplicated — it is a session identifier, not a hull identity. IMO number is the permanent key. Bonus: AIS static/voyage messages carry IMO alongside MMSI, so Ripple's own AIS table already contains the IMO↔MMSI crosswalk, observed in the wild — which is exactly what a sanctions-evasion hunt needs (a hull whose MMSI keeps changing is itself a red flag).

*Evidence:* AIS message structure: position reports carry MMSI; IMO appears only in static/voyage data (searoutes and maritime-tracking documentation). MMSI reassignment on reflag and IMO permanence hull-to-scrapping are standard maritime practice (Wikipedia MMSI article; multiple vessel-tracking industry sources: 'a specific vessel might appear with a unique IMO number linked to several MMSI numbers').

*Datasets:* NOAA AIS (wired — MMSI-keyed); OFAC SDN vessel entries (IMO, sometimes MMSI)

**TAIL_NUMBER and ICAO24 are both reassignable — the permanent aircraft key is the serial number the FAA registry already carries**

Planned keys TAIL_NUMBER and ICAO24 are treated as if either is stable identity. Neither is: N-numbers are surrendered and reassigned to different airframes over time, and the ICAO24 Mode S hex code is derived from the current registration, so it changes whenever the aircraft re-registers (including moving to a foreign registry — a standard move in opaque-ownership aviation). The FAA registry MASTER file carries manufacturer serial number alongside N-number and Mode S code; MSN+make is the IMO-number equivalent for airframes. Tier tail/ICAO24 as STRONG session keys and anchor identity on serial number, or a hunted aircraft vanishes from the map the day it reflags — which is precisely when it gets interesting.

*Evidence:* FAA aircraft registry releasable database documents N-number reassignment and includes MODE S CODE HEX and serial number fields per record; US Mode S addresses are allocated as a function of the current US registration, changing on re-registration — the same logic verified for ships (MMSI vs IMO) applies.

*Datasets:* FAA aircraft registry (releasable database); OpenSky-style ADS-B archives

**Near-misses flagged but NOT verified this session — TTB permits, NMLS**

Two regulated-industry IDs belong on the watch list but did not get URL verification this session, so per the no-assumed-facts rule they are flagged, not reported: (1) TTB permit numbers (breweries/distilleries/wineries/importers) — TTB is believed to publish permittee lists in its FOIA reading room, unverified; (2) NMLS ID (mortgage companies and individual loan originators) — NMLS Consumer Access is search-only and bulk public data availability is doubtful, though state enforcement actions key on it and it would complement the HMDA/LEI lane Ripple already holds. Also note: three fetch-blocked agencies (atf.gov, dot.gov family, nrc.gov all 403 bot-blocked) will need browser-agent or mirror-based acquisition — plan for that in the loader, it is a pattern, not a one-off.

*Evidence:* ATF, railroads.dot.gov, phmsa.dot.gov, and nrc.gov all returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch this session while their datasets were independently confirmed via search index and data.gov mirrors. TTB and NMLS dataset URLs were not verified at all.

# Part 1b — Checked against the warehouse by hand

*Everything above came from agents. Everything in this section I ran as SQL against Snowflake myself and read the numbers. These are facts, not claims.*

**A key column existing is not the same as a key column working.** Two of the most attractive "free win" findings above turned out to be exactly this trap, and one of them is a bridge someone would otherwise have spent a build cycle on.

### ✅ Confirmed real

| Claim | Verdict | The numbers |
|---|---|---|
| State medical-license numbers are already inside landed NPPES | **TRUE** | `FED_CMS_NPPES` carries `PROVIDER_LICENSE_NUMBER_1..15` plus a matching `..._STATE_CODE_1..15`. The state-board key is already in the building. |
| MMSI is already in a landed table | **TRUE** | `FED_NOAA_AIS.MMSI` exists. The master map lists MMSI as "known, no table anywhere" — that is wrong. |
| Clinical-trial IDs are landed | **PARTLY** | `FED_CLINICALTRIALS.NCT_ID` exists, so one side of the join is real. I could not find a second landed table carrying NCT by column name, so "both sides of a join" is unproven. |
| An FCC table is already landed | **TRUE, and bigger than the map says** | `FED_FCC_LICENSING`: **1,689,338 rows, 1,198,926 distinct FRNs**. FCC_FRN is not a "new candidate we've never touched" — it is landed and unwired. |
| `FED_IRS_990` is a stale/partial load | **TRUE** | Exactly **200 rows, 200 distinct EINs**, against a real universe in the hundreds of thousands. "Exactly 200" looks like a test load that was never replaced. The open flag is real. |

### ❌ Traps — columns that look like bridges and are not

| Trap | What it looks like | What it actually is |
|---|---|---|
| `FED_FCC_LICENSING.EIN` | An EIN column, **100% populated** across 1.69M rows — looks like a hard bridge from telecom straight into the wired EIN spine | Every single row is the **empty string**. One distinct value. The FCC redacts it in public ULS files. There is no EIN bridge here — the join has to run on entity name (weak) or call sign. |

This is the same masking pattern already known from NPPES, now confirmed in a second source. Treat *any* newly discovered ID column as unproven until someone counts its distinct values — "not null" is not the test.

**A second trap, same family — same name, different key.** *(Reported by the FCC hunt agent, not SQL-verified here — the datasets are external. Verify before building, but do not ignore.)* In USAC's E-Rate and Rural Health Care data, a column called **`FRN` means "Funding Request Number"** — a per-application number — **not the FCC Registration Number** that identifies the company. Joining the two on the obvious column name produces a silently wrong answer rather than an error. The real FCC Registration Number is present, but under names like `FCC Registration Number` or `Billed Entity FCC Registration Number`.

Together these are the two ways an ID column lies: **it can be empty, or it can be a different key wearing the same name.** Both survive every column-name scan we have.

### 🔎 New suspicion worth one query

`FED_DOL_FORM5500` holds **33,484 rows / 29,069 distinct EINs**. The real Form 5500 universe is far larger (hundreds of thousands of filings). Nobody has flagged this table, but it has the same thin smell as the 990. Not proven stale — worth checking against the source before anyone leans on it.

### ⚠️ Config break found in passing

`library-onboarding/.env` sets `SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE=DBT_WH`, but that warehouse **no longer exists for the `RIPPLE_READER` role** — the only ones visible now are `COMPUTE_WH`, `SERVE_WH`, and a Streamlit warehouse. Any script relying on the configured default currently dies with "No active warehouse selected." I used `COMPUTE_WH` for these read-only checks rather than editing the repo config.

## NPI — National Provider Identifier

*Status in Ripple:* wired (7 tables).

**Already sitting in our scouted index:**

| Ineligible Provider Report | NJ Open Data Center | State exclusion list keyed by NPI - direct 'banned but still billing' lead vs LEIE/Part D |

**Brief critique:** The brief's "HRSA workforce files" pointer is a dud — AHRF/NHSC files are county- and site-level aggregates without NPI; the genuinely rich un-landed vein is the PECOS enrollment family (Revoked, Order & Referring, Public Enrollment, reassignment) plus the NBER crosswalks. Also worth knowing: LEIE's NPI column is mostly blank on older rows, so the "banned but still billing" lens needs the Revoked dataset and state exclusion lists more than the wired LEIE table.

**Brief critique:** The brief's "HRSA workforce files" starting point is a dud for this key: AHRF is county-level and the NPDB public file is de-identified, so neither carries NPI. The brief also undersold the PECOS side, which is where the two bridges Ripple actually needs live: Facility Affiliation + All Owners give the NPI-to-CCN bridge flagged in memory, and Transparency in Coverage MRFs publish NPI-TIN pairs — the NPI-to-EIN crosswalk memory says never existed.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- Hospital/SNF/HHA/Hospice/FQHC/RHC Enrollment files (data.cms.gov) carry NPI and CCN in the same row — a free, current, official NPI-to-CCN bridge that directly fixes the bridge-fuel gap noted in Ripple's memory (CCN side already wired, 8 tables)
- PECOS All Owners files chain NPI -> enrollment ID -> PAC ID -> individual/org owners: an ownership-network mechanism; org-owner names match EDGAR/CIK holdings probabilistically for private-equity roll-up stories
- NBER also publishes an NPI-to-DEA-number crosswalk (from a 2010-2012 NPI-DEA directory, via data.nber.org/npi/) — seed material for the unconfirmed DEA key candidate
- NPPES bulk itself embeds 'Other Provider Identifiers' (state Medicaid IDs, state license numbers) per NPI — Ripple already holds a multi-key crosswalk to state license and state Medicaid keys inside its own wired roster, unparsed
- Payer Transparency-in-Coverage machine-readable files and CMS-mandated MA/Medicaid provider-directory FHIR APIs publish negotiated rates and network membership keyed by NPI — open, no key, but terabyte-scale; a targeted-extract mechanism rather than a landable table
- Transparency in Coverage payer MRFs publish NPI + billing TIN on every negotiated rate - a de facto NPI-to-EIN crosswalk at national scale, connecting the provider spine to Ripple's IRS/DOL EIN holdings (bridge-fuel memory says this crosswalk 'never existed'; it does now, monthly).
- PECOS All Owners files chain NPI/CCN to named individual and organizational owners with associate IDs - name-matchable to SEC EDGAR (CIK) and SAM/UEI holdings to expose private-equity roll-ups behind bad facilities.
- NPPES records (bulk + API) carry state license numbers per taxonomy - a bridge from NPI to state medical-board disciplinary actions, which never carry NPI themselves.
- QHP Machine-Readable PUF links NPI to HIOS issuer/plan IDs - a new key family (HIOS) not in Ripple's candidate list, connecting providers to specific insurance products sold on healthcare.gov.
- QPP Experience PUF exposes practice TIN next to NPI - a second, cleaner NPI-TIN pairing source to seed the NPI-EIN crosswalk.
- DocGraph Hop Teaming turns NPI into a graph edge (shared-patient flows) - lets exclusion/deactivation findings propagate through referral networks instead of stopping at one provider.
- 340B OPAIS daily JSON/Excel reports key covered entities by 340B ID + Medicare Provider Number (CCN) - joins the 340B drug-discount universe to Ripple's CCN facility tables even though NPI presence is unconfirmed (site returned 503 this pass).
