(2) CCN = Texas PUC Certificate of Convenience and Necessity: 2 Tex…

**Brief critique:** The brief undercounts Ripple's own holdings ("wired 8 tables" - the repo has 12+ CCN staging tables including POS and the HPT MRF index) and its starting-point list misses the single richest untouched vein: the PECOS enrollment/ownership family (6 Enrollments + 6 All Owners + 4 CHOW files, all monthly/quarterly, all carrying CCN+NPI+owner identity). Also note the landed POS copy is the retired edition - the file is now published as QIES + iQIES halves and needs a refresh; the ~41 already-scouted state-portal hits were not re-enumerated here since they are already indexed.

**Brief critique:** The brief's starting points were all real, but they frame CCN as a quality-data key when its unique leverage for Ripple is the ownership/enrollment layer: the PECOS All Owners, CHOW, and Enrollments files carry CCN + NPI + Associate ID in single rows, giving a CMS-maintained CCN-to-NPI crosswalk plus an owner-network graph — this partially compensates for the dead NPI-to-EIN bridge noted in memory. Also note the sibling keys riding in these files: PECOS Associate ID (owner-level) and CLIA number (POS CLIA file) deserve tracking, and CCN itself churns on ownership change, so LTCFocus's stable building ID (accpt_id) is needed for longitudinal facility identity.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- PECOS Associate ID: every Enrollments, All Owners, and CHOW file carries an owner-level Associate ID - a de facto new connection key that chains the same individual/organization across nursing homes, hospitals, HHAs, and hospices; it is the ownership-graph key the CCN brief did not anticipate and arguably worth tracking as its own spine key.
- Provider of Services File - Clinical Laboratories (https://data.cms.gov/provider-characteristics/hospitals-and-other-facilities/provider-of-services-file-clinical-laboratories, confirmed, quarterly): same POS system but keyed by CLIA number - a ready-made authoritative registry for the unconfirmed CLIA candidate key.
- Hospital Service Area file doubles as a CCN-to-beneficiary-ZIP flow matrix - a GEO bridge that connects facility-level findings to Ripple's existing county-level justice/health marts (double-burden counties).
- Hospital/SNF Enrollments files carry both CCN and NPI from PECOS - an independent, higher-authority validation of the landed Facility Affiliation NPI-CCN bridge (and a partial answer to the starved bridge-fuel problem, since owner organizations listed there can be name-matched toward IRS BMF/EDGAR entities).
- CMS Hospital Price Transparency enforcement actions (hospitals fined for hiding prices) would pair directly with the landed fed_cms_hpt_mrf table, and the AHRQ Compendium of U.S. Health Systems would roll CCNs up to corporate health systems - both cms.gov and ahrq.gov blocked automated fetch this session (403/empty), so neither is confirmed; verify manually.
- ESRD QIP PY2026 includes NHSN-sourced infection measures (COVID-19 HCP vaccination, bloodstream infection) - a natural on-ramp to CDC NHSN facility data as a future CCN-adjacent source; CDC's data.cdc.gov NHSN files were not covered this session.
- CCN-to-NPI machine bridge: the six Facility Enrollments files (hospital/SNF/HHA/hospice/FQHC/RHC) each carry CCN + NPI + Enrollment ID + PECOS Associate ID per row - one join wires all 8 CCN tables into the NPI spine (LEIE bans, Open Payments, Part D).
- Owner-network graph: All Owners + CHOW Owner Information files list owner orgs/individuals with PECOS Associate IDs; owner org names/addresses probabilistically match Ripple's EIN (IRS BMF) and UEI (SAM exclusions) holdings - 'excluded owner, still owning' lens.
- FISS Attending and Rendering refreshes weekly with facility-number-to-clinician-NPI pairs from live claims - a near-real-time 'banned provider still billing inside a certified facility' detector.
- POS Clinical Laboratories file pairs CMS provider numbers with CLIA certificate data - free seed crosswalk for the CLIA candidate key.
- AHRQ Compendium hospital linkage file maps CCN to health_sys_id (corporate system) - a stepping stone from facility CCNs to system parents matchable against CIK (EDGAR) and EIN holdings for for-profit chain finance stories.
- CCN churn mechanism: CMS reissues CCNs on ownership change, so LTCFocus accpt_id (stable building ID) enables 'same building, new CCN, same harm' longitudinal tracking that raw CMS files cannot.
- Purge insurance: discontinued CMS COVID files (nursing home and hospital facility-level) are archived at ICPSR DataLumos - a resilience mirror pattern worth adopting for other at-risk federal datasets.
- Care Compare state/national averages files (e.g., State US Averages xcdc-v8bm) give ready-made benchmarks so facility-level outliers can be scored without recomputing national baselines.

**Brief critique:** The NTIS pointer is stale: NTIS ended DEA-file distribution 2020-11-17 (classic.ntis.gov no longer resolves) and the successor RDA is free but registrant-only, with the shareable "limited" version stripped of DEA numbers — so there is no legal public current roster for this key, and even the one-off DEA validation lookup now sits behind a registrant login. Net: DEA is a historical/enforcement key (ARCOS 2006-2014, NPPES-era crosswalks, Federal Register revocations), and NPI stays the working spine — the key's unique payoff is ARCOS plus revocation matching, not a live registry.

**Brief critique:** The brief overweights two starters: ARCOS retail summary reports are aggregate PDFs with no DEA numbers (GEO at best), and the NTIS registrant file is dead - discontinued Nov 2020, now DEA-run and restricted to registrants, so the authoritative issuer file is effectively closed to journalists. State PDMP dispensing data is statutorily restricted in essentially every state (public releases are DEA-number-free aggregates), so the practical play is DEA-as-attribute-on-NPI: the NBER crosswalk plus Federal Register revocation events make NPI stay the spine while DEA becomes the opioid-harm event key.

**Flags:**

- **CMS Provider of Services File - Clinical Laboratories (POS…** — data.cms.gov page is a JS app (verified via catalog.data.gov); public domain; mirrored on catalog.data.gov, HealthData.gov, and multiple state portals — treat mirrors as duplicates.

- **CMS QCOR - Enforcement Actions / Terminations reports (CLIA…** — Same 503 bot-block as the lookup; verified indirectly (mission brief's QCOR pointer is correct). Enforcement detail may lag paper actions
- **NPPES Other Provider Identifiers - embedded CLIA numbers (N…** — Self-reported and optional, so coverage is partial and the identifier-type field is messy free text; commercial crosswalks (e.g. npiprofile.com/clia, 403 to automated fetch) are just this data repackaged under ToS — build in-house instead.
- **NIH Genetic Testing Registry (GTR) bulk data** — Lab info is self-submitted to NIH, not independently verified; CLIA field present but voluntary — validate against POS roster.
- **NBER Provider of Services archive - CLIA files** — data.nber.org directory returned 403 to automated fetch (research page confirms public availability); some conveniences are NBER-affiliate oriented.
- **Washington State Health Care Provider Credential Data (Medi…** — Carries state MTS credential numbers, not CLIA numbers — linkage is name/address matching; portal notes privacy caveats on the dataset.
- **New York CLEP Approved Clinical Laboratories (Wadsworth Cen…** — Search-only, PFI-keyed, CLIA numbers not displayed — linkage is name/address; scraping the paginated UI raises ToS questions; no bulk file found.
- **New Jersey CLIS Clinical Laboratory Enforcement Actions** — No CLIA numbers in listings — facility name/date matching only; other states (e.g. Michigan LARA) run similar pages, not exhaustively enumerated here.
- **California CDPH Laboratory Field Services - facility/licens…** — cdph.ca.gov fetch failed on an SSL certificate error — page existence confirmed via search only; verify manually before relying on it.
- **DataLumos (ICPSR) archive - Provider of Services File Clini…** — Direct fetch returned 403 (existence confirmed via multiple search listings); ICPSR download typically wants a free account.
- **John Snow Labs - Provider of Services CLIA (repackaged mirr…** — Free tier is non-commercial share-alike with EULA; commercial tier paid; low priority - prefer CMS/NBER originals
- **CMS QCOR - CLIA Laboratory Lookup (active lab demographics…** — qcor.cms.gov returned 503 to automated fetchers on repeated tries (bot-blocking or outage); existence and content verified via CDC archive notice, Wadsworth CLEP page, and PA DOH page all pointing here; no documented bulk API - scraping ToS should be checked before wiring
- **CMS Provider of Services File - Hospital & Non-Hospital Fac…** — Primary key is CCN, not CLIA; the portal index's CLIA hit here is likely via cross-reference/description fields - verify actual CLIA columns before wiring under this key
- **CMS Provider of Services File - IQIES (HHA, ASC, Hospice)** — Same caveat as the other POS file: CCN-keyed; CLIA presence in columns unverified
- **NY State CLEP Approved Clinical Laboratories directory (Wad…** — Keyed by NY PFI, not CLIA - verified the search results do NOT display CLIA numbers; linking to CLIA spine is name/address matching. Search UI only, no download
- **CAP Accredited Laboratory and Biorepository Directory** — Name search only, no CLIA field or bulk download confirmed; cap.org ToS not reviewed - check before systematic collection. COLA and Joint Commission directories not verified this pass
- **CDC CLIA Laboratory Search (RETIRED)** — Discontinued source - listed only to correct the mission brief
- **Wake County COVID case GEONUM lookups (POSITIVE CASES GEONU…** — Could not verify any CLIA column this pass - recommend de-indexing unless field list proves otherwise. NOT COVERED in this recon: state Medicaid enrolled-provider rosters (some carry CLIA), CA LFS and WA Medical-Test-Site license lookups (verified lookup-only, no bulk file found on their open-data portals), COLA/Joint…
- *Index false positives:* Broad 'laboratory' title search matched 146 rows; ~140 dropped as non-CLIA: (1) Research-article metadata mirrored into the Virginia Open Data Portal (e.g. 'Impact of HIV vaccination on laboratory diagnosis: case reports', 'Preoperative prediction... routine laboratory data', 'Types and frequency of preanalytical mistakes in the first Thai ISO 9002:1994 certified clinical laboratory') - academic…

**Brief critique:** Two brief corrections: the CDC CLIA lookup was retired 2024-01-16 (folded into QCOR), the "monthly" demographics file is now a weekly QCOR lookup/extract plus the quarterly POS file, and QCOR currently exposes no standalone CLIA enforcement-actions report — the annual PDF Laboratory Registry is the real sanction list. Also, the three Wake County GEONUM index hits are false positives (COVID case counts by geography, no CLIA key), and the POS Hospital and IQIES index hits are CCN-keyed files that touch CLIA only via the cross-reference field.

**Brief critique:** Two starting points are stale: the CDC CLIA lookup was retired 2024-01-16 (QCOR is now the only live lookup) and the demographics file is no longer a monthly download - the maintained artifacts are the quarterly POS-CLIA file plus the weekly-refreshed QCOR tool. Also note CLIA is half-redundant with the landed CCN spine (an independent lab's Medicare CCN is its CLIA number), so the key's unique payoff is the ~200K+ waived/non-billing labs, the sanctions trail, and the Wake County index hits look like false positives.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- NPPES Other Provider Identifier columns in the already-landed NPPES table contain self-reported CLIA numbers - an NPI-CLIA crosswalk Ripple can build tonight with zero new downloads, wiring CLIA labs to LEIE, Medicare billing, and Open Payments.
- The POS CLIA file's CROSS_REF_PROVIDER_NUMBER field (positions 48-57 of the POS layout) links CLIA labs to related Medicare provider numbers - a direct structural bridge from CLIA to Ripple's 8 wired CCN facility tables (hospital and nursing-home labs).
- CLIA numbers encode geography for free: first 2 digits are the state code (format ##D#######) - instant state mapping and validation with no lookup table.
- Nursing homes hold CLIA Certificates of Waiver for point-of-care testing - address/name-matching waiver certificates in the POS CLIA file to the landed CMS nursing home table surfaces facilities running patient testing with essentially no routine lab surveys.
- QCOR is not lab-specific: the same public extract machinery serves survey/deficiency/enforcement data for nursing homes, hospices, and other CCN provider types Ripple already holds - one new source feeds many existing keys.
- The annual Laboratory Registry lists fraud and false-billing convictions by name - name-match against the landed LEIE and the staged DOJ FCA settlements table for 'convicted lab operator resurfaces under a new certificate' leads.
- NPPES (already landed) is a hidden NPI-CLIA crosswalk: lab NPIs commonly carry their CLIA/OSCAR certification number in the Other Provider Identifier columns - scan the landed NPPES table for 10-character CLIA-pattern values before building anything new
- CLIA-CCN identity: for independent labs the Medicare CCN IS the CLIA number, so CLIA records join directly to Ripple's existing CCN facility spine with zero new bridge work for that segment
- Flagship pipeline stumbled into shape: QCOR/registry sanctions (CLIA) + NPPES other-identifier crosswalk (CLIA to NPI) + landed Medicare utilization (NPI) = 'is the lab sanctioned for botched tests still billing Medicare' - every link uses tables Ripple already holds plus one new file
- NBER mirrors the FDA CLIA test-categorization database (test complexity by device, 2000-present): pairs with certificate type in POS-CLIA to flag waived-certificate labs whose test menus imply complexity beyond what their certificate allows

**Flags:**

- **SAM.gov Entity Management Public Extract (entity registrati…** — Requires a SAM.gov account + API key even for the public extract (rate limits 10-10,000 req/day by account type). EIN/TIN is in the 'Sensitive' CUI tier only - the public file will NOT give you UEI-to-EIN.
- **Federal Audit Clearinghouse (FAC) Single Audit data** — API needs a free api.data.gov key; bulk CSVs are open. Confirmed auditee_uei plus additional_ueis/additional_eins tables in the data dictionary (fac.gov/api/dictionary).
- **Federal subaward data (FSRS successor - SAM.gov subaward re…** — FSRS.gov retired March 2025 - cite SAM.gov, not FSRS. SAM page confirms public subaward/subcontract APIs exist but I could not confirm on-page whether the API needs a SAM API key; USAspending bulk path is fully open.
- **USAspending.gov prime awards (contracts + financial assista…** — usaspending.gov UI pages are a JS app (fetch-empty); use API/bulk endpoints.
- **NIH ExPORTER / RePORTER project files** — Old exporter.nih.gov domain is dead (DNS fails) - use reporter.nih.gov/exporter. UEI only reliable from ~FY2022 onward; carries both DUNS and UEI (crosswalk).
- **Treasury SLFRF (State & Local Fiscal Recovery Funds) public…** — home.treasury.gov timed out on 3 fetch attempts during verification - page existence and content confirmed only via search index and Treasury's PE Report User Guide PDFs; verify UEI columns in the downloaded file before wiring.
- **OpenFEMA HMA Subapplications (Hazard Mitigation Assistance)** — fema.gov HTML doc pages return 403 to non-browser fetchers, but the API endpoint itself is open and was verified live returning applicantUei/subapplicantUei. Check other OpenFEMA datasets for UEI adoption over time.
- **SAM.gov Responsibility/Qualification records (formerly FAPI…** — Viewing is public/no role, but Data Bank report generation requires a SAM.gov sign-in; no confirmed standalone bulk extract - pull via Entity Management API integrity section.
- **SBIR.gov award and company data (SBIR/STTR)** — Web download pages cap at 10,000 records per pull; full files available but API returns fewer fields than downloads. Carries DUNS+UEI side by side (free crosswalk).
- **NSF Award Search downloads + Awards API** — nsf.gov download page is JS-rendered and returned empty to fetch; existence + UEI fields verified via the official API documentation. Download format switched XML to JSON in Jan 2025.
- **HHS TAGGS (Tracking Accountability in Government Grants Sys…** — Exports capped at first 25,000 rows per query - bulk acquisition means chunked queries; no documented bulk file or API. Largely overlaps USAspending for amounts.
- **FPDS contract action reports (ATOM feed / SAM.gov Data Bank)** — Being absorbed into SAM.gov: fpds.gov archives already 301-redirect to sam.gov/contracting; ezSearch decommissions Q2 FY2026, ATOM feed later in FY2026. Largely redundant with landed USAspending - low priority.
- **HHS Expiring Contracts List FY23-FY26** — Snapshot data (rows updated Aug 2023) - useful as a fixed-period slice, not a live feed.
- **SAM.gov Contract Opportunities daily CSV** — UEI present only on the award-notice subset. data.gov catalog entry stale (2022) but the underlying SAM.gov service is live.
- **SBA Small Business Search (certifications.sba.gov, successo…** — Site is a JS app; fetch confirmed only the title 'SBA Small Business Search' - could not confirm on-page UEI display, bulk export, or API. Treat field availability as unverified until inspected in-browser.
- **SNP CE Applications, PY19-PY25 (Texas Dept. of Agriculture)** — Companion TX site-level SNP datasets do not list a UEI column - only this sponsor-level one carries the key.
- **Charter Schools (Mecklenburg County GIS Open Data)** — Portal returned 403 to automated fetch this session - URL is portal-level and the UEI attribute rests on the scouted index, not re-verified today. Verify layer name at land time.
- **SAM.gov Contract Award Data + Contract Awards API (successo…** — FPDS.gov public site was decommissioned 2026-02-24; ATOM feed retires later in FY2026 - build against the new SAM.gov Contract Awards API, not FPDS. User account required for public data access.
- **NIH RePORTER / ExPORTER award files** — UEI only populated for recent years (post-DUNS transition, April 2022); older records carry DUNS. Field names confirmed in ExPORTER data dictionary (report.nih.gov/exporter-data-dictionary).
- **FDP Expanded Clearinghouse organization profiles** — No bulk download - per-profile pages only, so landing it means polite scraping (check site ToS first). Small N but high-quality, self-attested data.
- **SAM.gov Entity Management API (live registration lookup)** — Harsh rate limit for non-federal personal keys (10 requests/day without roles) - fine for spot-checks, useless for bulk; use the extract for bulk.
- **HigherGov (commercial aggregator)** — Paid subscription; data is repackaged public data - build from the primary sources instead. Listed for landscape completeness.
- **SNP CE Applications, PY19-PY25 (Texas Open Data Portal)** — URL given is portal root - exact dataset URL is in Ripple's scouted index; not re-fetched this session. Treat as a sample of a much larger state-portal long tail.
- **Charter Schools (Mecklenburg County GIS Open Data Portal)** — URL is portal root - exact dataset URL is in the scouted index; not re-fetched this session.
- *Index false positives:* The loose '%UEI%' substring search returned 100+ junk columns, all dropped via a word-boundary regex ((^\|[^A-Z])UEI([^A-Z]\|$)). Dropped families: (1) UniqueID/UNIQUEID/uniqueId GIS feature IDs — the overwhelming majority, across Harris County, Open Baltimore, Open Data DC, Raleigh, LA County, Kentucky, Tucson, TN portals; (2) other ID words: ISSUEID, GISHistoryQueueID/QUEUEID; (3) camelCase col…

**Brief critique:** Grants.gov is a dud for this key: its only public bulk product is the daily opportunities XML extract, which carries no applicant/recipient UEI (UEI is visible only inside logged-in applicant profiles). FPDS is near-redundant with already-landed USAspending and is being folded into SAM.gov during FY2026; the genuinely missing piece is the SAM Entity Management extract itself - Ripple has UEI transactions and bans but not the registry roster that says who each UEI is, and that roster also activates the CAGE sibling key for free.

**Brief critique:** Two of the brief's starting points are stale: FPDS's public site was decommissioned 2026-02-24 (ATOM feed dies later in FY2026 - the successor is the SAM.gov Contract Awards API) and FSRS retired March 2025 into SAM.gov. Grants.gov is a dud for this key - its public XML extract is funding-opportunity notices only, no awardee UEIs (verified 2026-07-22); the real grant-side UEI landscape is FAC, agency award files, and USAspending.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- FAC single audits carry auditee_uei AND auditee_ein side by side - a free UEI-to-EIN bridge joining federal-spend holdings to Ripple's IRS 990/BMF/Form 5500 EIN tables, directly easing the starved bridge layer noted in memory (NPI-EIN masked).
- NIH ExPORTER and USAspending download files both carry legacy DUNS next to UEI - a ready-made DUNS-to-UEI crosswalk for wiring any pre-2022 dataset that still keys on DUNS (a tagger-known key with no table).
- The SAM Entity Management public extract carries CAGE code and immediate/ultimate parent UEIs per entity - it activates the CAGE candidate key and hands over corporate family trees (parent-subsidiary rollups) with no extra source.
- SAM entity records carry per-entity NAICS codes - fuel for the tagger-known NAICS key across the whole federal vendor census.
- HHS TAGGS recipient pages cross-reference each grantee's historical EIN, DUNS, and UEI - a second UEI-to-EIN bridge specifically for health grantees.
- USAC's open datahub (E-Rate Service Provider Information, datahub.usac.org/d/xcy2-bdid, verified) does NOT carry UEI values (only a filed-with-UEI yes/no flag) but links SPIN to FCC Registration Number - a sibling registry for the FCC FRN candidate key covering telecom vendors paid from the Universal Service Fund.
- FAC single-audit records carry auditee_ein and an additional_eins table right next to auditee_uei - a free, machine-readable UEI-to-EIN crosswalk at national scale, directly patching the missing EIN bridge noted in Ripple's Bridge Fuel memory (links federal-award world to IRS 990/BMF/5500 holdings).
- SAM Entity Management public extract carries a CAGE code for every registrant - an instant UEI-to-CAGE crosswalk if the CAGE candidate key ever lands (defense-supply-chain lens).
- SAM.gov/FPDS contract data carries immediate, domestic, and ultimate parent UEIs per vendor - free corporate ownership trees, no paid D&B needed; pairs with CIK/LEI holdings for public-company parents.
- USAspending archives and SBIR.gov files carry legacy DUNS and UEI side by side - a free DUNS-to-UEI crosswalk that unlocks every DUNS-keyed legacy dataset (DUNS is tagger-known with no table).
- FDP Expanded Clearinghouse profiles publish UEI+EIN+CAGE+single-audit status per research institution - a small, clean multi-key Rosetta stone connecting the NIH/NSF award world to EIN holdings.
- NIH ExPORTER links UEI-keyed institutions to resulting publications and patents - an unanticipated UEI-to-PATENT bridge (PATENT is tagger-known, no table).

**Flags:**

- **IRS Form 990 Series e-file bulk (XML)** — AWS-hosted mirror was retired (2022) — files now live at apps.irs.gov/pub/epostcard/990/xml; 2021-2022 folders show gaps, so backfill needs the index CSVs checked year by year.
- **IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File (EO BMF) extr…** — State assignment is HQ mailing address, not where the org actually operates.
- **Federal Audit Clearinghouse (FAC) single-audit data** — Download page doesn't enumerate fields — auditee EIN + UEI confirmed via the FAC data dictionary and search filters; API may need an api.data.gov key; Login.gov only for submitters.
- **OSHA Injury Tracking Application (ITA) establishment data** — EIN column only reliably populated for 2023+ data years; earlier years link on establishment_id/name only.
- **IRS 527 Political Organization Filings (Forms 8871/8872, PO…** — EIN field in the download layout not eyeballed this recon (8871/8872 forms require EIN, so presence is near-certain) — confirm in the data-layout file at land time.
- **Transparency in Coverage payer in-network machine-readable…** — No central portal — files sit on each payer's site; raw files run to terabytes, needs targeted extraction, not bulk landing.
- **IRS SOI Annual Extract of Tax-Exempt Organization Financial…** — IRS notes adjustments mean extract values can differ from as-filed returns.
- **SEC EDGAR submissions API (EIN per filer)** — data.sec.gov 403s requests without a declared User-Agent and rate-limits (10 req/s) — confirmed via SEC docs, direct fetch blocked this recon.

(2) 'count_distinct_ein' in Austin APD Sworn Retirements - Austin HR uses EIN as internal Employee ID Number, and it is an aggregate count anyway; note the JOIN_KEYS tagger wrongly tagged this one EIN. (3) The entire employer_id family (10 datasets): Ch…

**Brief critique:** PPP was mis-scoped: the public FOIA release carries no borrower EIN/TIN, so it is a fuzzy-name dataset, not an EIN dataset. The bigger miss is that the highest-value EIN plays are crosswalk fields already sitting inside wired tables — EDGAR's ein field (CIK↔EIN), HCRIS Worksheet S-2 (CCN↔EIN), and FAC (EIN↔UEI) — which upgrade the whole spine faster than any new standalone landing except the overdue 990 e-file refresh.

**Brief critique:** Two starting points were wrong: CMS HCRIS is not an EIN carrier — the official Hospital Provider Cost Report data dictionary keys everything on CCN/rpt_rec_num with no EIN variable (the real hospital-EIN bridge is the price-transparency MRF filename mandate, 45 CFR 180.50(d)(5)); and SBA PPP public data carries no EIN at all, so it is name-match only. Otherwise EIN is exactly as valuable as billed — it is the only key that welds nonprofits, pensions, workplace injuries, single audits, unions, colleges, and (via EDGAR's ein field) public companies into one spine.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- SEC EDGAR submissions API and Financial Statement Data Sets carry an 'ein' field per CIK — a ready-made CIK↔EIN crosswalk already inside wired EDGAR holdings, linking public companies to their pension plans (5500), injury records (OSHA ITA), and audit findings (FAC).
- Transparency in Coverage in-network files pair every provider TIN (type 'ein') with NPI arrays — a national-scale EIN↔NPI crosswalk that substantially solves the NPPES-masked EIN bridge problem noted in the Bridge Fuel memory.
- FAC single-audit records carry both auditee EIN and auditee UEI — a direct EIN↔UEI bridge tying the nonprofit/employer spine to USAspending awards and SAM exclusions.
- HCRIS Worksheet S-2 carries hospital EIN alongside CCN in a table Ripple already wired — facility quality/cost data joins employer, pension, and 990 records with zero new landing.
- 990 XML Schedules R and I list the EINs of related organizations and grantees — the filings are a funding-network edge list (who controls whom, who funds whom), not just entity attributes.
- Form 5500 Schedule C service-provider entries carry vendor EINs — employer-to-vendor edges already inside landed 5500 data.
- TAGGS documents the 2021-2022 recipient migration from EIN to DUNS/UEI with legacy cross-display — a historical crosswalk for stitching pre-2022 HHS grants onto the modern UEI spine.
- SEC EDGAR submissions JSON exposes every filer's EIN — a free CIK↔EIN crosswalk that joins the wired EDGAR/CIK spine to the EIN spine (reported as a dataset row too; the key list treated CIK and EIN as separate islands).
- Federal Audit Clearinghouse records carry auditee EIN AND UEI in the same row — a ready-made EIN↔UEI bridge onto the wired USAspending/SAM spine, no fuzzy matching needed.
- IPEDS HD files carry EIN + UEI + OPEID + UNITID per college — one annual file bridges the tagger-known NCES key and the wired UEI key into the EIN spine.
- DOL Form 5500 Schedule C lists each plan's service providers by the providers' own EINs — network edges from every employer plan to the banks/recordkeepers/consultants paid from worker money (already-landed table, unexploited columns).
- Hospital price-transparency MRF filenames embed the hospital's EIN — links our CCN-keyed CMS facility tables to EIN-keyed 990 finances through the hospital's own required disclosure.
- Transparency in Coverage payer machine-readable files identify employer group health plans with plan_id_type 'EIN' (CMSgov price-transparency-guide schema) — NOT verified this recon, but if confirmed it maps employer EINs to insurer networks and joins straight to Form 5500.
- OSHA ITA's EIN column makes injuries joinable to benefits: same-EIN pairing of injury rates (ITA) with plan behavior (5500) and audit findings (FAC) asks whether the employers hurting workers are the same ones shorting them.

**Brief critique:** The brief's hunch about a public SAM-transition DUNS-to-UEI crosswalk is half wrong: GSA never published a standalone one and actively scrubbed DUNS from current SAM extracts - the real crosswalks are USAspending's own recipient tables, NIH ExPORTER (DUNS+UEI in the same row), and the CC-licensed academic FPDS corpus. The brief also undersold that DUNS is not purely a legacy key - FDA still uses it as the live unique facility ID for every drug establishment - and missed the urgency that FPDS public access is being dismantled through 2026, so the legacy landscape is actively shrinking.

**Brief critique:** The brief's "old NSF award files" pointer is a dud - the current NSF Awards API exposes ueiNumber/parentUeiNumber but no DUNS field, and no DUNS-bearing public NSF bulk file was confirmed. Bigger reframe: DUNS is not purely legacy (FDA still uses it as its live facility identifier, EPA registries still carry it), and its highest value is as the historical alias of the already-landed UEI spine - the requested public DUNS-to-UEI crosswalk does exist, but the working open copy ships inside the Figshare FPDS 1979-2023 dataset, not from GSA, whose official fpds.gov crosswalk was retired and whose SAM extracts purged DUNS in April 2022.

- Data Rescue Project maintains a mirror of the USAspending database (portal.datarescueproject.org) - resilience option given the 2026 FPDS decommissioning wave.

*Sweep note:* True totals: 408 distinct datasets carry NAICS-like columns in PORTAL_DATASET_INDEX (only top 40 returned here); 363 LANDING tables in LIBRARY_RAW carry NAICS columns (10 federal + 353 portal). Tagger comparison: JOIN_KEYS tag 'NAICS' hits 364 datasets - a strict subset of the 408 column-regex hits (0 tag-only, 44 column-only). The tagger systematically misses fused/suffixed column names: naicscode, naicsdescr, BUSNAICSCD, naicscode1..40, naics2/naics6, industrybynaicscode_*. Several tagger misses are high-value: PPP loan datasets in CT/LA/CO/NJ/NYS, Miami-Dade Local Business Tax (192K rows),…

*Landed tables carrying it:* `FED_DHS_HIFLD (NAICS_CODE)`, `FED_DOL_OFLC (NAICS_CODE)`, `FED_EPA_ECHO (FAC_NAICS_CODES, RCRA_NAICS, CWA_NAICS, CAA_NAICS)`, `FED_NAAG_MULTISTATE_SETTLEMENTS (RELATED4DIGITNAICSCODE, RELATED6DIGITNAICSCODE)`, `FED_SBA_LOANS (NAICSCODE, NAICSDESCRIPTION)`, `FED_SBA_PPP (NAICSCODE)`, `FED_USASPENDING_BULK (NAICS_CODE, NAICS_DESCRIPTION)`, `FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS (NAICS_CODE, NAICS_DESCRIPTION)`, `FED_USITC_DATAWEB (NAICS_CODE)`, `FED_US_USASPENDING_API (NAICS_CODE, NAICS_DESCRIPTION)`, `...plus 353 PORTAL_* LANDING tables (ARC/SOC/CKA prefixes) with NAICS columns - largest clusters: Utah Open Data (~100+), Harris County (~40), Atlanta (~33), LA County (~25), Tucson (~19), Orange County (14, all NAICS_ICS), Raleigh (7), plus Socrata state portals CT/CO/TX/NY/DE/OR/PA/MD/SF/DataLA`

What I dropped as low-value rather than false: (1) ~150+ one-off GIS map exhibits derived from ESRI Business Analyst / InfoGroup / Data Axle extracts (grocery-store buffers, therapist points, places of worship, hotels, 'Digital Divide McDonalds', faith-instit…

**Brief critique:** NAICS can never be STEEL — it is a lens/denominator, not a connector, so a NAICS match between two rows is context, never a link between entities; its 364 index hits overstate its connective value. The highest-leverage moves are attaching NAICS to entities Ripple already holds (SAM public extract → every UEI; Form 5500's NAICS-derived business code → every EIN) and treating SIC as the sibling key — EDGAR/CIK filings carry SIC, not NAICS, so NAICS+SIC bridged by the Census concordance should be one workstream, not two keys.

**Brief critique:** NAICS can never be STEEL - it is a dimension, not a connector, and the 364 index hits overstate its linking value: its real payoff is denominators and peer baselines (rates instead of counts) plus industry-tagging entities Ripple already holds. Its necessary sibling is SIC - SEC EDGAR (wired CIK holdings) and pre-2006 TRI/OSHA vintages classify by SIC, so NAICS+SIC with the Census concordance should be built as one industry dimension table, not two keys.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- DOL Form 5500 (already wired via EIN) carries a BUSINESS_CODE field that is NAICS-derived — Ripple already holds an industry code on every 5500 filer; tagging it gives an industry lens on the EIN layer with zero new landing.
- SEC EDGAR (wired via CIK) classifies filers by SIC, not NAICS — the Census NAICS-SIC concordance bridges wired CIK financials into the entire NAICS landscape, making the crosswalk itself the connector.
- SAM.gov Entity Management Public Extract attaches every registrant's claimed NAICS codes (with small-business flags) to UEI — one monthly file industry-tags Ripple's whole USAspending + SAM-exclusions holdings and exposes size-standard gaming (firms claiming small-business status in NAICS codes they don't match).
- EPA ECHO Exporter carries FRS ID + NAICS + lat/lon + compliance history in one file — landing it for NAICS simultaneously seeds the FRS_ID candidate key and a GEO join to county-level marts.
- PPP and 7(a)/504 FOIA files carry borrower name/street address — PROBABILISTIC joins to the state/city business-license registries already scouted (SF, LA, Salt Lake, Atlanta), which can resolve loan recipients to licensed local establishments.
- DOL Form 5500 (EIN, already landed) carries a 6-digit 'business code' that is the IRS NAICS-derived principal business activity code - a NAICS column already sitting inside a wired table, so EIN entities can be industry-tagged with zero new landings
- SEC EDGAR (CIK, wired) classifies filers by SIC, not NAICS - the Census SIC-NAICS concordance is the bridge that pulls the wired CIK financials into the same industry lens
- SAM Entity Management Public Extract maps UEI to NAICS - industry-profiles the already-landed SAM exclusions and USAspending tables (which industries' contractors get debarred most, and who wins awards anyway)
- EPA ECHO Exporter carries FRS ID alongside NAICS - landing it advances the unconfirmed FRS_ID candidate key and the NAICS lens in one pull
- QCEW/CBP as a denominator engine converts every count table in Ripple (exclusions, violations, bans) into per-1,000-workers or per-1,000-establishments rates by industry and county - the difference between trivia and a pattern
- IRS SOI corporate statistics use NAICS-based activity codes, matching the codes on IRS BMF/990 filers - a second industry-tagging path for the EIN spine

**Brief critique:** SIC can never be STEEL anywhere — it is an industry bucket shared by thousands of entities, so it is a grouping/bridge dimension, not an entity link; its real value is historical continuity (pre-1997 federal files) plus the live EDGAR assignment, making it the time-machine sibling of NAICS rather than a standalone key — land the two together with the Census concordance as the hinge. Also, at least one scouted hit (UK data.gov.uk) is UK SIC 2007, a different classification that must not be cross-joined with US SIC.

**Brief critique:** SIC can never be STEEL — it is a shared industry classification, not a unique registry ID, so every match is industry-level context, and its real payoff is as a lens/crosswalk (live CIK→SIC in EDGAR plus the Census concordance to NAICS). Also the tagger conflates codesets: the data.gov.uk hit uses UK SIC 2007 (NACE-aligned, different values), and many city-portal hits are commercial InfoGroup/Data Axle extracts — so raw index-hit count overstates this key versus its sibling NAICS.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- SEC Financial Statement Data Sets sub.txt carries an EIN column alongside SIC — a free CIK↔EIN bridge connecting wired EDGAR tables to wired IRS 990/BMF and DOL Form 5500 tables, directly easing the documented bridge-fuel shortage.
- EPA FRS national CSV carries FRS_ID plus program IDs (NPDES, RCRA, ICIS-Air) for every facility — landing it for SIC simultaneously seeds the FRS_ID and EPA NPDES candidate keys with one download.
- EPA TRI files carry parent-company DUNS numbers — a free seed table for the tagger-known DUNS key that currently has no table.
- MSHA data introduces MINE_ID plus controller/operator history — controller names match probabilistically to SEC coal/mining filers, tying mine injury records to public companies.
- OSHA inspection establishment names/addresses match probabilistically to USAspending (UEI) recipients — enables a 'federal contractor with willful safety violations' mechanism.
- Schott's HS-SIC concordance ties trade flows to industries, letting import-shock exposure join county harm data through the CBP county-industry panel.
- SEC EDGAR submissions JSON carries EIN (and LEI when registered) alongside SIC per filer — a live, free CIK↔EIN bridge to Ripple's wired IRS BMF/990 and DOL Form 5500 tables that the key list did not anticipate (verified: Apple returns ein 942404110)
- EPA FRS single-file CSV is a facility spine carrying FRS_ID (a Ripple new-candidate key) plus SIC, NAICS, and lat/long in one row — one download seeds three keys and joins TRI/NPDES/RCRA/air programs
- ICIS-NPDES NPDES_SICS.csv binds the NPDES candidate key directly to SIC — one table advances two unlanded keys
- MSHA open data carries MSHA Mine ID plus operator/controller names — a federal registry key absent from Ripple's key list, linking mines to violations, accidents, and owning companies
- Schott concordances map SIC to HS product codes, connecting industry harm patterns to trade-flow data (import shocks) — a mechanism no current key reaches
- UK 'SIC' datasets bridge to Companies House company numbers and GLEIF LEI (wired), suggesting a separate UK_SIC key rather than folding them into US SIC

**Brief critique:** The brief's "wired (2 tables)" badly undersells CIK — it is probably the densest free key in the catalog (25+ SEC bulk sets, all open, all keyed CIK, most refreshed daily/quarterly), and EDGAR's own submissions file already carries EIN and LEI, making CIK a free crosswalk hub rather than just a filer ID. One landscape correction: there is essentially no state-level CIK carriage — state securities regulation runs on CRD/IARD numbers, so CRD is the missing sibling key for this domain (the Form ADV bulk data is the free CIK-CRD bridge).

**Brief critique:** Two corrections: (1) there is no official GLEIF CIK-to-LEI file — the real CIK↔LEI bridge is inside SEC's own structured data (N-CEN/N-PORT/ADV rows carry both), so don't budget for a registry crosswalk that doesn't exist; (2) the brief treats CIK as a company key, but Forms 3/4/5 give tens of thousands of individual officers/directors their own CIKs — it doubles as Ripple's first person-level corporate spine, which raises its value estimate. State-level coverage is inherently thin (CIK is federal); NASAA EFD is the only meaningful state-side echo.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- EDGAR submissions API includes each filer's EIN — a free machine-readable CIK-EIN crosswalk straight into wired IRS BMF/990/Form 5500 holdings, no name-matching needed (verified: Apple record carries ein 942404110)
- Submissions API plus N-PORT/N-CEN carry LEI — a CIK-LEI bridge into wired GLEIF and HMDA without any third-party mapping
- 13F info tables and N-PORT holdings carry CUSIP/ISIN — landing either instantly activates the planned CUSIP key, and N-PORT lets you screen US fund portfolios against OFAC-linked issuers
- Form ADV bulk data doubles as a CIK-CRD crosswalk — CRD (FINRA BrokerCheck/IAPD) is a strong new candidate key with its own disciplinary-history datasets
- Insider Forms 3/4/5 assign CIKs to individual people — a person-level spine for board/officer interlocks across companies, joinable by name to Open Payments physician-executives
- Submissions API carries SIC code and state/country of incorporation for every filer — free fuel for the TAGGER-KNOWN SIC key and a GEO attribute
- EDGAR submissions JSON carries an 'ein' field for most corporate filers — a free, authoritative CIK↔EIN crosswalk directly into the wired IRS BMF/990 and DOL 5500 tables, no new dataset needed
- N-CEN and N-PORT structured data carry registrant and service-provider LEIs alongside CIK — an SEC-native CIK↔LEI crosswalk into the wired GLEIF/HMDA tables
- 13F and N-PORT holdings rows carry CUSIP and ISIN — combined with the open cik-cusip-mapping crosswalk and GLEIF's official daily ISIN↔LEI file, this chains CIK→CUSIP/ISIN→LEI and activates two planned/candidate keys at once
- Every EDGAR filer record carries a SIC code — instant activation of the TAGGER-KNOWN SIC key across the whole CIK spine
- Form ADV bulk data bridges CIK↔CRD (FINRA's adviser/broker ID) — CRD is a strong sibling key not on Ripple's list, and it leads to FINRA BrokerCheck's individual disciplinary records
- Insider forms give individual people durable CIKs — name-joinable to Open Payments physicians and (planned) FEC donor/candidate records for person-level conflict mapping
- PCAOB also publishes downloadable firm inspection-findings datasets — joined via Form AP issuer CIKs, that links audit-quality defects to the specific public companies those firms audit

Dropped from title search: agricultural/land 'holdings' (Ireland CSO…

**Brief critique:** The brief treats CUSIP like an entity key, but it identifies a security, not an entity — the entity join is the CUSIP-6 issuer prefix or a crosswalk (ISIN→LEI, 13D/13G→CIK), and unlike NPI/LEI there is no free authoritative registry dump: CGS/FactSet is paid and litigiously licensed, so the usable registry must be assembled from SEC/Treasury/GSE files. Also the separately-listed ISIN candidate key is ~redundant for this domain: US/Canada ISINs literally embed the CUSIP, so landing CUSIP gets ISIN for free.

**Brief critique:** Two corrections: EMMA cannot be a landed table (ToS bars scraping/bulk; bulk is paid) so the real muni feed is state portals + SEC/Fed sources, and the ISIN candidate key is largely redundant for this domain since US ISINs are just "US"+CUSIP+check digit - landing CUSIP gets ISIN for free. Also note the identifier itself is licensed IP (CGS/FactSet, active antitrust litigation), so republishing CUSIP-keyed marts at scale needs a RED-lane legal look even though every source above is public.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- GLEIF ISIN-to-LEI daily file is a free CUSIP-to-LEI crosswalk (US ISIN = 'US' + CUSIP + check digit) — plugs every CUSIP dataset straight into Ripple's already-wired GLEIF LEI spine without touching CGS licensing.
- SEC Schedule 13D/13G cover pages pair each CUSIP with the subject company's CIK — EDGAR full-text search API (verified live) yields a build-your-own CUSIP-to-CIK bridge into the wired EDGAR tables.
- NRSRO 17g-7 rating history files key actions by CUSIP AND obligor CIK — a second CUSIP-to-CIK bridge that also adds a downgrade-timeline lens.
- 13F/N-PORT/N-MFP filers are themselves CIKs — fund-holdings data joins the wired CIK spine on BOTH sides (holder CIK directly, issuer via crosswalk), so CUSIP multiplies the value of tables Ripple already has.
- Agency MBS disclosure files (Ginnie/Fannie/Freddie) connect security CUSIPs down to originating-lender names and loan geography — pairs with wired HMDA/LEI for mortgage-harm stories the key list never anticipated.
- data.ny.gov carries two unscouted siblings of the indexed dataset: New Debt Issuance for Local Authorities (data.ny.gov/d/qbd7-9grw) and for Industrial Development Agencies (data.ny.gov/d/cci8-aavx).
- N-PORT holdings print CUSIP, ISIN and LEI on the same row - a free CUSIP-to-LEI crosswalk straight into the wired GLEIF/LEI spine (and via LEI into CFPB HMDA lenders).
- SEC fails-to-deliver files carry CUSIP + ticker + issuer name, giving a free CUSIP-to-CIK bridge through the wired EDGAR company-tickers table - no paid CUSIP master needed for listed issuers.
- 13F and N-PORT filers are identified by CIK, so every holdings row is an edge landing on the already-wired CIK spine: institution -> security -> issuer.
- The first 6 characters of any CUSIP are the issuer number - a derivable issuer-level key that groups all of an entity's securities across every dataset above, effectively a second registry ID for free.
- SEC Rule 13f-2 Form SHO aggregated short-position data (by CUSIP, with LEI and FIGI) is slated to start publishing on EDGAR during 2026 - not yet verified live; watch https://www.sec.gov/files/34-98738-fact-sheet.pdf for the launch.
- Fed SMCCF CUSIP-level purchases map 2020 emergency public money onto named corporate issuers - join CUSIP6 to 13F issuer names to CIK to ask whether bailed-out firms later appear in SAM exclusions or OSHA/EPA-style harm data.
- Not covered this pass (flagging, not skipping silently): NAIC insurer Schedule D bond holdings (paid), FINRA TRACE (licensed), DTCC NIIDS (restricted), the other ~48 states' unclaimed-property securities files, public pension funds' CUSIP-level holdings reports, FHLB Office of Finance and SBA pool disclosures - all carry CUSIPs and are candidates for a second sweep.

**Flags:**

- **GLEIF ISIN-to-LEI Relationship Files** — Coverage limited to early-mover numbering agencies, so not 100% of world ISINs; no record count published on page.
- **ESMA FIRDS (Financial Instruments Reference Data System)** — Verified via ESMA's databases-and-registers page which points to the registers portal; full XML files are large and need the ESMA download-instructions doc (ESMA65-8-5014).
- **SEC Form N-PORT Data Sets (fund portfolio holdings)** — sec.gov returns 403 to automated fetch (verified instead via catalog.data.gov entry); files are large; ISIN field populated only where the issuer assigned one (foreign securities especially).
- **OFAC NS-CMIC List (Chinese Military-Industrial Complex, wit…** — Treasury/OFAC HTML pages time out for automated fetchers; raw TXT works. File is prose-formatted text, needs parsing, not tabular.
- **OpenSanctions Securities Dataset (sanctioned issuers to ISI…** — CC-BY-4.0-NonCommercial - free for journalism/non-commercial, but a monetized Ripple product needs a commercial data license.
- **FCA UK FIRDS (UK instrument reference data)** — Download portal at data.fca.org.uk/#/viewdata; tech-spec PDF documents the automated file interface. OpenSanctions also mirrors it (gb_fca_firds, CC-BY-NC).
- **OpenFIGI API (ISIN-FIGI-ticker mapping)** — FIGI is Bloomberg-stewarded; usage is free but the page does not state redistribution license terms - check before republishing mapped data at scale.
- **ECB List of Eligible Marketable Assets (Eurosystem collater…** — None.
- **SEC Form N-MFP / Money Market Fund Information** — Monthly summary CSVs are fund-level; per-holding ISINs require parsing N-MFP XML filings from EDGAR. Declared User-Agent required (sec.gov 403s generic fetchers).
- **ESMA FITRS (Financial Instruments Transparency System)** — Verified as listed on ESMA's databases page; direct file download follows the same registers-portal mechanics as FIRDS.
- **Deutsche Boerse Xetra T7 All Tradable Instruments** — Sibling exchange lists (Euronext, LSE, Nasdaq Nordic) not individually verified in this pass. Deutsche Boerse disclaims warranty on accuracy/completeness.
- **FCA Aggregated Net Short Positions (short-selling disclosur…** — Public file mixes named positions at/above 0.5% with anonymised aggregates - check which layer you need. EU national siblings (BaFin, AMF, CONSOB) exist but were not verified in this pass.
- **Wikidata ISIN property (P946)** — Crowdsourced - treat every mapping as a lead requiring verification; item count using P946 not published on the property page.
- **ANNA Service Bureau ISIN Lookup (registration authority)** — Free tier is lookup-only, no bulk export; bulk is commercial. This, not isin.org (a lookalike commercial site), is the real authority.
- **OpenSanctions EU FIRDS Mirror (eu_esma_firds)** — CC-BY-NC license - commercial use needs a paid license. LANDSCAPE GAPS not covered this pass: NSDL India ISIN master (connection reset), ECB CSDB (not public at security level), WM Datenservice / CUSIP Global Services / SEDOL (paid commercial), FINRA TRACE (licensed), ESMA securitisation repositories (restricted), oth…
- **ESMA FIRDS — Financial Instruments Reference Data System** — Register UI is JS-heavy (WebFetch shows 'No data found'); bulk download works via the documented HTTP file-listing requests (ESMA65-8-5014 instructions, verified). OpenSanctions mirrors it in friendlier CSV/JSON under CC-BY-NC.
- **OFAC Non-SDN Lists / Consolidated Sanctions List (NS-CMIC,…** — ofac.treasury.gov timed out on automated fetch (likely bot-blocking); ISIN presence confirmed via OFAC recent-actions notices and Federal Register texts. OFAC SDN data is already landed in Ripple via IMO — same publisher, new key.
- **OpenFIGI API (ISIN ↔ FIGI ↔ ticker mapping)** — Bloomberg-operated; check Terms of Service for redistribution limits on mapped results. FIGI is the open-license alternative key — SEC 13F filings now carry a FIGI column, making it a US-side spine candidate.
- **ESMA European Ratings Platform (ERP)** — Register UI is JS-based and caps exports at high row volumes; large-scale access is via ESMA's machine-to-machine web services — expect integration work, not a one-click bulk file.
- **NRSRO Rule 17g-7(b) Rating History Files (S&P, Moody's, Fit…** — Files sit on each agency's own site behind free registration/click-through ToS; sec.gov guide page 403s automated fetch. - **SEC Form N-MFP Data Sets (money market fund holdings)** — ISIN column not directly confirmed (sec.gov blocks automated fetch; readme not readable this session) — CUSIP and LEI are confirmed fields, and US ISINs are mechanically derivable from CUSIP. OFR's Short-term Funding Monitor (financialresearch.gov, verified) republishes this via free API.

Not covered this pass: exchange master files (Euronext/LSE/Deutsche Börse — paid licensed products, largely redundant with FIRDS), Luxembourg SE official list, ECB CSDB (restricted), and…
- *Index false positives:* Dropped all 106 broad-substring index matches as junk: FUNDRAISING/RAISING variants (~60 datasets, e.g. charity fundraising numbers by AU state, IRS-990-style FUNDRAISINGAMT), ADVERTISING variants (~15), DISINFECT*/DISINFECTANT water-quality columns (~10), DISINVESTMENT survey columns (4), ISINCAMA = 'IsInCAMA' parcel-appraisal flag on Harris County TX GIS layers (19 datasets, largest single clus…

**Brief critique:** The brief undersells one structural fact: for US paper, ISIN is just CUSIP wearing a "US" prefix plus a check digit, so landing ISIN makes the planned CUSIP key nearly free by deterministic transform - and ISIN is the better one to land first because its sources (FIRDS, GLEIF, N-PORT) are genuinely open while CUSIP bulk data is CGS-licensed and paid. Also, FIGI should be promoted from a flag to a real candidate key: it is the only fully open, freely mappable securities identifier in this domain.

**Brief critique:** The brief undersold one landmine and one shortcut: US ISINs mechanically embed CUSIPs ("US" + CUSIP + check digit), which makes the planned CUSIP key largely redundant once ISIN lands — but CUSIP Global Services asserts IP claims over embedded CUSIPs (subject of an EU antitrust case), so mass-deriving a CUSIP column from ISINs carries licensing risk. FIGI is the genuinely open sibling key (free bulk mapping, now an optional column in SEC 13F filings) and is the safer US-side spine.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- OFAC NS-CMIC list carries ISINs directly on a sanctions list - joining it to SEC N-PORT holdings extends Ripple's OFAC lens from ships (IMO) to securities: 'which US funds still hold paper Americans are banned from financing' is a ready-made story mechanism the key list did not anticipate.
- US ISIN = 'US' + 9-char CUSIP + check digit: every CUSIP-keyed dataset (Ginnie/Fannie/Freddie MBS disclosures, TreasuryDirect auction results, MSRB) becomes reachable from an ISIN spine with a one-line transform - ISIN and the planned CUSIP key can share one spine column.
- ESMA FIRDS and GLEIF ISIN-LEI files put issuer LEI on every instrument, landing directly on Ripple's already-wired LEI tables (GLEIF registry, CFPB HMDA) - mortgage lenders to their parent group's bond issuance in two hops.
- SEC N-PORT filings carry the filing fund's CIK, bridging fund holdings straight into Ripple's already-landed EDGAR/CIK financials - fund family behavior joins issuer behavior with no new key needed.
- SEC 13F filings now accept FIGI as an identifier column; with OpenFIGI's free ISIN-FIGI-CUSIP mapping, FIGI becomes a working bridge between 13F institutional holdings and everything ISIN-keyed.
- eFIRDS (efirds.eu, by Nordic Trustee) - free third-party FIRDS search UI useful for manual ISIN verification during investigations (surfaced in search results; not deep-verified).
- ESMA FIRDS records carry the issuer's LEI on every instrument — an ISIN→LEI→GLEIF chain that welds 5.3M securities onto Ripple's already-landed GLEIF/LEI and CFPB HMDA tables without any new bridge work.
- SEC 13F institutional-holdings filings added an optional FIGI column in 2023 — via OpenFIGI's free ISIN↔FIGI mapping, 13F connects to the ISIN world entirely on open identifiers, bypassing licensed CUSIP.
- SEC N-PORT holding rows carry CUSIP + ISIN + LEI side by side — a free, government-published Rosetta-stone crosswalk that seeds three Ripple keys at once from one already-public source.
- OFAC sanctioned-securities ISINs (NS-CMIC list, EO 14071 Russian ban) joined to N-PORT fund holdings yields a dated who-held-banned-paper timeline — connects Ripple's landed OFAC/sanctions holdings to retail investors' money through a securities key the OFAC work (IMO ships) never anticipated.
- Wikidata items link ISIN, LEI, and SEC CIK on the same entity (properties P946/P1278/P5531) — a CC0 patch cable between Ripple's landed EDGAR CIK spine and the securities world.
- ESMA's ERP ratings-by-ISIN joined to fund holdings enables a 'downgraded but still held' lens — the securities analog of Ripple's 'banned but still operating' flagship story.

## LEI — Legal Entity Identifier

*Status in Ripple:* wired (2 tables).

**Already sitting in our scouted index:**

Nothing in the index carries this key.

*Sweep note:* True total of genuine GLEIF LEI hits in PORTAL_DATASET_INDEX: 0 out of 338,520 datasets across 96 portals. Verified exhaustively: word-boundary regex for the LEI token, LEI_CODE/LEI_NUM/ISSUER_LEI/GLEIF/LEGAL[-_ ]ENTITY[-_ ]ID variants, full enumeration of all 189 distinct columns containing the LEI substring, and title searches for 'legal entity identifier', word-boundary LEI, and GLEIF - all empty. Query shape was sanity-tested (same pattern finds 44 NPI datasets), so the zero is real, not a query bug. The key IS live in the landed warehouse: LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.INTL_GLEIF (the GLEIF regist…

**Brief critique:** Two of the brief's starting points are weaker than billed: the CFTC swap dealer list and the SEC SBS list are name-only (verified: no LEI codes), so they're fuzzy-match sources, not LEI carriers — the structured substitute is EDGAR Form SBSE filings. Also note the ISIN-LEI file covers only newly issued ISINs from participating agencies, and RSSD (via the free NIC crosswalk) is the denser sibling key for everything US-bank — LEI's unique power is the free who-owns-whom tree and the fund-holdings (N-PORT/N-MFP) join.

**Brief critique:** Two corrections: the CFTC swap-dealer list carries no LEIs at all (names only - the SEC SBS list is the real prize, and it's better than billed: a CIK-to-LEI crosswalk hiding in a column mislabeled 'UIC No.'), and 'significant state-level sources' basically don't exist for LEI - states don't use it; the state bridge runs through GLEIF's OpenCorporates mapping and the HMDA Panel instead. Also note the ISIN-LEI file only covers newer issuances, not the full legacy universe.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- HMDA Panel carries tax_id next to LEI — a direct LEI-to-EIN bridge into Ripple's wired IRS BMF / Form 5500 / 990 holdings (verify the column on download)
- Wikidata P1278 items also carry CIK (P5531) — a free CC0 LEI-to-CIK crosswalk onto Ripple's wired EDGAR tables
- GLEIF Level 1 records embed the local registration authority + company number for every entity — an implicit LEI-to-state-Secretary-of-State bridge even without OpenCorporates
- SEC N-CEN discloses fund service providers (custodians, administrators, auditors) with LEIs — vendor-network mapping around money, not just ownership
- GLEIF-GEM mapping (June 2026) connects Global Energy Monitor asset IDs to LEIs — an unexpected on-ramp for the planned EIA Plant/ORIS key
- Negative result worth recording: FDIC BankFind API has no LEI field (checked live, 95 fields) — FFIEC NIC is the mandatory hop from LEI to FDIC cert numbers
- GLEIF also lists an S&P CIQ Company ID-to-LEI mapping (served via LEI Search weekly rather than a bulk file) — a paid-vendor-ID bridge if S&P-keyed data ever arrives
- HMDA Public Panel carries tax_id (EIN) next to LEI - a direct LEI-EIN bridge into Ripple's IRS 990/BMF/Form 5500 holdings that no key list anticipated; a mortgage lender's LEI now reaches its pension filings and nonprofit ties.
- SEC SBS dealer list's 'UIC No.' column contains GLEIF LEIs alongside CIK numbers - an official, if tiny, CIK-LEI crosswalk (verified inside the Excel file).
- OFAC SDN Advanced XML schema includes LEI among its identification types (confirmed in the sdn_advanced_notes spec, sparsely populated) - Ripple's existing OFAC holdings can join GLEIF directly where present, no name-matching.
- GLEIF publishes a Global Energy Monitor entity-ID-to-LEI mapping (monthly, free) - an unanticipated bridge from financial identity to physical power plants and fossil assets, feeding the planned EIA/ORIS key.
- NRSRO Rule 17g-7(b) credit-rating-history XBRL files (each rating agency's website, free) identify rated obligors by CIK, not LEI - a discovered CIK-keyed dataset: full rating histories joinable to EDGAR holdings.
- GLEIF golden copy is mirrored on AWS Open Data (s3://gleif, CC0, no account, refreshed 3x daily) - the cheapest ingestion path for keeping the wired GLEIF table current.
- FFIEC NIC 'transformations' file logs bank M&A/succession events by RSSD - paired with ID_LEI it answers 'the bank died, but which legal entity absorbed its conduct record?'

*Sweep note:* Headline: RSSD appears in ZERO of the ~338,520 scouted portal datasets (column regex '.*RSSD.*' = 0 hits; title regex incl. RSSD/FFIEC/CALL REPORT = 0 relevant hits). The key lives exclusively in the landed federal warehouse. The real connection graph is internal: FED_FFIEC_CALL_REPORTS.IDRSSD <-> FED_FDIC_BANK_DATA.RSSDID is a live RSSD-to-RSSD join, and FED_FDIC_BANK_DATA carries both RSSDID and CERT, making it the Rosetta table that pulls FED_FDIC_FAILED_BANKS (CERT) and FED_SBA_LOANS (BANKFDICNUMBER) into the bank spine. That enables leads like 'which failed/troubled banks were funneling…

*Landed tables carrying it:* `LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FFIEC_CALL_REPORTS (IDRSSD, RSSD_ID) - direct RSSD carrier`, `LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FDIC_BANK_DATA (RSSDID, CERT) - direct RSSD carrier + the RSSD<->FDIC-CERT crosswalk`, `LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_FDIC_FAILED_BANKS (CERT, CHARTER) - sibling keys, joins to RSSD via FED_FDIC_BANK_DATA.CERT`, `LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_SBA_LOANS (BANKFDICNUMBER, BANKNCUANUMBER) - sibling keys: lender's FDIC cert + NCUA charter`, `LIBRARY_RAW.LANDING.FED_CFPB_HMDA (LEI) - modern HMDA institution key; LEI bridges to INTL_GLEIF.LEI and to RSSD via public LEI-RSSD crosswalks`

**Brief critique:** Two corrections: Fed enforcement actions do NOT carry RSSD (public CSV is names-only and only reaches back to ~2015), and most of the scouted state-portal hits are false positives — the two Texas datasets verifiably have no RSSD column and the Utah one is dead. Bigger than the brief implied: the CURRENT HMDA panel (2018+) carries rssd + lei + taxId in one file, making RSSD an instant three-way bridge into Ripple's already-wired LEI and EIN holdings, not just a legacy banking key.

**Brief critique:** The brief oversold Fed enforcement actions as an RSSD carrier — the bulk CSV is name-only (no RSSD column), so that pairing is probabilistic until name-matched through NIC. It also undersold NIC itself: the attributes file is not just the registry but a six-way crosswalk hub (ID_LEI, ID_ABA_PRIM, ID_FDIC_CERT, ID_NCUA, ID_OCC, ID_TAX), meaning landing NIC effectively delivers the sibling keys FDIC CERT and ABA routing number for free; the FHFA-hosted Avery file (legacy HMDA-to-RSSD crosswalk) appears retired (404 at all known FHFA paths).

**Unexpected connections found:**

- NIC Attributes file is itself a multi-ID crosswalk hub: alongside RSSD it carries FDIC CERT, OCC charter, primary ABA routing number, and an LEI column — a direct free bridge from the bank spine into Ripple's wired GLEIF/LEI holdings
- HMDA Public Panel (2018+) carries taxId (EIN) next to rssd and lei — bridges banks into Ripple's wired EIN holdings (Form 5500, IRS 990/BMF), e.g. bank charitable foundations and benefit plans
- NY Fed CRSP-FRB link chains RSSD to PERMCO to ticker to CIK — publicly traded bank holding companies land in Ripple's wired EDGAR/CIK tables, connecting bank enforcement to insider filings and financials
- Fed Discount Window quarterly transaction data (federalreserve.gov/regreform/discount-window.htm, Excel, 2010-present with ~2-year lag) identifies emergency borrowers by name + ABA routing number — no RSSD, but joinable via the ABA column in NIC Attributes to ask which shaky banks leaned on the Fed before failing
- Fed enforcement actions CSV names sanctioned INDIVIDUALS with their bank affiliation — a person-level layer that can be name-matched against other Ripple people tables (SDN persons, SEC filers) for the 'banned banker resurfaces elsewhere' pattern
- NIC attributes ID_LEI gives a direct RSSD-to-LEI bridge into Ripple's wired GLEIF/HMDA LEI spine — no fuzzy matching needed
- NIC attributes ID_TAX is a potential RSSD-to-EIN bridge into the wired IRS/DOL EIN spine (population/masking unverified — check at landing)
- HMDA Public Panel rows carry lei + rssd + taxId together, a triple crosswalk that ties one lender's LEI, RSSD, and EIN in a single confirmed record
- Fed discount-window loan-level disclosures (federalreserve.gov/regreform/discount-window.htm, verified) identify borrowers by ABA routing number, which joins to RSSD via NIC ID_ABA_PRIM — emergency-borrowing stories with a two-year lag
- NY Fed CRSP-FRB link chains RSSD to PERMCO to ticker, reaching Ripple's wired EDGAR/CIK spine — regulator-known trouble vs. what shareholders were told
- FDIC BankFind failures endpoint (CERT-keyed) joins to RSSD via the institutions endpoint, replacing the dead Utah failed-banks dataset nationwide

**Brief critique:** The Missouri portal hit "Raise The Roof Insurance" is a mis-tag — it's a single licensee record (a roofing outfit), not a NAIC-keyed dataset; the real Missouri asset is the DCI reports site, off-portal. Two additions the brief underplayed: NPN (National Producer Number) is a second live sibling key already sitting in the Texas agent files and SBS, and the tagger must hard-disambiguate NAIC from NAICS — every open-data portal is littered with NAICS "NAIC code" columns (confirmed directly in catalog searches). Core insurer financial statements by NAIC code are paid (NAIC/AM Best), so the free landscape is exactly this: federal ACA files + state market/complaint files.

**Brief critique:** The brief's "FIO reports" pointer is near-worthless for this key - FIO publishes aggregated PDFs (and its homeowners dataset is ZIP-level, insurer-anonymous), and treasury.gov timed out on every fetch; meanwhile the brief missed the single best federal carrier of this key: DOL Form 5500 Schedule A, which stamps an NAIC code on every insured ERISA plan and lands directly on Ripple's already-wired EIN spine. The HIOS-issuer-ID sibling hunch is confirmed and the free crosswalk is the CMS MLR PUF itself (both codes in one file); also note the authoritative NAIC registry is only free as a PDF summary - the machine-readable statutory data is paywalled, so states (TX, FL) are the free registry route.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- Form 5500 Schedule A is an EIN-to-NAIC bridge already inside Ripple's wired 5500 lane: every employer plan names its carrier's NAIC code plus broker commission dollars — connects the EIN spine to the insurer spine with money on the edges.
- The CMS MLR PUF doubles as the NAIC-to-HIOS crosswalk (both IDs in one file), and the MLR template also reportedly carries the company's federal EIN — verify at landing; if present it links insurers straight to IRS BMF/990 holdings.
- NPN (National Producer Number) appears in the Texas agent/adjuster datasets and NAIC SBS — a person-level key for tracking a revoked or complaint-heavy agent resurfacing under new carriers across states.
- Washington's Health Plan Prior Authorization dataset (data.wa.gov/d/fysr-7kwx) joins carriers by name to the WA loss-ratio table — a probabilistic care-denial lens the key list did not anticipate.
- SERFF tracking numbers form a document-trail key per NAIC company: rate-hike justification filings that serve as receipts for any carrier the map flags.
- DOL Form 5500 Schedule A: NAIC-to-EIN bridge - every employer benefit plan (EIN, already landed) names its insurance carrier by NAIC code plus commissions paid, connecting insurers to the worker-benefits money flow
- Texas TDI Authorized Companies list: a literal NAIC+EIN+NAIC-Group crosswalk file - joins insurers to IRS BMF/Form 5500 holdings and builds corporate family trees for free
- Texas TDI agency appointments dataset carries Agency EIN beside insurer NAIC ID - maps the agency businesses (EIN spine) distributing each carrier's products
- CMS MLR PUF doubles as the free NAIC-HIOS crosswalk, opening the whole healthcare.gov/HIOS dataset family (QHP landscape, rate review) to the NAIC spine
- NY DFS premium datasets and NAIC Listing give clean name+NAIC pairs for public insurers - name-match to CIK (EDGAR, landed) to compare what insurers tell Wall Street vs what state complaint data shows
- SERFF and state complaint data keyed by NAIC can be joined to LEI/GLEIF (landed) for large insurance groups via name-match, tying US regulatory behavior to global entity structures

**Brief critique:** The brief undersells what's already in-house: the wired congress-legislators roster (BIOGUIDE+ICPSR) is the very crosswalk this key needs — its id.fec column is likely already landed and just unkeyed, so the bridge may be a dbt model away, not a new source. Also, FEC_CMTE_ID and FEC_CAND_ID are tracked as two planned keys but are one family with a first-class linkage file (ccl) — spec them together; and "significant state-level sources" for this key effectively don't exist as hard IDs (states use their own numbering; it's name-match via FollowTheMoney/OpenSecrets only).

**Brief critique:** The brief bundles two distinct namespaces into one key: FEC_CMTE_ID (C########) and FEC_CAND_ID (H/S/P########) never collide and are joined only by the ccl linkage file - the spec should model them as two keys plus a bridge table, matching Ripple's existing planned split. Also note the crosswalk is already in-house: the wired congress-legislators roster carries the fec id list, so part of this key is sitting in the warehouse waiting to be extracted, and IRS 527 / lobbying sources don't actually carry FEC IDs - their real join to Ripple runs through EIN and name-match.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- FEC committee master's CONNECTED_ORG_NM field name-matches corporate PAC sponsors to EDGAR registrants — an FEC-to-CIK bridge the key list didn't anticipate (corporate PAC -> parent public company -> SEC filings).
- Schedule A contributions carry EMPLOYER/OCCUPATION free text — name-match to USAspending recipients (UEI) and SAM exclusions enables the federal-contractor pay-to-play lens (52 USC 30119 bans contractor contributions) using tables Ripple already holds.
- IRS 527 filings are EIN-keyed, so landing them joins STEEL into the wired EIN spine (IRS BMF, 990, revocations) even before any FEC name-match — one dataset feeds two spines.
- Wikidata items carrying P1839 (FEC ID) typically also carry P1157 (Bioguide), CIK, and EIN properties — a free multi-spine crosswalk hub across four Ripple keys at once.
- FEC operating-expenditure payee names match to USAspending vendor names: consultancies paid by both campaigns and federal agencies — a conflict lens connecting FEC to UEI holdings.
- FCC political files tie committee ad buys to broadcast stations via FCC Facility ID — a sibling identifier to the FCC FRN already on Ripple's candidate-key list.
- Senate LD-203 honoree names join to the wired congressional committee-membership tables (BIOGUIDE): lobbyists donating to members of the exact committees they report lobbying.
- FEC committee master's CONNECTED_ORG_NM field names each corporate/union PAC's sponsor - name-match to EDGAR CIK, GLEIF LEI, and IRS EIN holdings gives 'company PAC money vs. the federal decisions that benefit the company' without any new key.
- FEC individual contributions carry EMPLOYER/OCCUPATION - name-match to SAM/USAspending UEI recipients surfaces federal contractors' executives funding the legislators who oversee their contracts (pay-to-play lens).
- IRS 527 filings are EIN-keyed, so they join STEEL to Ripple's landed IRS BMF/990/revocation tables - a 527 spending big with no FEC registration, or one whose IRS status was revoked while still reporting expenditures, is a self-contained lead.
- FEC's 'lobbyist/registrant committees' and 'lobbyist bundled contributions' bulk files are a built-in bridge between the FEC world (committee IDs) and the Senate LDA lobbying world (registrant names) - a cleaner join than raw name-matching LD-203s.
- FEC ID -> congress-legislators -> ICPSR -> already-wired Voteview rollcalls closes the loop money-to-votes entirely within existing holdings: donation timing vs. roll-call switches needs zero new crosswalk work.
- Health-sector donors: contribution EMPLOYER strings name-match to NPPES organization names, connecting campaign money to the provider/facility tables (including LEIE-banned entities) already at the core of Ripple.

**Brief critique:** The brief's one stale pointer is GovTrack: its bulk data/API died in 2017, so it is not a landable source - its live remnants are the misconduct database and the unitedstates scrapers it co-maintains. Bigger point the brief undersold: this key is the cheapest multiplier in the whole warehouse, because the already-landed crosswalk carries FEC candidate IDs, OpenSecrets CIDs, LIS IDs, and Wikidata QIDs - the planned FEC_CAND_ID key is essentially pre-wired the day FEC bulk lands.

**Brief critique:** Bioguide and ICPSR never co-occur in any federal file — the pairing exists only in Voteview's members file and congress-legislators, both already wired, so the real landscape is event data keyed to ONE of the two (bioguide on the federal/legislative side, ICPSR on the academic/money side). The brief also missed that live Senate votes carry neither ID — they use LIS member IDs — so the 'lis' field in the wired roster is a load-bearing bridge, and the ids.fec[] field already hands you the planned FEC_CAND_ID key for free.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- Stock trades to CIK: Senate Stock Watcher records carry stock tickers, and Ripple already holds EDGAR ticker-to-CIK - a two-hop join from a senator's bioguide to the SEC filings of the exact company traded, no new key needed.
- FEC IDs ride free: legislators-current/historical include fec candidate IDs, so landing FEC bulk (planned key) instantly connects money to the existing member spine without any new crosswalk work.
- Wikidata as a bridge hub: P1157 (bioguide) sits on the same items as company/board/employer links, giving probabilistic paths from members to LEI- and CIK-keyed entities Ripple already holds.
- Committee jurisdiction to USAspending: committee assignment tables name the agencies each member oversees; joining those agencies' awards (UEI, already landed) to the member's district asks whether oversight seats steer contracts home.
- Senate LIS ID is a hidden fourth ID in the landed crosswalk - it unlocks senate.gov's real-time roll call XML, which Voteview only mirrors after curation.
- Ticker-to-CIK bridge: House/Senate PTR stock trades list tickers that join straight to the wired EDGAR company_tickers table - member trades vs companies their committee regulates, using only already-landed holdings.
- congress-legislators ids.fec[] is a deterministic bioguide-to-FEC_CAND_ID crosswalk - the planned FEC key arrives pre-bridged to the legislator spine at zero cost.
- govinfo MODS metadata for Congressional Record (CREC), hearings (CHRG), and committee reports (CRPT) reportedly embeds bioguideId per speaking/authoring member - would key full-text floor statements to members; NOT verified this session, scout it.
- House Appropriations Community Project Funding (earmark) disclosure tables link member names to recipient organizations that resolve against wired EIN/UEI tables - money steered to connected nonprofits/vendors; page not verified this session.
- Wikidata P1157 items link members to spouses, employers, and board seats on org items that carry CIK/LEI - relationship edges from the legislator spine into wired corporate registries.
- Rot warning worth indexing: congressionalbills.org now serves a gambling site and housestockwatcher.com is DNS-dead - two commonly-cited congressional data URLs are traps; use Comparative Agendas Project and the House Clerk FD index instead.
- Senate LDA API dies 07/31/2026 (migrating to LDA.gov) - any lobbying ingestion planned against lda.senate.gov has a 9-day fuse.

- *Index false positives:* The DOCKET key spans two real universes plus one big junk family, and I treated them separately. (1) COURT dockets (case numbers, per-court formats) and (2) AGENCY dockets (rulemaking/administrative proceedings: FDMS/regulations.gov, PUC/ACC, SOAH, city admin hearings) - both kept and labeled per hit. (3) DROPPED, the dominant false positive: RECORDER dockets - ~95 of 148 column hits are Tucson O…

**Brief critique:** DOCKET is not one key — it is dozens of per-issuer namespaces (PACER case numbers, EPA docket IDs, FCC proceeding numbers, NLRB case numbers) that never overlap, so it is only STEEL as a composite (issuer + docket); the index should split it into COURT_DOCKET and AGENCY_DOCKET or the tagger will produce false joins between, say, a FERC docket and a foreclosure docket. The highest-leverage sibling is the CourtListener docket ID as a canonical spine, since RECAP already normalizes court+number.

**Brief critique:** DOCKET is not one key - it is hundreds of per-issuer namespaces (every court and agency mints its own format), so the raw string collides across issuers and the usable key is the composite (issuer, docket_no); several of the 145 index hits (Maricopa Water/Sewer Provider, Community Solar, Maryland SIPs) look like incidental 'docket' column matches, not real proceeding IDs. Best sibling spine: CourtListener's docket_id, which already normalizes court + docket number for free and would serve as Ripple's canonical docket surrogate.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- SEC administrative proceedings name respondents that map directly onto Ripple's wired CIK/EDGAR tables — DOCKET becomes a discipline-history layer on companies already in the warehouse
- FCC ECFS filings carry the filer's FRN, bridging DOCKET to the FCC FRN candidate key without name matching
- NTSB accident dockets contain aircraft registration (tail) numbers — a ready-made feed for the planned TAIL_NUMBER/ICAO24 key
- EPA ECHO ICIS FE&C enforcement cases join to facilities via FRS ID, activating the FRS_ID candidate key alongside DOCKET
- Ripple's existing fed_doj_fca_settlements and fed_doj_crt_cases staging tables contain federal case numbers that should join straight into RECAP/CourtListener dockets — a DOCKET connection already sitting in the repo
- USPTO PTAB proceedings (covered in Docket Alarm, also via free USPTO PTAB API) link docket-style trial numbers to patent numbers, bridging DOCKET to the tagger-known PATENT key
- RECAP party names can be screened against LEIE and SAM exclusions to ask the flagship question — is the banned provider/contractor currently in federal litigation?
- Chapter 11 bankruptcy filings mirrored in RECAP list the debtor's EIN in the case caption - a direct docket-to-EIN bridge into IRS BMF/Form 5500 holdings that the key list did not anticipate
- EPA ICIS FE&C enforcement cases carry FRS registry IDs - wires DOCKET to the unconfirmed FRS_ID candidate key facility-by-facility
- NTSB investigation dockets carry aircraft tail numbers and operators - a live on-ramp to the planned TAIL_NUMBER/ICAO24 key
- FCC ECFS filings carry the filer's FRN, validating the FCC FRN candidate key and tying licensees to the proceedings they fight
- FEC MUR respondents include committee IDs - docket-side entry to the planned FEC_CMTE_ID key before that table even lands
- GAO bid-protest dockets carry solicitation/contract numbers that join USAspending awards (UEI) exactly, not probabilistically by name
- CourtListener bulk also ships the federal judge database and judicial financial disclosures - a judge-level conflict-of-interest layer (judge's stockholdings vs parties' CIK/tickers) no key anticipated
- Fed/FDIC/OCC enforcement orders identify banks by RSSD and FDIC cert numbers - docket-side entry into the RSSD candidate key and existing GLEIF/HMDA holdings
- HHS DAB civil-remedies dockets name LEIE-excluded providers and CCN-identified nursing homes - joining two already-wired Ripple keys with zero new plumbing
