**Brief critique:** The brief is right that LEAIC is the canonical geography bridge, but it's frozen at 2012 and ICPSR-gated — the live public ORI roster is the FBI Crime Data API agency endpoint (free key), which should be the registry spine, with LEAIC as the FIPS/census bridge; also note the true issuer file (CJIS/NCIC ORI registry) is not public at all. LEOKA and hate-crime files are not separate landscapes — they ship inside CDE bulk and Kaplan's mirrors, so treat them as one landing, not three.

**Brief critique:** The brief's 'authoritative issuer/registry file' does not exist publicly — the FBI/CJIS NCIC ORI file is restricted, so the public spine must be assembled from the CDE agencies endpoint + LEAIC (which is a 2012 snapshot, staler than the brief implies); also note ORI covers jails, courts, and prosecutors, not just police, so the key is bigger than 'law-enforcement agency'. COPS grant data is weaker than billed — public award lists are name-only PDFs with no ORI, and the money trail is better reached through already-wired USAspending/UEI.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- Kaplan's County-Level UCR Arrest and Offense Data (openICPSR project 108164, verified live) is FIPS-keyed, not ORI-keyed - it joins Ripple's existing county marts (CDC drug poisoning, county double-burden, jail disparity) directly, no ORI spine needed.
- COPS and other DOJ grants to police agencies already sit in wired USAspending under recipient UEI (assistance listings like 16.710) - matching grant recipients to ORIs via LEAIC/LEAR name+geo gives an ORI-to-UEI bridge, i.e. 'federal money vs agency harm record' using a table Ripple has already landed.
- LEAIC's FIPS columns make every ORI dataset joinable to every county-keyed Ripple mart - the ORI key's first payoff may be county-level lenses, not agency-level ones.
- DLA LESO 1033 military surplus transfer data (quarterly public xlsx, agency name + state) name-matches through LEAR/LEAIC to ask whether militarized agencies show worse harm records - DLA page blocked headless fetch today, verify in browser before scouting.
- WaPo's fatal-police-shootings-agencies.csv doubles as a free, newsroom-maintained ORI-to-agency-name crosswalk that is fresher than LEAIC 2012 - useful for spine QA even ignoring the shootings data.
- COPS/DOJ grants to police agencies also appear in USAspending under UEI (already wired) — a name/geo ORI-to-UEI crosswalk would let Ripple ask 'agency with worst force/killing record still receiving federal grant money', connecting the ORI lane to the money lane with no new key
- DoD 1033/LESO military-surplus transfers to police agencies (dla.mil publishes quarterly public Excel files at Disposition-Services/Offers/Law-Enforcement/Public-Information — site 403'd automated fetch, verify manually) — agency-name match to ORI: militarized gear vs harm record
- NY jail-population data revealed ORIs are issued to jails/detention facilities — deaths-in-custody and jail datasets can join the same spine, extending 'who gets hurt' past arrest into detention
- Washington Post / Mapping Police Violence officer names cross-matched against National Police Index employment histories is a person-level (not key-level) mechanism for the wandering-officer pattern — an officer involved in a killing resurfacing at another ORI
- LEAIC's ORI-to-FIPS-to-census-place bridge connects the ORI lane to every geography-keyed holding Ripple has (e.g., HMDA lending via census geography): policing patterns vs lending patterns in the same places
- Scouting note: Socrata catalog search misses ORI when it only appears as a column name — the Discovery API (api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1) with column-level probing is how the state/local long tail actually gets found; not covered this session: California OpenJustice URSUS use-of-force and deaths-in-custody files (JS site, unverifiable via fetch), state UCR portals beyond CO/CT (TX DPS, PA, W…

- **USCG PSIX (Port State Information eXchange, MISLE snapshot)** — FOIA-cleaned snapshot; exact export scope needs a manual pass; SOAP API is old-style

- **UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List** — main.un.org page 403s to bots; the list itself serves via redirect to time-limited blob URLs - lander should hit scsanctions.un.org endpoints

**Brief critique:** The brief undersells MMSI: AIS position reports are keyed by MMSI, with IMO only in static messages, so the IMO landscape is only fully joinable once the ITU MARS IMO-MMSI crosswalk exists — MMSI should be promoted from tagger-known to planned alongside this key. Also, OFAC maritime advisories are unstructured PDF annexes largely redundant with the SDN vessel entries; the higher-value unlisted sibling is the PSC-detention family (Paris/Tokyo/PSIX), which the brief did name but which is where the story actually lives.

**Brief critique:** The brief undersells a structural fact: AIS data (one of the two wired IMO tables) natively keys on MMSI, not IMO — only a minority of NOAA static records carry IMO, so the sibling key MMSI (currently tagger-known, no table) is nearly co-equal and the ITU MARS / GFW / Equasis IMO-MMSI crosswalk is the piece that makes the AIS holdings fully joinable. Also, the true authoritative issuer file (S&P Global's issuance database) has no bulk form — GISIS + Equasis together are the practical registry spine, both registration-gated with no bulk export, which caps how "landable" this key's core is compared to NPI or LEI.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- IMO Company Number: Equasis/GISIS link every hull to its registered owner and ISM manager via a second IMO-issued ID (company number) - a whole new candidate key that bridges ships to GLEIF LEI and OFAC entity records, connecting ship-level harm to the shore companies profiting
- ITU MARS gives the IMO-MMSI-callsign crosswalk that turns Ripple's existing NOAA AIS table from movement trivia into an identity engine - catches ships that swap MMSI to launder identity while the IMO stays hull-permanent
- OpenSanctions FollowTheMoney graph links sanctioned vessels to persons and companies that carry LEI/registration numbers already in the Ripple spine - a ready-made cross-domain bridge from IMO into the corporate side of the map
- UK/EU/UN sanctions files carry aircraft designations in the same structures as ships - the same lander pattern would seed the planned TAIL_NUMBER/ICAO24 key for free
- USCG CGMIX NVDC vessel documentation links IMO hulls to US official numbers and documented owners - a path from foreign hulls to US corporate records (UEI/EIN side)
- NOT COVERED / UNVERIFIED THIS SESSION (bot-blocked or budget): USCG marine casualty for-researchers Excel files (dco.uscg.mil 403), Indian Ocean MoU + other regional PSC MoUs (iomou.org 403; Black Sea/Mediterranean/Vina del Mar/Abuja/Riyadh MoUs not fetched), MARAD US-flag fleet reports (maritime.dot.gov 403, not found on Socrata), EMSA THETIS, OFAC maritime advisories PDFs, per-RFMO vessel regis…
- ITU MARS (and GFW vessel identity / AIS static) provide an IMO-to-MMSI-to-callsign crosswalk — this promotes MMSI from tagger-known to a landable, connected key and detects identity-swapping hulls.
- Equasis/GISIS expose IMO Company Numbers for registered owners and ISM managers — a second IMO-namespace key that turns ship-level findings into company-network findings, probabilistically joinable to GLEIF LEI (already wired) by name/country.
- OpenSanctions entities frequently carry LEI and national registration numbers — a ready-made bridge from sanctioned-vessel owners into Ripple's GLEIF table.
- THETIS-MRV pairs each IMO with the reporting company and per-year fuel/CO2 — an emissions-harm lens on the same hulls, and a free annual fleet census independent of AIS.
- NGO Shipbreaking Platform lists connect hull histories to worker deaths at scrap yards — the 'who gets hurt' receipt at end-of-life, joining last-voyage flags/owners back to sanctions and PSC records.
- Wikidata P458 is CC0 and links IMO to dozens of other identifier systems, letting Ripple enrich without licensing risk.

## TAIL_ICAO24 — Tail Number + ICAO24 hex

*Status in Ripple:* planned, spec-only.

**Already sitting in our scouted index:**

Nothing in the index carries this key.

*Sweep note:* Real portal-index hits: 5 total (no truncation). The decisive finding is in the landed warehouse, not the portals: FED_FAA_REGISTRY holds both halves of TAIL_ICAO24 (N_NUMBER is the tail, MODE_S_CODE_HEX is the icao24 transponder hex) plus registrant identity, so it is the natural spine table for this key. No ADS-B/OpenSky-style track data (icao24 columns) exists anywhere in the 338K scouted portal datasets - the icao24 half of the key lives only in the landed FAA registry. **Brief critique:** The brief's biggest miss is BTS: On-Time Performance carries a Tail_Number for every US domestic flight since 1987 and Schedule B-43 gives annual airline fleet inventories by tail — together the largest federal carriers of this key, unmentioned. Also note FAA enforcement actions is a weak carrier (name-keyed PDFs, not tails), while OFAC SDN — a file Ripple already loads for IMO ships — carries sanctioned aircraft with tail numbers, so the first connection for this key is free.

**Brief critique:** Two corrections: (1) for US aircraft, ICAO24 hex is algorithmically derivable from the N-number (deterministic mapping), so the US crosswalk is nearly free — the real crosswalk work is foreign-registered hexes; (2) tail numbers and hexes are reassigned when aircraft are re-registered, so the durable per-airframe key is the manufacturer serial number (MSN), which the FAA file carries — the spine should key on MSN with tail/hex as time-bounded aliases, and 'FAA enforcement actions' is the weakest starting point (name-keyed, not tail-keyed) while SDR + AIDS are the strong siblings the brief undersold.

- OFAC SDN aircraft entries: the already-wired SDN source (used for IMO ships) also lists sanctioned aircraft with tail numbers - a zero-new-source join for this key.

- forfeiture.gov notices carry federal case numbers - bridges seized-aircraft tails to the DOCKET key (tagger-known) and PACER records.
- FAA registry owner name/address joins probabilistically to EDGAR CIK (corporate jet perk/personal-use disclosures) and to IRS BMF/990 EINs (nonprofit- and hospital-owned aircraft) - 'who flies on the charity's jet'.
- ICE Flight Monitor tail numbers join to USAspending (UEI, already landed) charter contractors - the deportation-flight profit chain.
- B-43 owned-vs-leased field exposes aircraft lessor chains that join to EIN/UEI/CIK holdings - the financial owners behind airline fleets.
- OFAC SDN file already landed for ships (IMO key) also contains AIRCRAFT entries with tail numbers — one parser change on an existing source yields the sanctioned-aircraft table, no new ingestion
- SEC EDGAR (CIK, landed): proxy statements disclose executive personal use of corporate aircraft — pair perk disclosures with FAA registry owner names and flight tracks to show whose shareholder-funded jet flew where
- IRS 990 / BMF (EIN, landed): nonprofit air-ambulance and charity-flight operators appear as FAA registry owners — links the healthcare/nonprofit holdings to NTSB/SDR safety records (air-ambulance crash pattern is a known who-gets-hurt story)
- USAspending (UEI, landed): federal air-charter contractors (including ICE deportation flight brokers) name-match to FAA registry owners — contract dollars joined to actual tail-level flight activity
- FAA registry owner name/address is a PROBABILISTIC bridge into every entity spine Ripple has (EIN, UEI, LEI, CIK) — aircraft ownership becomes an asset attribute on existing entities, not a separate island
- BIS 'aircraft subject to General Prohibition 10' list (export-control-violating aircraft by tail number) exists but its URL was lost in the bis.doc.gov -> bis.gov migration — worth a manual hunt; pairs with tracking for a banned-but-still-flying variant

**Brief critique:** The brief's 'likely overvalued' instinct is correct: there is no open authoritative per-vehicle registry (NMVTIS is restricted, state bulk registration is DPPA-walled — NY's 12.6M-row file is the lone real exception), and most federal VIN fields are truncated to 11-12 characters, which makes them model-level joins (STRONG), not vehicle-level matches. The genuinely new STEEL value is entirely in the FMCSA truck files, where VIN rides alongside USDOT number — so the higher-value sibling key in this domain is USDOT/MC (already planned), with VIN serving as its vehicle-level bridge plus a free vPIC decode-enrichment layer.

**Brief critique:** The "likely overvalued" call is right for consumer-facing stories — DPPA strips owner identity from every public VIN file and the authoritative registry (NMVTIS) is closed, so VIN never reaches a human owner — but the brief missed where the real value is: the FMCSA MCMIS cluster, where VIN sits beside USDOT carrier numbers, making VIN chiefly the vehicle-side join that activates the USDOT/MC sibling key (which carries the actual harm story). Practical warning: nearly every high-value file publishes only a 10-12 character VIN prefix, so the working join key is the "squish VIN" prefix, not the full 17 characters.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- FMCSA SMS Input files carry DOT_Number next to every VIN — a ready-made bridge to the planned USDOT/MC key; the companion 'SMS Input - Motor Carrier Census' (data.transportation.gov kjg3-diqy) adds carrier legal name/address, giving a probabilistic hop from VIN to Ripple's EIN/UEI/SAM-exclusion holdings (carrier banned from federal work but trucks still passing inspections).
- VIN-prefix join mechanism: even where the serial is redacted (complaints 11-char, SGO ~11-char, FARS ~12-char, WA EV 10-char), the shared prefix still decodes via vPIC to exact make/model/year — so 'truncated' datasets all interconnect at model level; treat VIN-prefix as its own STRONG sub-key rather than discarding truncated sources.
- Government fleet chain-of-custody: Seattle 'Sold Fleet Equipment' and KC auction VINs (already scouted) can be traced into later tow, citation, and crash appearances — what happens to publicly-owned vehicles after disposal, and who gets hurt by dumped fleet junk.
- Santa Clara's permitted septic/grease pumper truck VINs (scouted) can be joined to FMCSA inspection VINs — county-permitted trucks with open federal out-of-service violations.
- Mexico's REPUVE public per-VIN registry (not verified this session) could trace whether VINs from US stolen/recovered lists (e.g., Louisville) reappear registered in Mexico — a cross-border theft-export story lane.
- VIN-to-USDOT bridge: FMCSA Crash File (aayw-vxb3) and SMS Input files carry VIN and DOT_Number in the same row, and FARS vehicle.csv carries MCARR_ID (motor carrier ID) beside the VIN - landing these instantly activates the planned USDOT/MC key with zero extra crosswalk work.
- FARS ships vpicdecode.csv inside each year's zip - NHTSA pre-decoded VIN attributes, so FARS needs no decoder pass at build time.
- Plate-to-VIN bridges exist in public data despite DPPA: FMCSA SMS inspections (Unit_License + VIN) and the Providence 2017 tax roll (plate + VIN) let plate-keyed municipal datasets (citations, tows) join the VIN world.
- Manufacturer/reporting-entity names in vPIC, SGO automation-crash reports, and ODI complaints name-match to Ripple's CIK/LEI corporate holdings (Tesla, GM, Ford), connecting vehicle-level harm to corporate filings.
- NY registration scofflaw/suspension/revocation indicator flags are a built-in enforcement-status signal - crossed with NY inspections and crashes they support a 'flagged but still on the road' pattern without any owner data.

**Brief critique:** The brief treats this as scattered portal hits, but every Virginia-portal item is just a federated pointer to one canonical home: datahub.transportation.gov, where the entire FMCSA core (census, crash, inspection, violation, SMS, OOS, revocation, and the full L&I insurance family) is free bulk CSV updated daily-to-monthly — the old MCMIS fee is dead, so this key is cheaper and richer than the brief implies. One structural note: FMCSA is retiring MC/docket numbers in favor of USDOT-only (the Motus migration is live now), so model USDOT as the primary key and MC as an attribute, and watch both legacy and Motus dataset families during the transition.

**Brief critique:** The 13 scouted "Virginia Open Data Portal" hits are almost all federated mirrors of FMCSA's own files - the authoritative home for every one of them is datahub.transportation.gov, so this key is far more federal-centric and cheaper to land than the index implies. Also, MC numbers are being phased out (URS consolidation; legacy L&I retired to Motus in May 2026): build the spine on USDOT number and treat MC/FF/MX docket as an attribute, not a co-equal key.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- Insurance files (Insur/InsHist/ActPendInsur) name every insurer underwriting every carrier — a direct bridge to the NAIC company code candidate key: which insurers profitably back the deadliest fleets.
- BOC-3 agent names/addresses are a network key the brief did not anticipate: shared process agents across revoked and newly-registered carriers is a machine-detectable chameleon-carrier mechanism, same shape as EIN shell-tracking.
- Census LEGAL_NAME/DBA + address name-matches to USAspending recipients and SAM exclusions (UEI): carriers hauling federal freight or mail while under OOS orders, and cross-system ban leakage (excluded in SAM, active in FMCSA or vice versa).
- MCS-150 mileage/power-units/drivers in the census give exposure denominators — per-mile and per-truck harm rates, a normalization trick reusable for other Ripple harm lenses.
- CT hazardous waste manifests link transporter USDOT to EPA generator/facility IDs — a ready-made bridge into the planned EPA FRS_ID key.
- Carrier physical addresses geocode to counties, joining trucking harm (crashes, OOS carriers domiciled) to existing county-level marts like drug-poisoning and double-burden.
- Many state crash-report datasets beyond Chicago carry a carrier USDOT field (state crash forms follow MMUCC) — a repeatable GEO pin mechanism per state, even though Socrata full-text search surfaces few of them.
- USDOT-to-DUNS crosswalk: Company Census File carries DUN_BRADSTREET_NO filled on ~369K carriers - a direct bridge from trucking to Ripple's tagger-known DUNS key (and via DUNS to legacy federal-contracting records).
- USDOT-to-VIN bridge: Inspections Per Unit (13.6M rows, VIN + plate) joined to Vehicle Inspection File on Inspection ID seeds the VIN candidate key and proves chameleon carriers at the physical-truck level; the census's PRIOR_REVOKE_DOT_NUMBER column corroborates the same mechanism from the registry side.
- Insurer bridge: L&I Insur/ActPendInsur files name every insurance company and policy underwriting each carrier - a natural on-ramp to the NAIC company-code candidate key (which insurers profitably underwrite the worst fleets).
- EPA SmartWay files link carriers to SCAC codes and EPA program membership - a crosswalk toward shipping/logistics identifiers and the EPA world (FRS candidate key).
- Carrier physical/mailing addresses in the census enable address-cluster matching against IRS BMF and NPPES addresses already in Ripple - reincarnation farms where dozens of carriers (or carriers + clinics) share one address.

**Brief critique:** The brief's landscape list was accurate but understated two things: the ORIS bridge lives in the standalone USEPA camd-eia-crosswalk repo (which natively carries FRS IDs since v0.3) rather than in CAMD/CAMPD itself, which never exposes FRS; and TRIFID (TRI facility ID) behaves as a high-traffic sibling key — most state/local portal hits carry TRIFID, not FRS, so the tagger should learn TRIFID alongside FRS. Several scouted hits (DC/NOAA wastewater, CA wastewater surveillance, KY STORET) look like false positives for this key. Not covered due to search-budget exhaustion: state master facility registries (CalEPA Regulated Site Portal, TCEQ Central Registry, NJDEP DataMiner) — real, high-value, unconfirmed this session.

**Brief critique:** The brief undervalues FRS: its program-links file is not just a facility roster, it delivers two other planned/candidate keys for free (EPA NPDES permit numbers and CAMD-ORIS/EIA-860 plant IDs), making it the highest-leverage planned key on the board. One correction: CAMD and RCRAInfo native files carry no FRS column at all — the bridge lives only in FRS_PROGRAM_LINKS, so that one file must land before those programs connect.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- CAMD-EIA crosswalk (github.com/USEPA/camd-eia-crosswalk) delivers ORIS <-> EIA plant ID <-> FRS in one file — it simultaneously seeds the planned EIA Plant/ORIS candidate key and, via EIA-860 utility ownership, opens a name-match path from power plants to CIK/LEI corporate entities already wired in Ripple.
- GHGRP parent-company files include ownership percentages, and TRI carries standardized parent-company names (historical DUNS in older Basic Plus files) — a corporate-family bridge from FRS facilities to EDGAR CIK and legacy-DUNS/UEI (SAM) holdings.
- ECHO Exporter embeds EJScreen demographic percentiles per facility — a built-in 'who lives next door' layer that pairs with any Ripple harm mart without a separate census join.
- ECHO ICIS FE&C enforcement cases name defendants and penalty amounts — matching defendant names to EDGAR financials (CIK, wired) asks 'was the fine material to the company that paid it'.
- FRS combined download ships a NATIONAL_NAICS table — direct fuel for Ripple's tagger-known NAICS key, classifying every EPA facility by industry.
- ECHO SDWA files establish PWSID (public water system ID) as a strong new candidate key not on Ripple's list — the join point for state drinking-water quality data.
- FRS ORGANIZATION table carries a (sparse) DUNS field — a thin but real facility-to-DUNS bridge relevant to the tagger-known DUNS key.
- TRI_FACILITY carries parent_co_db_num (DUNS) plus parent company name — a corporate-ownership bridge from polluting plants to the tagger-known DUNS key and, via name-match, to EDGAR CIK / GLEIF LEI: which public companies own the plants.
- GHGRP pub_dim_facility carries parent_company with exact ownership percentages — same corporate rollup, machine-readable enough to build an owner-share table.
- FRS_PROGRAM_LINKS rows with PGM_SYS_ACRNM in (CAMDBS, EIA-860, EGRID) are a free FRS-to-ORIS-to-EIA-plant crosswalk — lands the planned EIA Plant/ORIS key without a separate source.
- FRS_PROGRAM_LINKS NPDES rows land the EPA NPDES candidate key for free at the same time.
- ICIS FE&C defendant company names can be matched against SAM exclusions / USAspending (UEI): are EPA-fined firms still winning federal contracts?
- ECHO Demographics download (population within 1/3/5 miles of each REGISTRY_ID) gives the who-gets-hurt denominator with zero GIS work.
- FRS facility records carry federal_agency_code — federal facilities as polluters, joinable to the USAspending agency universe.
- FRS_NAICS/FRS_SIC files activate the tagger-known NAICS/SIC keys across the whole facility spine.

- **EPA ICIS FE&C Federal Civil Enforcement Case Download** — Links to NPDES via REGISTRY_ID/FRS, not directly by NPDES ID; case names may not match facility names exactly

**Brief critique:** The brief undersold how top-heavy this key is: the ECHO/ICIS-NPDES bulk + FRS crosswalk delivers ~90% of the landscape in one landing, and most of the 40 already-scouted state-portal hits are thin GIS slices of the same ICIS data (their real add is fresher spill/SSO detail and state-only permits outside federal ICIS). One ID caveat: NPDES ID is STEEL at the permit level, but one facility can hold several permits and general-permit covers reference shared master permits — facility-level uniqueness comes via the FRS Registry_ID, which this landscape delivers for free.

**Brief critique:** The brief is essentially right and NPDES is a genuine STEEL key, with one structural caveat: the ID identifies facilities/permits, not companies, so it only pays off against Ripple's corporate spine (CIK/UEI/EIN) through the FRS crosswalk plus name matching - land FRS_ID (already planned) in the same motion or the NPDES tables sit orphaned. Also note the state 'XPDES' variants (SPDES/KPDES/VPDES/TPDES) are the same key with a state-code prefix, so all 40+ scouted state hits join the federal spine directly - the scouted list undersells that they're one family, not separate keys.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- FRS PROGRAM_LINKS maps NPDES facilities to CAMD and E-GGRT program IDs — CAMD facilities are keyed by ORIS plant code, giving a free verified bridge from NPDES to the EIA Plant/ORIS candidate key (power-plant cooling-water discharges) without a new tagger.
- FRS also links NPDES to TRI facility IDs; TRI files carry standardized parent-company names (historically DUNS) — a bridge from water polluters to corporate parents, then probabilistic match into existing CIK/LEI holdings.
- FRS_NAICS/FRS_SIC files in the same download feed the tagger-known NAICS and SIC keys for every water-permitted facility.
- Good Jobs First Violation Tracker links EPA Clean Water Act enforcement cases to parent companies (bridging toward CIK/LEI) — both goodjobsfirst.org and violationtracker.goodjobsfirst.org returned 403 to automated fetch (bot protection), so it is NOT reported as a verified dataset; verify manually, and note bulk access is subscription/ToS-restricted.
- ECHO's Facility Demographics download (567MB, weekly, verified on the downloads page) attaches community demographic profiles to the same REGISTRY_ID/NPDES facilities — the environmental-justice 'who lives next to the violator' layer.
- SDWIS drinking-water data (457MB quarterly, same ECHO downloads page, PWSID-keyed) is a sibling key worth its own scouting run: violating dischargers upstream of violating drinking-water systems is a two-key story.
- Session constraint flag: the WebSearch budget was already exhausted at session start, so discovery ran on direct-URL verification only; the long tail of other state portals (FL, PA, OH, IL, GA, etc.) and academic replication datasets (Harvard Dataverse/Zenodo NPDES studies) exist but were not individually verified — a follow-up pass with search restored would close that gap.
- FRS program-links crosswalk chains an NPDES ID to the same facility's TRI, RCRA, and air-program IDs (and FRS has carried EIA plant links) - one hop from this key to the planned FRS_ID and the candidate EIA/ORIS key, making one polluting site visible across every EPA program at once
- ECHO Exporter carries NAICS and SIC codes per NPDES facility - direct feed for the tagger-known NAICS/SIC keys with zero extra sourcing
- ICIS FE&C defendant names plus penalty dollars name-match (probabilistic) to SEC CIK filers and USAspending UEI recipients: 'company under a Clean Water Act consent decree still winning federal awards' is a ready-made lens
- Municipal POTW permittees are local-government entities that appear in IRS BMF (EIN) and receive Clean Water SRF money visible in USAspending (UEI) - chronic-spill utilities vs. the federal dollars they already got is a who-gets-hurt story connecting three wired keys
- TRI Basic Plus facility file (confirmed live, 1987-present) carries original/current facility names and parent company info for many facilities that also hold NPDES permits - a facility-to-parent-corporation bridge; TRI Form R also collects NPDES permit numbers, though that field was not visible on the summary page - verify in File 4 layout
- Good Jobs First Violation Tracker pre-matches EPA enforcement cases to corporate parents - both violationtracker.goodjobsfirst.org and goodjobsfirst.org returned 403 to automated fetch (bot-blocked, not gone); free search exists, bulk data is paid - flagged, not verified
- HIFLD Open's legacy Wastewater Treatment Plants GEO layer is in limbo after the 2025 HIFLD retirement (hub URL 404) - do not chase it; it was derived from EPA FRS, which Ripple can rebuild from source
- Not covered for lack of search budget (web-search quota was exhausted at session start; all verification done by direct fetch): the other ~45 state portals (PA eDMR, OH, FL, MI, IL, CO, OR all run authorized programs with public permit data), USGS SPARROW/ScienceBase point-source datasets keyed by NPDES, the HydroWASTE academic WWTP dataset, and data.gov catalog mirrors

**Brief critique:** The brief lists EIA-861 as a starting point, but it never carries plant IDs — it is utility-level, keyed by EIA Utility ID. That utility ID is a worthy sibling key in its own right (EIA-860 owner/operator fields bridge plants to EIA-861's sales, revenue, and service-disconnection data — a direct who-gets-hurt lead); the plant-key landscape itself is otherwise exactly as the brief framed it, with the official EPA-published CAMD-EIA crosswalk (not only PUDL) doing the ORIS-to-EIA unit-level work.

**Brief critique:** EIA-861 was a wrong starting point: it is keyed by EIA Utility ID (utility-level sales/revenue) and carries no plant/ORIS codes - the sibling key actually worth scouting is EIA Utility ID, which PUDL already links to both plants and FERC respondents. Otherwise the brief undersold the key: ORIS and EIA Plant ID are the same namespace, so this single key unifies the entire EPA emissions world and the entire EIA operations world with zero fuzzy matching - one of the cleanest STEEL keys in the candidate list.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- PUDL now integrates SEC 10-K filings and links utility parent companies to EIA utilities - a plant-to-parent-company bridge into Ripple's existing CIK/EDGAR holdings without name matching
- EIA-923 fuel-receipts schedule carries the source coal mine's MSHA mine ID per delivery - a plant-to-mine supply-chain bridge to MSHA violation/fatality data (MSHA is not on Ripple's key list)
- EPA's CAMD-EIA crosswalk v0.3 added EPA FRS facility IDs - a ready-made ORIS-to-FRS_ID bridge that unlocks ECHO/NPDES enforcement joins for the planned FRS_ID key
- FERC Form 1 plant costs join EIA plant IDs via PUDL's published record linkage - ratepayer economics meets smokestack emissions, i.e. who pays for the pollution
- EIA-860 owner/operator names and utility IDs give a probabilistic name bridge to Ripple's EIN (IRS BMF) and UEI (USAspending/SAM exclusions) holdings - are excluded federal contractors among plant owners?
- CAMD-EIA crosswalk v0.3 carries EPA FRS IDs per unit - a ready-made machine bridge from ORIS plants into Ripple's planned FRS_ID key, and through FRS into ECHO enforcement, ICIS-NPDES water permits (an existing NEW-candidate key), and TRI toxic releases
- EIA-923 fuel-receipt schedules record the source coal mine's MSHA ID - links every coal plant to specific mines and thus to MSHA safety-violation data; MSHA ID is a real registry key not on Ripple's key list at all
- GHGRP Parent Companies file (XLSB) names the corporate parent of every large emitter - a name-match bridge from ORIS plants to Ripple's CIK/LEI/UEI corporate spine (who profits from the pollution)
- PUDL's FERC1-EIA plant-parts association connects plant economics to EIA plant IDs, and FERC respondents' holding companies file with SEC - a two-hop path from a smokestack to an EDGAR CIK
- CAMPD allowance-transaction data names account owners trading pollution allowances - probabilistic name-match to corporate keys reveals who monetizes emission headroom
- EIA-860 Owner file percentages let you apportion a plant's emissions harm across co-owners, including municipal utilities and co-ops that also appear in USAspending (UEI) as federal award recipients

**Brief critique:** The brief's anchor is stale: PatentsView's site and Search API were retired into USPTO's Open Data Portal (patentsview.org redirects, search.patentsview.org DNS is gone, bulkdata.uspto.gov and developer.uspto.gov are dead hosts), so every USPTO pipeline must target data.uspto.gov/api.uspto.gov (free key) instead. Also, the already-scouted state-portal hits (CT 1800s, VA translated cluster, Roswell) are trivia next to this federal spine, and a sibling key worth tagging is the patent APPLICATION/publication number, since assignments, PTAB, and prosecution data all key on applications too.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- NBER CUSIP-match file + KPSS permno links form a ready-made PATENT-to-CUSIP/CRSP bridge — jump-starts the planned CUSIP key and reaches EDGAR CIK filers without name matching
- DISCERN 2 resolves patent assignees through SEC-filing subsidiary trees into listed parents — a largely name-free path from PATENT to the CIK holdings already wired
- OSTI/DOE patent records carry DOE contract/award numbers — connects PATENT to federal spending already wired via USAspending (UEI)
- FDA Orange Book patent file puts PATENT two hops from wired Open Payments: patent -> NDA drug -> manufacturer -> payments to prescribers
- USPTO assignment recordations include security-interest filings (banks taking patents as collateral) — surfaces lender relationships findable in GLEIF LEI and EDGAR
- CourtListener patent suits double as fuel for the tagger-known DOCKET key — one landing serves two keys
- Reliance on Science links patents to scientific papers and researchers — a natural future bridge to the ORCID candidate key via OpenAlex author records
- Patent-to-securities bridge the brief didn't anticipate: DISCERN 2.0 (GVKEY), KPSS (CRSP permno), and NBER (CUSIP) crosswalks hang patent portfolios onto Ripple's wired CIK/EDGAR spine and planned CUSIP key — corporate monopoly holdings joined to financial filings.
- Orange Book patent.txt -> NDA -> drug/brand name joins directly to Ripple's wired CMS Part D prescriber tables: every listed drug patent becomes priceable against Medicare spending (the evergreening-cost story).
- NIH ExPORTER patents -> grant core project numbers -> grantee universities/hospitals name-match to Ripple's wired EIN holdings (IRS 990/BMF): nonprofit institutions monetizing taxpayer-funded patents.
- PatentsView's government-interest table names funding agencies (DOD, HHS, DOE, NASA) — name-joinable to USAspending awards (UEI wired) to ask which contractors patent on top of federal R&D money.
- Patent litigation sources (CourtListener/RECAP, USPTO litigation dockets, Stanford NPE) each carry district-court docket numbers, giving dual-key PATENT+DOCKET edges — one corpus feeds two tagger-known keys at once.

**Brief critique:** "NCES" is really three sibling key families — CCD LEAID/NCESSCH (public K-12), PSS PPIN (private K-12), and UNITID/OPEID (higher ed) — and UNITID/OPEID deserve their own registry entries, since the highest-value enforcement datasets (FSA default/closed-school/HCM lists, Clery, DAPIP) carry only OPEID and never a K-12 NCES ID. Also, the 31 scouted index hits are mostly state GIS convenience layers and stale state copies; the federal core (CCD, CRDC, EDFacts, SAIPE, E-Rate) is where the value is, and note EDFacts' old ed.gov home now 404s — its files moved to data.ed.gov.

**Brief critique:** The brief folds UNITID and OPEID under NCES, but they are separate key families with their own registries (IPEDS, PEPS) and deserve their own tagger keys — about half this landscape is really theirs. Also, the key's biggest lever isn't federal-to-federal joins (those are trivial); it's that CCD embeds ST_LEAID/ST_SCHID state-ID crosswalks, which is what actually connects the 31 scouted state/county portal hits — most of which are just local slices of CCD, EDGE, CRDC, F-33, and Scorecard and become redundant once the national files land.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- USAC E-Rate Supplemental Entity Information is a confirmed triple-key bridge nobody anticipated: NCES public district/building codes AND NCES private school ID AND UEI (Form 498, already wired via USAspending/SAM) AND FCC Registration Number (FRN, a Ripple new-candidate key) in one row — plus E-Rate Entity Number joins to E-Rate funding-commitment datasets for dollars and telecom vendors (SPINs),…
- For-profit college chains bridge higher-ed keys to Ripple's wired CIK: OPEID/UNITID institutions roll up to publicly-traded parent companies in SEC EDGAR via ownership names in FSA/PEPS and Scorecard — 'college chain collapsing in EDGAR filings while FSA still shows it enrolling aid recipients'.
- Ripple already stages DOJ Civil Rights Division cases (fed_doj_crt_cases): education cases name districts that can be matched to CRDC harassment/discipline data by district name — enforcement actions vs self-reported harm.
- Private schools and nonprofit colleges file IRS 990s (EIN, wired): PSS and IPEDS rosters name-match to the IRS BMF, connecting school finances to the tax-exempt layer.
- EDGE geocode files assign every school a congressional district — a direct join to Ripple's wired BIOGUIDE/Voteview holdings (which members' districts contain the schools with the worst CRDC harm numbers).
- FAFSA federal school codes are OPEID variants — the already-scouted Missouri FAFSA-completion dataset joins the higher-ed key family through them.
- E-Rate entity data carries NSLP student counts and Community Eligibility Provision percentages — a school-level poverty measure independent of Census, cross-checkable against SAIPE for districts gaming discount rates.
- IPEDS HD file carries EIN and UEI fields (verified in the HD2023 data dictionary): every college joins directly to Ripple's wired IRS 990/BMF and DOL 5500 (EIN) and USAspending/SAM exclusions (UEI) — enabling 'college excluded or sanctioned as a federal awardee but still drawing Title IV' leads with zero new crosswalk work.
- College Scorecard's bundled OPEID-to-UNITID crosswalk file bridges all FSA sanction/default/closure data into IPEDS finance and enrollment without fuzzy matching.
- CCD directory files carry state school/district IDs (ST_LEAID, ST_SCHID) — a deterministic bridge from the NCES spine into state-keyed datasets already in the scouted index (TX AskTED campus numbers, CA CDS codes, TN, AZ, VT layers).
- SAIPE's district identifier is state FIPS + district code, which equals the NCES LEA ID by construction — Census poverty joins the NCES spine with no crosswalk at all.
- Negative finding worth recording: USAC E-Rate open data contains zero NCES-keyed datasets (Socrata catalog search returned 0 results) — school broadband subsidy leads would have to route through state IDs or name matching, not this key.

**Brief critique:** Three of the brief's federal starting points do not publicly carry ORCID at all - verified in-session: NIH RePORTER's API exposes PI names/profile IDs only, NSF's award API has no ORCID field, and OSTI's public v1 API returns bare author names (Semantic Scholar's author externalIds also showed no ORCID in sampling) - so the real federal ORCID carriers are NLM's PubMed/PMC, and grants must be reached via RePORTER's PMID-to-project link tables. Also note ORCID is graph fuel, not a direct-match key for Ripple: its harm stories only land after a second hop bridging ORCID names to NPI (Open Payments) or NCT (fed_clinicaltrials).

**Brief critique:** Three of the brief's starting points are dead ends as direct carriers: NIH RePORTER and NSF award APIs expose PI names only (no ORCID field — verified against both), and Semantic Scholar author records carry DBLP but not ORCID; the working NIH bridge is PubMed ORCID + ExPORTER project-to-PMID link tables instead. Bigger picture: ORCID has no public crosswalk to NPI or EIN, so it reaches Ripple's core health/money holdings only via two-hop joins (PMID link tables, institution matching) — real value, but one step removed from the brief's implied direct connections.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- NIH RePORTER ExPORTER publication link tables (reporter.nih.gov/exporter, api.reporter.nih.gov) map PMID to Core Project Number with awardee UEI/DUNS - bridges ORCID'd PubMed authors to NIH grants and Ripple's wired USAspending/SAM spine even though RePORTER itself carries no ORCID.
- PubMed records carry ClinicalTrials.gov NCT IDs in their databank fields - a direct join from ORCID'd publication authors to Ripple's fed_clinicaltrials staging tables (trial investigators vs. paper authors vs. pharma payments).
- PricePortal (Zenodo, doi 10.5281/zenodo.19941038, CC-BY, May 2026): 528-hospital identity crosswalk CCN-OSHPD-NPI-EIN with 95.6% NPI coverage plus 417M payer-negotiated rates - found while hunting ORCID crosswalks; directly feeds Ripple's known CCN/NPI/EIN bridge starvation.
- Wikidata person items co-hold ORCID (P496) with Bioguide IDs, and org items hold CIK/LEI - a single CC0 hub joining researchers to Ripple's legislator roster and EDGAR/GLEIF corporate spines.
- ORCID dump affiliation records carry ROR/GRID/Ringgold organization IDs - a future institution-level key that name-matches to UEI awardee institutions in USAspending.
- PMC JATS full text includes machine-readable conflict-of-interest statements alongside ORCID'd authors - an automatable COI-disclosure-vs-Open-Payments consistency check using tables Ripple already holds.
- NIH ExPORTER project-to-publication (PMID) link tables + PubMed's ORCID-tagged authors form a working ORCID-to-NIH-grant bridge even though RePORTER itself carries no ORCID; medical-school PIs often also hold NPIs, giving a two-hop path into Ripple's Medicare/Open Payments/LEIE world.
- Wikidata person items frequently carry BOTH P496 (ORCID) and P1157 (US Congress Bioguide ID) plus employer claims — a free crosswalk from ORCID into Ripple's wired BIOGUIDE spine for legislator-academics, unanticipated by the key list.
- Retraction Watch CSV has no ORCID but joins on DOI to Crossref/OpenAlex which do — enabling a 'retracted researcher, still federally funded' lens against USAspending/SAM exclusions via the researcher's employer institution.
- OpenAlex links every ORCID author to a ROR institution ID; university RORs map to UEI/EIN by name matching, connecting individual researchers to Ripple's USAspending, SAM exclusions, and IRS 990 employer holdings.
- Crossref author records carry an authenticated-orcid boolean — a built-in signal separating verified identity claims from typed-in ones, useful as a data-quality gate before any published finding.

- **FCC Universal Licensing System (ULS) — complete weekly bulk…** — FRN is field 23, char(10), in the EN (entity) record. www.fcc.gov landing page is bot-blocked from this environment; the data.fcc.gov directory itself was directly confirmed. Amateur/GMRS records include individuals' home addresses — personal-privacy handling required.
- **E-Rate Request for Discount on Services: Basic Information…** — Column is literally named 'FCC Registration Number' (10-digit, distinct from the Funding Request Number also in USAC data). Self-reported by applicants. Contains named contact individuals.
- **RHC SPIN Lookup Tool Dataset (Rural Health Care service pro…** — FCC Registration Number populated on only 15,008 of 22,259 rows. Also carries 'FCC Form 499 Filer' and 'FCC Form 498 Filed with UEI' flags — direct route into Ripple's UEI holdings.
- **Broadband Data Collection (BDC) Provider List — National Br…** — Could not fetch broadbandmap.fcc.gov/data-download directly (timeout) or help.bdc.fcc.gov (403) — URL taken from FCC's own published download specification, NOT fetch-confirmed.
- **Robocall Mitigation Database (RMD)** — FRN mandatory per FCC filing instructions. Registration NOT required to download. www.fcc.gov is bot-blocked from this environment — page not fetch-confirmed, but corroborated by FCC's own rmd-instructions.pdf and a Jan 2026 Federal Register rulemaking.
- **CDBS Broadcast Public Database Files — ownership, party and…** — DISCONTINUED for new data as of 2023-10-01 — historical only; current filings moved to LMS. A dedicated frn_history table exists = entity-resolution gold for FRN succession. Form 323 also collects race, gender and ethnicity of owners.
- **LMS Public Database Files (current broadcast licensing + Fo…** — Returned 403 to this environment's fetcher (bot protection) — existence corroborated by FCC Media Bureau pages and the CDBS retirement notice, but the file inventory was NOT directly confirmed. Verify table list and FRN column before building.
- **FCC Form 499 Filer Database (telecom carriers) + API** — API searchable by FRN. apps.fcc.gov returned 403 to this environment's fetcher; API doc page also 403. API version string dates to 2011 — confirm still live and unthrottled before relying on it.
- **ULS Ownership Disclosure Information Search (FCC Form 602)** — NO bulk download found — per-query interface only. Indirect ownership computed by successive multiplication per 47 CFR 1.2112. Scraping volume/ToS needs checking before any systematic pull.
- **Antenna Structure Registration (ASR) bulk database** — r_tower.zip confirmed reachable (oversize response). Also strong GEO value — coordinates support spatial joins to Ripple's CCN facility and school locations.
- **Emergency Connectivity Fund FCC Form 471** — Confirmed to carry all four identifiers: FCC Registration Number (position 14), Billed Entity Number (13), Funding Request Number (41), SPIN (47). Program wound down — historical dataset.
- **E-Rate Open Competitive Bidding: Basic Information (FCC For…** — Column named 'Billed Entity FCC Registration Number' — a real 10-digit FCC RN, NOT the Funding Request Number. Pairs with 471 award data to expose single-bid procurement.
- **FCC Auction Public Reporting System (auction results, bidde…** — Fetch-confirmed live for auction904. FRN presence in the downloadable files was NOT confirmed — Form 175 short-form applications require an FRN so the join likely exists, but must be verified against an actual file. RDOF defaults are a documented harm story.
- **ULS Ship Station licenses (maritime)** — Direct bridge to Ripple's IMO/MMSI holdings (OFAC SDN ships, NOAA AIS). Exact bulk field layout for MMSI NOT verified — confirm against the ULS data-definitions file before wiring.
- **ULS Aircraft Station licenses** — Companion file a_aatc.zip (110.8MB, aviation ground) also confirmed. Tail-number field presence not verified. Bridges outward to the FAA N-number registry, not currently a Ripple holding.
- **FCC ECFS (Electronic Comment Filing System) public API** — Returned 403 without a key — host live, api.data.gov key required. A reliable FRN field is NOT guaranteed, so the join is likely name-based (downgrade to PROBABILISTIC unless an FRN field is confirmed). Filings contain private individuals' comments — personal-data care needed.
- **FCC Commission Registration System (CORES) public FRN search** — CRITICAL GAP: there is NO public bulk download or API for CORES. The authoritative registry file the brief assumed exists does NOT exist as a downloadable artifact — per-query lookup only. FRN-to-TIN/EIN mapping is masked from public view (same masking problem as NPPES).
- **International Communications Filing System (ICFS, formerly…** — Renamed IBFS to ICFS after the International Bureau split (2023). The data.gov record is stale (last substantive update 2017) and points at an FTP URL that is very likely dead — not confirmed. FRN presence in bulk unverified.
- **FCC Experimental Licensing System (ELS)** — No bulk download found — per-query search only. Filers register via CORES so an FRN underlies each record, but an exposed FRN field in output was not confirmed.
- **Cable Operations and Licensing System (COALS) / Cable Commu…** — COALS access delegated through CORES usernames with authority over FRNs. Bulk download availability NOT confirmed — the FCC 'Download FCC Datasets' page is on www.fcc.gov, bot-blocked from this environment. Verify manually.
- **Fixed Broadband Deployment Data from FCC Form 477 (legacy)** — DISCONTINUED — superseded by BDC. Providers with both ILEC and CLEC arms may file under a single FRN while listing multiple 499 Filer IDs, so FRN-to-entity is many-to-one and messy. Confirm FRN column against an actual vintage file.
- **EAS Equipment Authorization Grantee Registrations** — NO FRN COLUMN — confirmed by direct column inspection. An FRN is required to obtain a Grantee Code, but the published file exposes only grantee code and name/address, so any join to FRN is name/address matching. Also appears stale (last update 2021-03-22).
- **FCC Pirate Radio Broadcasting Database** — By definition these are UNLICENSED operators, so most will have no FRN — join is name/address at best. Columns not inspected. Enforcement-selection bias is itself the story; handle named individuals carefully.
- **FCC.report — third-party mirror of ELS, IBFS/ICFS and equip…** — THIRD PARTY, not affiliated with or endorsed by the FCC (their own disclaimer). No formal ToS or licence statement found — provenance and reuse rights AMBIGUOUS. Treat as a discovery aid, not a system of record.
- **FCC Red Light Display System (delinquent debt by FRN)** — NOT PUBLIC. Login-gated by your own FRN; only shows debts for the FRN you authenticate with. No public bulk file. Listed so the gap is visible, not silently skipped — this is a FOIA target, NOT a scrape target. Do not attempt authenticated access.
- **EAS Test Reporting System (ETRS) Form One** — Form One pre-populates from FRN + Facility ID so FRN is definitely captured, but NO public download exists — FCC has treated ETRS filings as presumptively confidential on homeland-security grounds. Reported as a known restricted holding.
- **FCC License View API and FRN Conversions API** — CONFIRMED DEAD THIS SESSION. data.fcc.gov/api/frn/application.wadl and /getInfo both 302-redirect to the FCC not-found page; license-view/basicSearch 301-redirects away. Documented so nobody re-scouts it. Archived responses may survive at the Internet Archive.
- *Index false positives:* Dropped: (1) FRNCOD in 15 LA County layers (CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, McDonalds, Cell facilities, Digital Divide case studies) — it is the Esri Business Analyst/InfoUSA business-listing schema's franchise code (sits beside LOCNUM/CONAME/SALESVOL/HDBRCH), not FCC FRN, even in the cell-provider layers. (2) PCT_FRN_BORN_POVERTY (Open Baltimore Foreign Born Population) = 'foreign born'. (3) PETFRNDLY…

**Brief critique:** The brief's USAC bridge rests on an acronym collision: in USAC E-Rate and Rural Health Care data 'FRN' means Funding Request Number, NOT FCC Registration Number, so a naive join on the column named FRN would be silently wrong — the real FCC Registration Number does appear in E-Rate Form 470/471 and ECF (sometimes as 'Billed Entity FCC Registration Number'), and RHC reaches hospitals only indirectly via the SPIN lookup table since the RHC commitments file has no FCC RN at all. Second, there is no authoritative issuer/registry file: CORES offers per-query public search only, with no bulk download or API and TIN/EIN masked, and the FCC's own FRN crosswalk APIs (FRN Conversions, License View) are now dead, so the FRN-to-corporate-parent spine has to be rebuilt from ULS, LMS/CDBS ownership and Form 499 rather than fetched.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- USAC Service Provider 498 UEI Data (datahub.usac.org/d/skey-yj2y, 22,259 rows) carries SPIN + FCC Registration Number + a UEI-filed flag — a direct, unanticipated bridge from FRN into Ripple's wired UEI (USAspending, SAM exclusions), letting you ask whether a debarred federal contractor is still collecting universal-service subsidies.
- CDBS frn_history.zip is a dedicated FRN succession/change table — entity-resolution gold for tracking when a broadcaster's FRN changes hands, which is how ownership consolidation hides from a naive point-in-time join.
- FCC Form 323 collects race, gender and ethnicity of every attributable broadcast owner alongside their FRN — a demographic-harm dataset the brief framed only as a media-consolidation angle; it supports asking whether minority station ownership collapsed in specific markets.
- FCC ship station licences feed MMSI assignments to the ITU MARS international registry, so FRN reaches vessels not just through FCC files but through an independent global registry that can corroborate or contradict Ripple's OFAC SDN and NOAA AIS holdings.
- E-Rate Form 471 carries full-time enrollment and National School Lunch Program poverty counts next to the FCC Registration Number — a school-level poverty measure that turns any carrier-side finding into a who-gets-hurt map without needing an external education dataset.
- ASR tower coordinates plus BDC coverage polygons allow a purely spatial join from FRN-owned infrastructure to Ripple's CCN hospital facilities and E-Rate school locations, catching harm patterns that no shared identifier would reveal.
- The RHC SPIN Lookup table's 'FCC Form 499 Filer' boolean is an explicit pre-built link from the USAC world into the Form 499 carrier world, meaning FRN-to-SPIN-to-499-Filer-ID is a three-hop chain that resolves telecom identity across two agencies' systems.
- Aircraft station licences (a_aircr.zip) point outward to the FAA N-number civil aircraft registry, which Ripple does not hold — an FRN-to-tail-number-to-registered-owner chain that could surface shell-company aircraft also appearing in USAspending or SAM exclusions.
- FCC Consumer Complaints data (opendata.fcc.gov/d/3xyp-aqkj and unwanted-calls vakf-fz8e) has no FRN but names carriers in free text, so fuzzy-matching complaints to the Robocall Mitigation Database FRN roster turns anecdote into a ranked harm signal against certified providers.
- The Red Light Display system proves the FCC maintains a structured FRN-keyed delinquent-debt ledger that is simply not published — a concrete, well-scoped FOIA target rather than a dead end.

**Flags:**

- **Regrid Nationwide Parcel Data** — Paid enterprise licensing, no public pricing, no free bulk tier; also resold inside Esri Living Atlas. Buying is a RED-lane money call.
- **Cook County Assessor - Parcel Universe** — Key is the Cook 14-digit PIN (APN sibling, same family). Sister PIN-keyed datasets (Permits, Appeals, Sales) on same portal.
- **King County (WA) Assessor Data Download** — Download requires accepting an acknowledgement page; names present (unlike NJ/LA redactions).
- **CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS) Data** — Also mirrored on data.ca.gov; APN column confirmed this session via the FeatureServer schema.
- **Florida DOR Property Tax Data Portal (NAL tax rolls + GIS)** — GIS/roll download sits behind a request form (free but not one-click). Distinct dataset from the scouted 'Florida Statewide Parcels' (GIO geometry).
- **NC OneMap Parcels with Statewide Standardized Attributes** — Attribute completeness varies by county; existence verified via NC OneMap DCAT catalog.
- **Wisconsin Statewide Parcel Map (V12)** — Boundaries are not legal survey; parcel ID in schema (PARCELID) - confirm on load.
- **Montana State Library Cadastral (MSDI Parcels + CAMA)** — None.
- **NJGIN Statewide Parcels + MOD-IV Tax List** — Owner names redacted under Daniel's Law (2023-) - a transparency regression worth its own story.
- **NYS Tax Parcels (Statewide, Public Counties)** — 24 counties withhold data - coverage holes are county-political, not technical.
- **MassGIS Property Tax Parcels (Statewide L3)** — mass.gov landing page blocks bots (403) - use the gis.data.mass.gov item (verified via DCAT catalog).
- **Connecticut CAMA and Parcel Layer** — Multiple annual vintages exist - pick and pin one.
- **Vermont Statewide Standardized Parcel Data (parcel polygons)** — VCGI program page blocks bots; dataset verified via VT geodata DCAT catalog.
- **Texas TxGIO (TNRIS) StratMap Land Parcels** — Multiple 'Land Parcels' collections (vintages) in the API - confirm the current one; coverage not 100% of counties.
- **Utah UGRC Statewide Parcels + LIR** — None.
- **Washington State Current Parcels** — Attribute depth varies by county; verified via geo.wa.gov DCAT catalog.
- **Virginia Parcels (VGIN)** — Attributes standardized only partially - the richer fields live in the Local Schema Tables companion.
- **Maryland Property Data - Parcel Points (MD iMAP)** — Points not polygons; key is account number, treat as APN-family.
- **Delaware State Parcels 2.0 (FirstMap)** — FirstMap portal DCAT feed 404s; verified via ArcGIS Online item search.
- **Tennessee Property Boundaries Public Use (TNMap)** — 'Public Use' layer strips some assessment attributes - parcel ID presence to be confirmed on load; full CAMA data is a separate Comptroller product.
- **Arkansas GIS Office Parcel Polygons & Centroids** — URL is the site search (per-county product pages behind it); 74-county coverage statement verified on-site.
- **Hawaii Statewide Parcels (TMK)** — Key is TMK, an APN-family sibling.
- **ReportAll USA National Parcel Layer** — Paid, pricing undisclosed. LANDSCAPE GAPS not covered this session: MN Geospatial Commons (portal revamped mid-2026, API unverifiable), RIGIS (no parcel dataset on its hub), Oregon ORMAP (historically fee-based), CA DTSC EnviroStor / GeoTracker cleanup sites (likely APN-bearing, Cloudflare-blocked), paid vendors ATTOM…
- **Regrid Nationwide Parcel Data** — Paid, license restricts republication of bulk data; free web lookup only. This is the make-or-break flag on APN as a national key: no free equivalent exists.
- **Cook County Assessor - Parcel Universe (PIN)** — PIN is Cook's APN name; current-year values not final until Board of Review certifies.
- **NYC PLUTO / MapPLUTO (BBL)** — Key is spelled BBL (borough-block-lot), not APN — tagger must treat as same family. NYC.gov landing page blocks bots; verified via Socrata metadata.
- **NYC ACRIS - Real Property Legals (deeds/mortgages by BBL)** — BBL carried as borough+block+lot fields; join to ACRIS Master/Parties files via Document ID for names and amounts.
- **NYC HPD Housing Maintenance Code Violations** — Same-family suite exists (DOB violations, evictions) on NYC Open Data, all BBL-keyed — one landing effort captures them all.
- **Florida Statewide Parcels (FL Dept of Revenue via Florida G…** — Already in scout index; URL not re-fetched this session. FL key is spelled 'folio/parcel ID' by county.
- **MassGIS Standardized Property Tax Parcels (Level 3)** — mass.gov returns 403 to automated fetch; existence verified via MassGIS ArcGIS Online items (id 73d4c766167848b795f1048cad3919c7).
- **Connecticut Statewide CAMA and Parcel Layer** — Portal page is JS-thin; verified via CT GIS Office ArcGIS item 82a733423a244c43a9d4bf552954cea9.
- **Texas TxGIO StratMap Land Parcels** — geographic.texas.gov and tnris.org blocked/404 to automated fetch — verified via ArcGIS Online mirrors; primary hub URL needs manual confirm. Some counties missing/irregular vintage.
- **Minnesota Statewide Open Parcels (plan_parcels_open)** — Opt-in program — some counties absent; verified via live download directory (portal front-end moved to gis.data.mn.gov).
- **Maryland Parcel Points/Polygons + CAMA + Sales (MD Planning…** — Files served via Dropbox links; account/parcel ID presence per file not itemized on page (SDAT account number is the join key in CAMA).

**Brief critique:** The brief's implicit "every major federal dataset carrying it" premise is empty for this key: no federal dataset carries APN, the ID only resolves as a county+APN composite (STEEL within jurisdiction, not nationally), and the largest state (California) publishes no open statewide parcel file - national coverage is paid-only (Regrid/ReportAll). APN should be treated as a key FAMILY (Cook PIN, NYC BBL, Hawaii TMK, Maryland SDAT account, Vermont SPAN) or the tagger will miss half the real carriers.

**Brief critique:** The brief's caveat is right but understated: APN is ~3,100 separate county namespaces, so a bare APN match is meaningless across counties — the key must be stored as composite (county FIPS + APN) and it is STEEL only within a jurisdiction. Also, the "every major federal dataset" leg is empty — no federal open dataset carries APN (federal property data keys on address/tract); national coverage exists only via paid Regrid or stitching ~25-30 state programs, and the tagger should treat BBL, PIN, TMK, folio, SPAN, and OPA number as the same key family or it will miss the biggest markets.

**Unexpected connections found:**

- Assessor rolls with taxpayer/owner names (King County, Cook County, FL DOR NAL) are a probabilistic name bridge from APN-world to Ripple's wired EIN/UEI/LEI/CIK entities - e.g. CMS nursing-home ownership names vs. county owner names answers 'who owns the building vs. who runs the facility' (related-party rent).
- Cook County publishes sibling PIN-keyed Socrata datasets (Assessor Permits, Appeals, Sales) - same-key joins to the Parcel Universe, spotted via the Socrata discovery API.
- CAL FIRE DINS (APN + damage + assessed value, schema verified) joins directly to the already-scouted LA County DCBA Eaton/Palisades rent registry - fire-victim displacement and lot-buying vultures in one join.
- Owner-name redaction is spreading (NJ statewide under Daniel's Law; LA County's layer literally named 'OwnershipSecure') - the shrinking of property-ownership transparency is itself a trackable, publishable pattern.
- CFPB HMDA (wired via LEI) is census-tract level; parcels geocode to tracts, giving a GEO bridge from lender behavior to specific distressed parcels.
- Esri Living Atlas hosts Regrid's premium parcel layer - an alternate licensed access path if Ripple ever holds ArcGIS licensing.
- Zillow ZTRAX, the old free academic national parcel/transaction dataset, was discontinued - do not chase it.
- Parcel files carry lat/lon and census tract → free GEO bridge to CFPB HMDA (already wired via LEI): tract-level lending denial patterns can be laid directly over parcel-level blight, foreclosure, and tax-sale outcomes — modern-redlining stories without needing any new key.
- CMS facility addresses (CCN tables, wired) geocode onto parcel registries → reveals who actually owns nursing-home real estate (REIT/LLC landlords extracting rent from failing facilities) — an APN-to-CCN bridge via address the key list didn't anticipate.
- Parcel owner-name fields match IRS BMF nonprofit names (EIN, wired) → map tax-exempt property empires of hospitals and universities against their 990 charity-care claims.
- NYC ACRIS party names and NJ/MD sales files give deed-level buyer entities matchable to GLEIF LEI and EDGAR CIK names → institutional single-family buyers connect to securities filings.
- Vermont Property Transfers dataset (found via VCGI search) is a statewide sales ledger keyed by SPAN — same pattern as Maryland's monthly sales files: sales ledgers, not just parcel snapshots, are the flip-detection fuel.

## Provenance

Built by a 111-agent workflow: per key, one agent swept `LIBRARY_META.REGISTRY.PORTAL_DATASET_INDEX` (~338,520 datasets, 96 portals) and one hunted the open web; a third skeptic agent re-verified the top new claims. Five further agents attacked the brief itself. Each key was hunted twice by independent passes and the results unioned, so a dataset appears once even if both passes found it. Snowflake access was read-only (SELECT only). No dataset was downloaded or landed.

*Report assembled deterministically from agent output — every dataset name and URL is exactly as the agent reported it. Nothing on this page was written from memory.*
